limitations: Graph edges mean recorded relationships. Parent is a starting-state reference; combine is a selected second branch, not proof every change was incorporated. Continuation/idea is intellectual reuse, not Git ancestry.
Candidate IDs are campaign-qualified. Imports and re-evaluations remain separate records; identical local IDs or commits do not imply a new causal parent edge.

Ratios belong to their measurement_source baseline, workload and timing protocol. Imported records can retain an older evaluation even after rebasing. Do not multiply ratios across campaigns or mix isolated kernel ratios with whole-training ratios.
Hypothesis verdicts are worker claims. Acceptance, reviewer decisions and measured outcome remain separate, including confirmed hypotheses that were rejected or regressed.

Early capture/replay evolution traces, program databases and archived source bodies are absent locally. All retained evaluation records survive, but most UUID parent and inspiration edges cannot be reconstructed.
The replay score-selected best may differ from the fresh-process verified champion. The fill integration used verification rank 2, not the score-selected best.
The original construct champion later failed expanded wide-partition coverage. Its original passed checks are historical, not a claim that the unmodified champion is safe today.
One started construct3 worker has no final archive record; it is explicitly unarchived/interrupted, not silently dropped or assigned a measured score.
Mechanical kernel identity evidence does not establish quality equivalence for precision changes or Hessian-ridge changes.
Public data omit local locations, operational activity timestamps, worker cost/budget records, scheduler identifiers, and transcripts. Mechanism text may retain scientific kernel timing observations.

Source evidence labels and the portable hash manifest are logical references, not links to the private search repository. Original search commit hashes may be local-only; only public_commits are linkable.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: A deeper row batch (24 instead of 16 rows in flight per thread) at unchanged occupancy (80 regs, one 712-thread block per SM) puts 1.5x the gathers in flight and cuts the latency-bound construct by 5-10%.
nodes.falsification: Quick check ratio < 1.01, or the deep build spilling / losing resident warps (cuobjdump, occupancy), refutes it.

hypotheses.falsification: Quick check (100 rounds, 2 pairs) ratio < 1.02 vs master, or nsys construct time per round not lower by >= 8%, refutes it.
hypotheses.hypothesis:
A register-capped instantiation of the same kernel (__maxnreg__ so that two whole-row blocks fit an SM's register file),
with the whole-row block height chosen by cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor to maximise resident warps
(over both instantiations), raises resident warps from 23 to ~34-46 per SM, putting more independent gathers in flight
-> construct time -10-20% (0.25-0.5 ms/round), i.e. quick-check ratio >= 1.04.
hypotheses.observation:
The pair-joint construct is 2.44 ms of a 6.24 ms round (39%). ncu: long_scoreboard stalls dominate, DRAM at 62% of peak,
issue slots ~30%, and occupancy is 23.8 of 48 warps/SM: at 64 registers/thread one 712-thread whole-row block fills the
register file (occupancy limit registers = 1 block). It is a gather-latency-bound kernel short of warps.

src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu: move the pair-joint kernel body into a device function, add a
second __global__ wrapper with __maxnreg__; host: for whole-row launches choose (kernel, rows per block) maximising
resident warps via the occupancy API, grid y re-derived by the same formula and guard. include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h:
new cuda_plan key pair_resident_rows (default on).
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Refuted. The 40-register build spills (120-152 B stack) in the 16-row batch loop: 60-round runs at 48 resident
warps gave 10.2-11.2 ms/round (2, 3 or 4 rows per block) vs 6.06 ms for the uncapped 4-row block; the quick check of
the auto choice (capped, 2 rows) measured ratio 0.588 (md5 identical). Uncapped 1-row (30 warps) 6.18 and 5-row
(28 warps) 6.15 ms vs 6.06: more resident warps alone showed no gain beyond noise in single 60-round runs.

hypotheses.falsification: Quick check ratio < 1.01, or the deep build spilling / losing resident warps (cuobjdump, occupancy), refutes it.
hypotheses.hypothesis:
A build of the same kernel with a deeper row batch (24 rows in flight per thread instead of 16), launched for
whole-row blocks only when the occupancy API reports the same resident warps as the 16-row build, puts 1.5x the
gathers in flight per warp at unchanged occupancy -> construct -5-10% (0.12-0.25 ms/round), i.e. ratio >= 1.02.
hypotheses.observation:
With the 4-row whole-row block (712 threads, 23 warps) one block per SM is all that fits, and at 64 registers it
uses 47K of the 64K register file: up to 88 registers/thread still keep the same 23 resident warps. The construct
is long-scoreboard bound (each warp issues one 16-row batch of gathers, waits a full DRAM latency, then does 16
shared atomics), DRAM at 62% of peak; the 8 -> 16 row batch measured -11% earlier.
hypotheses.plan:
src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu: batch depth as a template parameter of the pair-joint inner
body; the second __global__ wrapper (replacing the refuted capped build) instantiates it with 24 rows and
__launch_bounds__ keeping one 23-warp block resident; host picks it by the occupancy API at equal resident warps.
include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: cuda_plan key pair_deep_batch (replacing pair_resident_rows).
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Refuted. The 24-row build compiled to 80 registers, no spill (0-8 B stack), same 23 resident warps, md5 not needed as
it lost: nsys (40 rounds each, same session) construct 2.604 ms/round (deep) vs 2.400 ms/round (16-row default),
+8.5% slower; 60-round e2e runs alternated 3x: 7.13 / 6.59 / 6.63 ms (deep) vs 6.51 / 6.39 / 6.55 ms (default).
More gathers in flight per warp at unchanged occupancy makes the construct slower, so it is not limited by
outstanding-load count (together with verdict 1: neither more warps nor deeper batches help).

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Reading two row bytes per thread with one 16-bit load doubles bytes in flight per load and halves per-byte index/gradient loads, speeding up the gather-latency-bound pair-joint construct by 15-25% on even-width trees.
nodes.falsification:
If the quick check (100 rounds, 2 pairs) shows ratio < 1.02 vs master's parent level (i.e. no gain over c027's 1.022),
or nsys shows the pair-joint kernel time per round not falling by at least 8%, the hypothesis is refuted.

hypotheses.falsification:
If the quick check (100 rounds, 2 pairs) shows ratio < 1.02 vs master's parent level (i.e. no gain over c027's 1.022),
or nsys shows the pair-joint kernel time per round not falling by at least 8%, the hypothesis is refuted.
hypotheses.hypothesis:
Letting each thread own two consecutive bytes (4 compact columns, two joint tables) and read them with one 16-bit load
doubles the row bytes in flight per load and per register, and halves the per-byte index and gradient loads (89 instead
of 178 threads per row read them). With the kernel latency-bound at 2/3 of DRAM bandwidth, this should cut the
pair-joint kernel time by 15-25% on trees where the row width is even (the 16-bit loads need 2-byte aligned rows),
i.e. ratio >= 1.04 on this workload (about half the trees have an even row width) and more if odd rows are covered too.
hypotheses.observation:
The pair-joint construct is 2.41 ms of 5.25 ms GPU time per round (46%). ncu: DRAM throughput 65-68%, 60% of warp
stall samples are long_scoreboard (global loads), issue slots only 26-33% busy, 1 block of 890 threads (28 warps) per SM
limited by 64 registers. SASS: each thread issues one LDG.E.EF.U8 per row (one byte of the 178-byte row) plus a
broadcast index load and a broadcast gradient load for the same row; 16 rows per batch is all 64 registers allow.
hypotheses.plan:
src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu: a template width W (1 or 2 bytes per thread) for the pair-joint
inner loop and kernel; the host launches W=2 (block x = row_bytes / 2) for the whole-row path when the row width is
even, under a new cuda_plan key pair_u16 (include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h, default on). Same rows per block-row grouping,
same per-block row extents and grid (pair_block_rows re-derived for the new block width and register count), same flush rule.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Refuted. md5 identical, but the quick check gave ratio 0.957 vs master (stock 5.97 ms, candidate 6.24 ms/round).
nsys per launch (60 rounds): two-byte kernel 283 us avg (80 regs, 89x4 blocks, 2/SM) and 314 us avg (72 regs, 89x5,
2/SM) vs 266-268 us for the one-byte kernel. ncu on the two-byte kernel: DRAM 60-64% (one-byte: 65-68%), occupancy
47%. The row bytes moved per load doubled but DRAM throughput did not rise: the gather sits at the DRAM efficiency
of random ~200-byte row reads (~200 DRAM bytes per row, ~65% of peak), not at the bytes in flight. Side finding: the
one-byte kernel is codegen-sensitive (the same source under __launch_bounds__(1024,1) ran 284 us, +6%).

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Keeping the gradient array L2-resident with an evict_last policy removes ~0.5-0.85 DRAM sector per gathered row at deep levels, cutting construct time 5-8% (ratio >= 1.025).
nodes.falsification: ncu on the same deep-level construct launches: if L2 hit rate does not rise by >= 5 points or L2->DRAM sectors/row do not fall by >= 0.3, or the quick e2e check shows ratio < 1.01, the hypothesis is refuted.

hypotheses.falsification: ncu on the same deep-level construct launches: if L2 hit rate does not rise by >= 5 points or L2->DRAM sectors/row do not fall by >= 0.3, or the quick e2e check shows ratio < 1.01, the hypothesis is refuted.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Loading the packed gradients with an L2 evict_last cache policy (createpolicy + ld.global.nc.L2::cache_hint), while the row bytes keep their evict-first streaming loads, keeps the gradient array resident in L2 across the pairs of a level (and across levels), removing ~0.5-0.85 DRAM sector per row at levels 3-9 -> construct DRAM bytes -6..-10%, construct time -5..-8%, i.e. e2e ratio >= 1.025.
hypotheses.observation: The pair-joint construct is 47.5% of train GPU time (2.65 ms/round). ncu: DRAM 60-62% of peak, long-scoreboard stalls ~60%, shared atomics only 22% of their peak. Per gathered row the kernel pulls 6.9 (level 2) to 7.4 (level 4) 32-byte sectors from L2, ~98% of them from DRAM (L2 hit 2.8-7.7%); the 178-byte row is 6.5 sectors, so the 4-byte gradient gather costs up to ~0.85 sector (~11%) per row at deep levels, although the whole gradient array (22 MB) would fit in the 96 MB L2.
hypotheses.plan: src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu: ConstructPairRowBatch takes an L2 cache policy and loads the gradient with ld.global.nc.L2::cache_hint (sm_80+, else __ldg); the pair-joint kernel creates an evict_last policy (cuda_plan key on) or evict_normal (off). include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: new key pair_grad_l2_keep (default on). Bit-identical by construction (same values loaded).
hypotheses.verdict_text: Refuted. The cache hint engages: ncu on the same six deep-level launches shows the construct's L2 hit rate up from 2.8-7.7% to 16.8-24% and kernel durations down from 345/387/387 us to 306/354/354 us. But ncu replays every kernel several times with caches uncontrolled, so the evict_last gradient lines stay warm from the previous pass, which flatters the result. End to end there is no gain: quick check vs master 1.0013 (2 pairs, md5 identical). Same-binary alternating A/B with pair_grad_l2_keep off vs on, 3 pairs x 100 rounds: 1.0000, paired saving 0.003 ms [-0.047, +0.052] ms/round (0.04%). The construct is not bound by the gradient gather's DRAM bytes; the row-byte gather sets its time. Not committed.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Striding each leaf's construct chunks so the resident blocks span the whole leaf instead of a contiguous 14-42% slice speeds levels 1-4 by 4-7%, the mirror image of H1's +7% slowdown from narrowing the fetch region.
nodes.falsification: Same-session nsys A/B (on/off/on/off, 40 rounds): L1-L4 construct summed less than 3% faster with the key on.

hypotheses.falsification:
Same-session nsys A/B (key on vs off): if the construct time summed over the levels with >= 8 pairs drops by < 5%,
or the quick check ratio is < 1.01 with md5 identical, the hypothesis is refuted.
hypotheses.hypothesis:
Dispatching the blocks pairs-fastest and placing each leaf's chunk gy at phase ceil(gy*G/n_p) (n_p = the leaf's
non-empty chunks) makes the concurrently resident blocks of all the level's smaller leaves walk the same global row
region together (combined density ~30-50% instead of 1-3%). Gradient sectors (8 rows per 32 B) and the partial
sectors at 178-byte row boundaries are then shared through L2, and DRAM pages serve several rows per opening.
Expected: L2 hit rate up, DRAM bytes down 10-20% on the many-pair levels, their construct time down 10-20%
(~0.2-0.35 ms/round), i.e. quick-check ratio >= 1.03. Bit-identical: the same (leaf, chunk) work items with the
same rows per block; only which hardware block index runs them changes (integer sums).
hypotheses.observation:
The pair-joint construct is 2.57 ms of 5.41 ms GPU time per round; the levels with 8-62 pairs take ~310 us each
(1.86 ms/round). Its grid is (1, G, P) and dispatch runs y fastest, so the ~170 resident blocks work on 1-2 leaves
at chunks spread over the whole row space; each deep leaf holds 1-3% of rows, so a block's consecutive rows are
5-18 KB apart. ncu: DRAM 55-64% of peak, L2 hit rate only 16-30%, ~466 MB of L2 read requests per 16-pair launch.
hypotheses.plan:
New cuda_plan key `pair_phase_order` (include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h, default on). In
src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu, CUDAConstructDiscretizedHistogramPairJointBatchedKernel takes a
flag; when set and gridDim.z > 1 it maps its linear block id to (phase = id / P, pair = id % P), computes the leaf's
chunk count n_p from the same rows-per-thread formula the inner body uses, runs chunk gy = floor(phase*n_p/G) only
if ceil(gy*G/n_p) == phase, and passes gy to the inner body instead of blockIdx.y.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Refuted. Same-session nsys A/B (40 rounds, 31 steady trees each, on/off/on/off): construct per tree 2683/2675 us
with pair_phase_order on vs 2513/2551 us off; levels 3-9 summed 2216 vs 2077 us (+6.7% slower with the order),
level 1 (unaffected, one pair) within noise. Quick check: 0.990 (md5 identical across the 3 runs that completed).
Concentrating all resident blocks on one region of the matrix loses more (fewer DRAM channels/banks busy at once)
than the shared sectors gain: the spread of today's dispatch across the row space is an asset, not a waste.

hypotheses.falsification: Same-session nsys A/B (on/off/on/off, 40 rounds): L1-L4 construct summed less than 3% faster with the key on.
hypotheses.hypothesis:
If concurrency over a narrow region is what cost H1 its 7%, the mirror image should gain: dispatching each pair's
chunks with a multiplicative stride (chunk = L * a mod n_p, a ~ n_p / SM count, coprime with n_p) makes the first
~SM-count blocks of a pair cover the whole leaf. Expected: L1-L4 construct 4-7% faster (40-70 us/round), deep levels
unchanged; quick-check ratio ~1.005-1.01 (near noise, so the nsys per-level A/B is the deciding measurement).
hypotheses.observation:
H1's A/B: narrowing the region of the row space that the resident construct blocks fetch from at once (pairs
interleaved at the same phase) cost +7% at L2 (2 pairs) and +7-10% at L7-L9. In today's pair-major order the
resident set (~170 blocks, one per SM) is already spread over whole leaves at the deep levels (n_p <= 160 chunks per
leaf), but at the levels with large per-leaf grids it is a contiguous slice of one leaf: L1 400 chunks (42% slice),
L2 ~1213 chunks per pair (14%), L3 ~650 (26%), L4 ~400. These levels take 155+300+259+293 = ~1.0 ms/round, and run
4.1-6.2 G rows/s.
hypotheses.plan:
Replace the H1 remap with key `pair_spread_order` (include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h, default on): pair-major dispatch
kept; in CUDAConstructDiscretizedHistogramPairJointBatchedKernel a block of row index y < n_p runs chunk
(y * a) mod n_p, a from the host-passed SM count; same chunks, same rows per block, bit-identical.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Refuted. Same-session nsys A/B (40 rounds, 31 steady trees each, on/off/on/off): L1-L4 construct summed
1000/999 us with pair_spread_order on vs 992/984 us off (+1.1% slower, not >= 3% faster); whole construct per tree
2550/2550 vs 2525/2520 us (+1.1%), all kernels 5380/5379 vs 5359/5348 us. The order of a leaf's chunks does not
matter (spread or contiguous slice: same speed); H1's +7% came from interleaving different leaves' blocks, not from
the narrowness of the region. Nothing committed; diff in [local artifact omitted]

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: An L2 prefetch of the tile after next puts a second 22.8 KB tile per block in flight, so the fused fill's next-tile loads hit L2 instead of stalling the unpack, cutting the fill 10-20% (ratio >= 1.025).
nodes.falsification: nsys fill-kernel time (same session, A/B by plan key) reduced by less than 3%, or quick-check ratio vs master not above the parent's ~1.02 (below 1.025) refutes it.

hypotheses.falsification: nsys fill-kernel time (same session, A/B by plan key) reduced by less than 3%, or quick-check ratio vs master not above the parent's ~1.02 (below 1.025) refutes it.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Issuing an L2 prefetch (prefetch.global.L2, no registers, no data change) for the source chunks and gradients of the tile two steps ahead puts a second tile per block in flight from DRAM, so the register loads of the next tile become L2 hits that arrive within the write+hist phase. This removes most of the unpack wait: fill kernel time drops 10-20% (1.525 -> 1.25-1.37 ms), i.e. 0.15-0.27 ms per round, quick-check ratio >= 1.025.
hypotheses.observation: The fused fill + root histogram kernel takes 1.525 ms of a 6.04 ms round (29% of GPU time). It moves 1.97 GB at 1.29 TB/s = 73% of DRAM peak while issue is only 53% active. 28% of its warp stall samples sit at the first use of the register-prefetched source words of the next tile (long scoreboard) and ~10% at the tile barrier: the words for tile k+1 are issued only after tile k is staged, one write+hist phase ahead, and they have not arrived when that phase ends. Each block keeps at most one 22.8 KB tile of loads in flight, and a deeper register prefetch would exceed the 64-register budget of the 2-blocks-per-SM launch.
hypotheses.plan: New cuda_plan key root_hist_l2_prefetch (include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h, default on). In CUDAFillCompactData4BitTiledRootHistKernel (src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu), on the word-prefetch path, prefetch to L2 the sectors of every source column's chunk (only bytes holding valid rows) and the gradients of tile step+2 right after the register loads of tile step+1 are issued (and tile step+1 before the loop). Host passes the key through LaunchFillCompactData4BitTiledRootHistKernel (cuda_histogram_constructor.cpp). Bit-identical by construction (a cache hint).
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Confirmed, smaller than predicted: fill kernel -6.3% (nsys, same session, 40 rounds per arm: 1423/1432 us with the
L2 lead vs 1523/1524 us without), i.e. -95 us/round GPU time; quick check vs master 1.0352 (3 pairs, quiet box,
md5 identical; parent c027 was 1.022), predicted >= 1.025 overall and 10-20% on the fill.
Engagement finding on the way: the fill's register word-prefetch path (root_hist_prefetch) was silently OFF on
this data: colmajor_direct's column-major store packs columns (num_data + 1) / 2 = 2,731,899 bytes apart (odd),
so the host's 4-byte-alignment check failed and the byte-staging path ran (ncu: 30.4 M byte LDGs vs 0.9 M word
LDGs). colmajor_align (column pitch rounded to 32 bytes) engages it, but the word path alone is worth only -0.3%
(1513 vs 1518 us); the L2 lead on top of it is the gain. Measured and dropped: a two-tile L2 lead (1550 us, worse
than none: 1512 us) and a compile-time-unrolled, loads-before-adds root-histogram loop (1430-1435 vs 1434-1435 us,
neutral; the fill is not bound by its histogram instruction stream).

nodes.observation: The fused fill + root histogram kernel takes 1.525 ms of a 6.04 ms round (29% of GPU time). It moves 1.97 GB at 1.29 TB/s = 73% of DRAM peak while issue is only 53% active. 28% of its warp stall samples sit at the first use of the register-prefetched source words of the next tile (long scoreboard) and ~10% at the tile barrier: the words for tile k+1 are issued only after tile k is staged, one write+hist phase ahead, and they have not arrived when that phase ends. hypotheses.hypothesis: With an even slot count and the one-run tile (row stride = slot count, 2-byte aligned), each lane reads two neighbouring slots with one 16-bit LDS. hypotheses.hypothesis:
Warp specialization with TMA: one producer warp per block loads the row indices and gradients and issues one
cp.async.bulk (TMA) copy per gathered row (its 16-byte-aligned 192/208-byte span) into a shared-memory ring of
stages, completing on per-stage mbarriers; the consumer warps only read bytes/gradients from shared memory and do
the atomics. TMA copies are not tracked by the L1 miss path and need no registers, so 3-4 stages (~200+ rows per SM)
stay in flight continuously, including while consumers do atomics. Expected: DRAM utilisation 65% -> 75-80%,
construct -12-20% (-0.3-0.5 ms/round), i.e. quick-check ratio >= 1.04 vs master (>= 1.02 over the parent).
hypotheses.observation:
The whole-row pair-joint construct is 2.41 ms of a 6.05 ms round (9 launches). ncu at real clocks: DRAM read 64-68% of
peak (1.13-1.21 TB/s, 6.6 sectors per gathered row, no overfetch), IPC 1.34 of 4, L1 requests ~23%, shared atomics ~26%:
nothing saturated. 55-60% of warp samples are long-scoreboard stalls, concentrated on the first use of each 16-row batch
(the byte extract and the first atomic). Every gathered row byte is an LSU load tracked by the SM's L1 (at most
5 rows x 16 batch = 80 rows per SM in flight, and none while a warp does its 16 atomics). Earlier MLP attempts that
stayed on the LSU path (48 warps via maxnreg, 24-row batch, u16 loads) were neutral.
hypotheses.plan:
- include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: new cuda_plan key pair_tma (default on).
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu: new kernel CUDAConstructDiscretizedHistogramPairJointTmaKernel
  (sm_90+ PTX: mbarrier init/arrive.expect_tx/try_wait.parity, cp.async.bulk global->shared), same per-block row ranges
  (block_start / block_num_data, per_pair_rows, level_row_blocks) and the same marginal flush as the whole-row
  pair-joint kernel, so per-block integer sums are identical; host launch for the whole-row pair_hist path when the
  device is sm_90+, the row data are 16-byte addressable with padding, and the ring + tables fit in shared memory.
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cpp: pad the compact buffer allocation by 64 bytes (16-byte-rounded
  row spans of the last rows stay in bounds).
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Refuted. md5 identical in all three variants. (a) One producer warp issuing per-row TMA bulk copies: quick check 0.747
(8.10 vs 6.05 ms); ncu shows 58% of samples spinning on the full barrier, DRAM 37-40%: per-lane bulk copies get
serialized into a uniform-register loop, so the copy-issue rate is far too low for ~200-byte rows. (b) Four producer
warps with gradients/indices prefetched a stage ahead: 0.799. (c) Four producer warps issuing 16-byte cp.async chunks
(26 warp instructions per 64-row stage), completion via cp.async.mbarrier.arrive, 5 stages = up to 320 rows per SM in
flight (vs 80): quick check 0.999 (6.163 vs 6.157 ms). ncu for the same launch: 333.8 us vs 323.0 us, DRAM read
374 MB vs 366 MB, i.e. the read rate stayed at 1.12 vs 1.13 TB/s. Four times more rows in flight did not move the
DRAM read rate, so in-flight depth / L1 miss tracking is not the limit; the gather runs at a DRAM-side ceiling of
~1.13 TB/s read for this access pattern.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Fusing the sync into the find kernel (the last finished block of each leaf, counted by a per-leaf atomic, runs the
used-task sync body for that leaf) removes one launch and its latency chain per level and lets the reduction of
early leaves overlap the find of later ones: saves ~5-8 us per level, 50-80 us of ~6.3 ms per round, ratio 1.008-1.013.
hypotheses.observation:
Per level the warp split finder (FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel, 8-29 us) writes one CUDASplitInfo per
(task, leaf) and the next kernel, SyncBestSplitForLevelUsedTasksKernel, immediately re-reads them to reduce one
best split per leaf. The sync kernel costs a near-constant 7.4-8.9 us per level (0.081 ms/round, 10 launches) at
every level from 1 pair to 512 pairs: ncu shows 2 blocks, 4.8k instructions, 15k active cycles at level 1, i.e.
a pure latency chain plus launch ramp. The construct (2.41 ms, 46%) and fill (1.50 ms, 29%) are the big items, but
six earlier workers found nothing on the construct; this is the hint's back-to-back producer/consumer pair.

(pair, role); a fused variant of the warp find kernel calls the per-item body, then __threadfence + per-leaf atomic
completion count; the completing block runs the sync body and resets the counter. Host skips the sync launch when
the fused kernel ran. New cuda_plan key fused_level_sync (include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h), default on.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Refuted. nsys, 60 rounds, same session: the fused find+sync kernel takes 28.0 us/level (0.280 ms/round) against

up to +7 us at deep levels (27.3 vs 20.4). Total kernel time 5.271 vs 5.242 ms/round. The sync's cost is its own
dependent-load chain (L1TEX scoreboard 40-47% of stalls), not the launch; inside the find kernel it pays two
gpu-scope fences + L1 invalidation + an atomic round trip, and runs on 128 instead of 256 threads. The 2-pair

Same-binary e2e A/B (pair_u16 on vs off, >= 2 pairs, 100+ rounds) below 1.01 for every variant, with ncu showing the

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Two bytes per thread (one 16-bit load) halves the threads per row, so at the same register budget the SM keeps ~1.7x
more gathered rows in flight (24 warps x 16 rows / 89 threads per row = 138 rows vs 80) and issues half the index and
gradient loads per byte. If the kernel is latency bound (not at the DRAM row-gather ceiling), this cuts pair-joint
time by >= 8% on engaged (even-width) trees, i.e. ratio of pair_u16 on vs off >= 1.02 (same binary).
The suspected limiter on the wide kernel is the shared-atomic pipe (2 ATOMS per thread per row with half the
threads, i.e. the same atomics per SM but more per warp instruction stream): if so, varying batch depth and block
rows should move it.
hypotheses.observation:
The pair-joint construct is 2.40 ms of 6.29 ms per round (38%; 268 us/launch, 9 launches). ncu: 890-thread blocks
(178 bytes x 5 rows), 64 regs, 1 block/SM (28 warps, 58% occupancy), DRAM 68.6%, issue 30%, long_scoreboard 58% of
stalls. Each thread gathers one byte per row (LDG.U8), plus a broadcast index and gradient load per row. c029's
two-byte kernel (pair_u16) measured 0.957 vs master, but on a build whose one-byte kernel was slowed 6% by
__launch_bounds__; its nsys per-launch numbers (283/314 us vs 267 us) mix shapes and were never A/B'd on one binary.
hypotheses.plan:
Re-apply c029's pair_u16 diff (src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu, include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h),
verify the one-byte kernel's SASS is unchanged vs the parent, then same-binary A/B pair_u16 on/off (e2e.py, both arms
this venv). Variants: batch depth kB (16, 8, 24), rows per block (pair_y via the resident-warp rule, forced 4/5/6+),
register cap (__launch_bounds__ min blocks 1 vs 2).
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Same-binary e2e A/B (pair_u16 on vs off, 100 rounds x 2 pairs, alternated; same-arm stock spread 0.0-0.4%): best
variant 0.9908 (kB=8, 89x10), others 0.9876 / 0.9806 / 0.9752 / 0.9716 / 0.9513. Never above 1.0; md5 identical throughout.
1. Defects fixed and re-measured: the one-byte kernel's SASS is byte-identical to the parent's (64 regs, the c029
   __launch_bounds__ slowdown is absent); the wide kernel's even per-lane table stride (pair_pad broken) was fixed by a
   parity-ordered layout (+2.1%); no variant spills (STACK:0).
2. Deciding numbers are same-binary A/Bs with the key off in --plan-stock, 2 pairs each, noise <= 0.4% between stock runs.
3. Mechanism: rows (gathered bytes) in flight per SM rose 11% to 90% across variants, DRAM throughput did not move
   (1.0-1.3 TB/s either way) and the kernel did not get faster: the pair-joint gather is at the DRAM efficiency of random
   ~180-byte row reads, not at its loads in flight. The doubled shared atomics per thread are not more conflicted
   (3.65 wavefronts per ATOMS in both kernels, same ATOMS count); their 32-deep per-warp bursts do raise mio/lg throttle
   at the 16-row batch, which batch 8 removes, but that only recovers parity.
4. Six variants measured: batch depth 16/8/4, block rows 5/10/11, registers 72/64/56, table layout host vs parity.
Side finding: fewer, taller blocks (y=5 -> 10 at the same residency) gained ~1% (half the zero/flush per row).

nodes.falsification:

DRAM bytes fell refutes it (bytes are not what binds); if DRAM bytes did not fall, the limit did not engage (defect).

hypotheses.falsification:
Same-binary alternated A/B (pair_l2_prefetch on vs off, >= 2 pairs): construct nsys time not lower by >= 2%, with

L2 hit rate does not rise, the prefetch did not engage (defect).
hypotheses.hypothesis:
Issuing an L2 prefetch (prefetch.global.L2, one thread per 32-byte sector of each row) for the rows of batch b+1
while batch b runs puts the next batch's DRAM reads in flight without holding registers or L1 lines; the demand loads
of batch b+1 then hit L2. More bytes in flight at the DRAM -> construct -4-8% (0.09-0.18 ms/round), ratio vs parent
>= 1.015.
hypotheses.observation:
The pair-joint construct (capped build, 48 regs, 178x2 blocks, 36 warps/SM) is 2.233 ms of 5.760 ms/round (38.8%).
ncu: long_scoreboard 39% of stalls, DRAM 66-68% (1.16-1.19 TB/s), L1 hit 65%, L2 hit 33-35%, issue 37%. c037 showed
more resident warps (28 -> 36) cut it 5.6%, i.e. it is still bound by the gathered bytes in flight, which registers
(48 x 36 warps, 15 rows/thread) and L1 staging (the 100 KB-carveout shapes lost) cap. A batch is ~2.6 us per lane,
much longer than a DRAM round trip.

in the gathering loop a thread with x < kB*sectors_per_row loads the index of row x/spr of the next batch one batch
ahead and issues prefetch.global.L2 for its sector. New capped gather instantiation with PF; host picks it under a

hypotheses.verdict_text:
1. Defects fixed and re-measured: the sink loads deleted by ptxas (fixed: accumulator + no-op atomic guard, loads in
   SASS); spills (spill-free variants (14,56), (12,52) sink, and (14,48) line prefetch, measured).
2. Deciding numbers, same binary, key on vs off alternated, 2 pairs each (same-arm spread 0.02-0.07 ms): line
   prefetch +5.7%, spill-free bulk prefetch +9.3%, spill-free L2 sink +2.6% (+2.0% vs its 56-register no-sink
   control), spill-free L1 sink +2.5-3.5%. nsys same binary, 60 rounds x 2 alternated pairs, spill-free L2 sink
   (14,56) vs off: construct 2.374/2.380 vs 2.239/2.238 ms/round (+6.1%; same-arm spread 0.006), all kernels
   5.225/5.234 vs 5.059/5.057.
3. Mechanism: ncu shows the quantity moved: L2 hit of the construct 37% -> 54% (line prefetch), 47-61% (bulk), 64%
   (sector-exact L2 sink, DRAM bytes unchanged within 2-4%), yet time did not drop (+1% ncu, +2% e2e). The L1 sink
   engaged only partly (L1 hit unchanged at 64%: the 64 KB L1 evicts ~40% of the warmed sectors). The pair-joint
   gather at 36 warps is not bound by its DRAM latency (and, verdict 2, not by its DRAM bytes): serving the rows
   from L2 instead of DRAM does not help; the prefetch instructions lose by over-fetching whole lines (+35-39%).
4. Variants: prefetch.global.L2 lead 1/2, bulk prefetch lead 1/2 (spilling and spill-free), ld.volatile dead load,
   ld.cg sink (L2) and ld.ca sink (L1) lead 1 at (14,48),(12,48),(14,52),(14,56),(12,52),(13,56),(12,56): six ways
   of issuing the warm-up, batch 12-15, caps 48/52/56.

hypotheses.falsification:
Same-binary nsys A/B pair_wide_rows on vs off (alternated, >= 2 pairs): construct not >= 4% faster while ncu shows LSU
instructions per launch down >= 30% refutes it (LSU count is not what binds). If LSU instructions did not fall, the

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Each thread owning two adjacent row bytes (four compact columns, two joint tables) read with one 16-bit load cuts the
warp-level LSU instructions per row from ~4 x 5.6 = 22 (24 with the 12th partial warp) to ~5 x 2.8 = 14 (-40%): index,
gradient and byte loads are issued by half as many warps, atomics unchanged. At equal resident warps (register-capped
build, occupancy-chosen height; c029's 2-byte try ran at 47% occupancy / 80 regs, a confound) this relieves the
LSU-pipe bound -> construct -8-15% (0.18-0.33 ms/round), ratio vs parent >= 1.03.
hypotheses.observation:
The pair-joint construct is 2.233 of 5.760 ms/round (38.8%). ncu (parent, real clocks): the LSU pipe issues at 75.4% avg /
81% max of peak (l1tex lsuin requests 75.4%, L1 throughput 80% of active), mio_throttle + lg_throttle are 26% of stalls,
while DRAM is at 67%, L2 hit 33%, issue 38%. Every prior lever on the memory side (4x rows in flight via TMA, L2 warming,
32 B fetch granularity) was neutral, and every one that added LSU instructions (prefetch, sink loads) was slower. Per
row and warp the kernel issues 4 LSU instructions (index LDG, gradient LDG, row-byte LDG.U8, shared ATOMS), the index
and gradient being the same broadcast for all 5.6 warps of a 178-byte row.
hypotheses.plan:
src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu: a whole-row "wide" pair-joint inner body (two byte contexts per
thread, u16 row loads, same row grouping / block extents / flush rule) in a __maxnreg__ build; host picks block height
(89 x c threads) by the occupancy API with the same carveout rule; only when row stride is even (2-byte aligned rows).
include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: cuda_plan key pair_wide_rows (default on). Bit-identical: same rows per block, integer sums.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
1. Defects fixed: the first build spilled (168 / 88 B stack; two byte contexts held across the loop as structs); fixed
   by scalar contexts re-derived for the flush; all three measured variants are 0 stack. The capped kernels are
   unchanged (48 regs, 0 stack).
2. Deciding number: same binary, pair_wide_rows on vs off alternated, 2 pairs per arm: construct 95.1-96.0 vs
   89.04/89.11 ms per 40 rounds (+6.8-7.8%; same-arm spread <= 0.15 ms); all kernels +3.0-3.4%.
3. Mechanism: ncu (real clocks) shows the LSU quantity moved: LSU pipe 27-31% of peak (wide) vs 49-66% (capped) in the
   same run, LSU instructions per row ~14 vs ~22, shared-atomic wavefronts/instr 3.5 vs 3.3; rows per ns did not rise
   (4.4-4.5 wide vs 4.5-4.7 capped). The construct is not bound by its LSU instruction rate.
4. Variants: three batch / register points (8/6@48, 10/8@56, 12/8@64), all +16-18% on the engaged launches.
Do not retry: fewer LSU instructions per row (2 bytes per thread) for the pair-joint construct.

hypotheses.hypothesis:

removes ~4% of the construct's rows, the expensive deep ones, and their find tasks: construct -4% (~0.09 ms/round),
all kernels -1.5-2%, ratio vs parent >= 1.015, bit-identical.
hypotheses.observation:
H1 shows the construct runs at a fixed ~4.5 rows/ns at deep levels whatever its instruction mix, so the remaining lever
is fewer rows. A tree dump (5 trees of this workload, my build) counts, per child depth, the smaller-leaf rows the
level construct reads and those in pairs where NEITHER child can split by count (both n + 2 < 2 * min_data_in_leaf =
20000): depth 5: 0.8%, 6: 2.7%, 7: 5.4%, 8: 10.6%, 9: 16.1% of the level's construct rows; 4.0% of all construct rows
(~0.52 M of 13.0 M per tree), all at the expensive sparse levels. Their histograms (and split searches) have no reader:
the finder rejects every threshold of such a leaf (both children need min_data_in_leaf). The existing construct_valid
gate only skips pairs whose leaves are both <= min_data_in_leaf. c026 (master lineage, accepted neutral with a
0.95-1.04 CI) gated exactly this; it is not in this lineage.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Coalescing the tree start's metadata uploads (split finder masks, histogram masks, compact-view layout, fill slot tables, fused-root
meta) into one pageable cudaMemcpyAsync into a device staging arena plus one scatter kernel, both on the same legacy stream right
before the fill launch, replaces ~14 copy-engine operations by 2 operations -> the fill starts ~15-20 us earlier per round
(round -0.3%, same-binary A/B saving >= 12 us/round), host API time at the tree start -20 us.
hypotheses.observation:
The tree start is device-command-queue-bound (fill launched at host t=158 us, started at GPU t=220 us). Ahead of the fill on the legacy stream sit
14 separate pageable H2D metadata copies (~46 KB in total, sizes 20 B .. 17.7 KB) that take 21.5 us of GPU timeline (t=195.9..217.4),
about 1.5 us per copy-engine operation, for data that one copy moves in ~2 us. (c041's Untried #1: one arena for the tree start's uploads.)
hypotheses.plan:
New cuda_plan key `tree_meta_batch` (default on, only with async_tree_start). New header src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_meta_batch.hpp
(batch: pageable host staging, device staging, segment table passed by value to a scatter kernel defined in
cuda_histogram_constructor.cu). UploadTreeStartMeta (cuda_leaf_splits.hpp) and LaunchCompactFill's upload lambda append to the
batch while a scope opened in CUDASingleGPUTreeLearner::BeforeTrain (split finder BeforeTrain .. BuildCompactView) collects;
flushed before every GPU operation in that region (each fill launch, the host-source staging path) and at scope end.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Predicted: ~14 copy-engine operations -> 2 at the device-command-queue-bound tree start, fill starting 15-20 us earlier, same-binary saving
>= 12 us/round. Measured on the final build (4888319a):
1. Defects: none known in the kept build. Existing kernels' codegen unchanged (construct 48 regs, fill 63 regs, no spills); new
   kernels MetaBatchScatterKernel 10 regs, BeforeTrainLeafInitKernel 34 regs, no spills. The one variant that made things worse
   (V4, kernel-parameter uploads per level) was measured and reverted, not kept.
2. Same-binary A/B, e2e.py 300 rounds x 6 pairs alternated, key off in --plan-stock: 5.477 -> 5.450 ms/round, paired saving
   27.0 us [16.4, 37.6] (0.49%), same-arm SD 0.010 ms; earlier builds: V1+V2 6.3 us [-9.0, 21.6] (4 pairs), V1-V3 27.6 us
   [14.4, 40.9] and 17.8 us [11.3, 24.3] (6 pairs each). md5 identical key on/off.
3. Mechanism (nsys 60 rounds, the quantity the hypothesis moves): tree-start GPU operations ahead of the fill 14 H2D + 6
   copy/memset -> 1 H2D + 2 kernels; GetGradients end -> fill start 167.2 -> 148.3 us/round (144 in p2/p3); FillDataIndices end
   -> ReduceMinMax 14.6 -> 1.9 us; fill end -> first root-level kernel 28.1 -> 23.7 us; tree end PrepareLeafBestSplitInfo ->
   leaf-map pass 64.2 -> 45.4 us; GPU-timeline round 5592 -> 5544 us; kernel time unchanged (5031 -> 5045 us, run-to-run).
4. Variants: V1 batch (-12.6 us to the fill under nsys), V2 leaf-init kernel (-10.3 us), V3 root sums one wait (-5 us after the
   fill), V5 page-locked tree readback (-19 us at the tree end), all kept; V4 level descriptors by launch parameters (+70 us,
   reverted). The e2e effect is smaller than the nsys one for V1/V2: CUPTI inflates every small GPU operation.
Quick check vs master on the final build: 1.0821 (md5 identical); parent c041 was 1.0752.

refutes the mechanism (copied rows did not drop); if it drops but all-kernel time does not fall by >= 0.3%, the saving is below use.

refutes the mechanism (copied rows did not drop); if it drops but all-kernel time does not fall by >= 0.3%, the saving is below use.
hypotheses.hypothesis:
After a level's gap copy and swap, both ping-pong buffers hold every terminal range of that level (the old main was only read). At the next
level the out buffer IS that old main, so a range that was already terminal there is copied onto identical values. Copying only the ranges
that became terminal at this level (gaps minus the previous level's gaps, tracked on the host; reset at every tree start and by every other
writer of the two buffers) cuts the gap copies from ~60 to ~30 us/round: HybridCopyDataIndicesBatchKernel -40-55%, all kernels -0.5%,
bit-identical (same values in the same buffer).
hypotheses.observation:
skip_unsplittable's untried items are exhausted on inspection: subtract / changed-bit copy / fix already skip construct-invalid pairs, and a
constructed pair (one leaf splittable by count) always has a splittable larger leaf (n_L >= n_S), so no subtract has an unread output; no
tighter "cannot split" bound exists without the leaf's own histogram. The same kind of work without a new reader remains in the level apply:
HybridCopyDataIndicesBatchKernel, 0.064 ms/round (5.73 launches), carries every terminal leaf's index range from the old main array into the
out buffer before the swap, at every remaining level (c040 timeline: 1.9, 4.3, 7.3, 18.0, 28.5 us at the last five levels, growing with the
accumulated terminal rows).
hypotheses.plan:
src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cpp/.hpp/.cu: SplitLevelBatched subtracts the previous level's gap set from this level's gaps
(two-pointer interval difference), launches copies for the remainder, stores this level's gaps; BeforeTrain, Split, SetUsedDataIndices,
ResetTrainingData, ResetConfig, ResetByLeafPred, SetLeafDataLayout, CollapseLeafWindows, the graph-flow functions and the mutable index
accessors invalidate the set. include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: cuda_plan key gap_copy_once (default on).

no new content or no reader) carried to the subtract, changed-bit copy and fix (-0.9%) and to the block shape of the tree-end map
pass and gap copy (-0.3%): all kernels 296.97 -> 290.89 ms per 60 rounds (-2.05%, all keys, same binary), same-binary e2e 300 x 3:

hypotheses.falsification:
Same-binary nsys A/B colmajor_dense5 on vs off (2+ pairs, alternated): fill not lower by >= 2.5% (with ncu DRAM bytes
per fill down by >= 50 MB) refutes it; e2e quick check vs master below the parent's ~1.12 by more than noise refutes it.
hypotheses.hypothesis:
A per-column codec copy (base 5 for columns below 5: 10 words per tile; base 6 for the rest: 11 words), with digits
stored as MSB-first 32-bit fixed-point fractions (decode = umulhi(F, b) + F *= b, 2 ops per digit instead of 3, and
skipping k digits = one multiply by b^k), cuts the fill's source bytes by ~9% (~-60 MB of 1.66 GB) and its decode
instructions by ~1/3. Mixed slots use the base-6 12-row grid and read a base-5 column's 12 rows from the tail of word
q-1 and the head of word q (skip by multiply). Expected: fill 1.25 -> ~1.19 ms (-4..-6%), round -0.05..-0.07 ms,
ratio vs parent >= 1.008.
hypotheses.observation:
Parent profile: the fused fill (CUDAFillCompactData4BitTiledRootHistKernel<1,6>) takes 1.252 ms of the 5.347 ms round
(23.4%), DRAM 71.7% busy, 1.66 GB per fill (0.67 GB base-6 source + 0.97 GB compact-view writes). c044 showed the fill
is byte-bound (an 8% source-byte cut gave -6% fill despite +39% instructions). 98% of the columns (3465/3525) hold only
values 0-4, so base 6 (12 rows / 32-bit word, 44 B per 128-row tile) wastes ~9% of their bytes vs base 5 (13 rows per
word, 40 B per tile). The previous worker's Untried #1 (per-column codecs) was blocked by mixed slots (a byte slot whose
two columns use different codecs, ~6 per tree).

- cuda_histogram_constructor.cu: per-column flag scan (>= 5, >= 6) replacing the any->=6 scan; encoder for codec 5
  (per-column offset table, fraction digits); fused fill DENSE == 5 path (load per column tile words, all-base-5 slots
  decode 13 rows per item, others 12 with the split read for base-5 columns); L2 lead with per-column tile words.
- cuda_histogram_constructor.cpp/.hpp: offset table, codec selection in MaybeBuildColMajorDense3, launch argument.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
The per-column base-5 part of the hypothesis (fewer source bytes -> faster fill) is refuted:
1. Defects: the variant-3 spill (8/16-byte stack) is gone in variant 7 (0 spill); the divergent mixed-slot decode
   (variants 1-3) is gone in variant 7 (one code path); every number above was taken on builds without known defects
   except variant 3 (noted).
2. Deciding number, same binary, nsys 60 rounds, alternated, 2 pairs: colmajor_dense5 on vs off fill 1219.2/1221.4 vs
   1226.5/1228.3 us (-0.6%; same-arm spread ~2 us), round within noise; the predicted -4..-6% fill is not reached.
3. Mechanism check (ncu, same binary): DRAM bytes per fill moved as predicted (-58 MB, -3.5%), the time did not
   (1.2797 vs 1.2801 ms) because the decode cost +3.7% instructions: at ~1.27 TB/s the fill is co-limited by issue,
   and each byte saved now costs as much in decode as it saves in DRAM time.
4. Variants measured: 1 (divergent, load), 2 (divergent, shuffles), 3 (divergent, class mask), 7 (uniform 13-row grid).
The decode-instruction part was split off as Hypothesis 2 (below) after variant 3's ncu showed the issue co-limit.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: H2 (ended on): fused-fill blocks of equal work finish up to a block's lifetime apart, so blocks sized for many waves of the resident blocks (with each block's second tile prefetched into L2 at its start) cut the end-of-kernel idle and the fill time by 3-4%; H1 (refuted as quantified, change kept): a warp-uniform root-histogram slot loop cuts fill instructions about 30% and fill time 5-10%.
nodes.falsification:
Same-binary nsys A/B root_hist_short_blocks on vs off (2 pairs): fill not lower by >= 2%, or ncu SM active cycles / elapsed not
higher, refutes it.

hypotheses.falsification:
Same-binary nsys A/B (key on vs off, 60 rounds, alternated, 2 pairs): fill not lower by >= 2% while ncu instructions drop by
>= 20% refutes it (instructions not dropping = defect in the implementation).
hypotheses.hypothesis:
A warp-uniform slot loop (full groups of 32 slots unrolled with compile-time offsets, one predicated tail group, per-lane bases
hoisted out of the row loop) runs the same atomics in ~50 instead of ~120 warp instructions per row: fill instructions -30..-40%,
ATOMS -14%; with the fill co-limited by issue (55%) and DRAM (73%), fill -5..-10% (60-120 us/round), ratio vs parent >= 1.01.
hypotheses.observation:
Parent profile: the fused fill takes 1.226 ms of the 5.357 ms round (22.9%); ncu: DRAM 73%, issue 55%, top stalls
short_scoreboard and mio_throttle. Own ncu SourceCounters: of the fill's 1.202G warp instructions 58% are the root-histogram
loop (warp per row, lanes over the 178 byte slots): ~120 warp instructions per row where ~48 do the work. The slot loop's trip
count differs per lane (5 or 6 slots), so it compiles into a 4-unrolled loop plus a divergent remainder (BSSY/BSYNC, 7 ATOMS
pairs per row instead of 6: 76.5M ATOMS = 14 per row), and the per-row prologue rematerializes the shared bases (~30 instr).
hypotheses.verdict_text:
1. Defects: v2's per-group rematerialization (instructions +3%) is gone in v3 (9 instr per group, 64 regs, 0 spill). v3's
   binary compiles the key-off path ~1.5% slower than the parent's (off 1236-1253 vs 1228 us), so the deciding A/B is v1's,
   whose off arm matches the parent (1228.6/1229.3 us).
2. Deciding number: same-binary nsys A/B (60 rounds, alternated, 2 pairs), v1: fill 1209.2/1209.2 vs 1228.6/1229.3 us,
   -1.6% (same-arm spread 0.7 us); v3 on vs the parent build: 1209 vs 1228 us (-1.5%). Below the predicted -5..-10% and the 2%
   bar of the falsification.
3. Mechanism check (ncu, v3 same binary): instructions -24% (1.221G -> 0.933G), shared atomics -14% (76.5M -> 65.6M), issue
   55.6% -> 43.1%: the quantity moved as predicted; the time moved -1.5% (nsys) / -4.7% (ncu): with fewer instructions the fill
   became DRAM/latency-bound (DRAM 73.5% -> 76.8%), so issue was a smaller share of the limit than assumed.
4. Variants: v1 (uniform loop), v2 (+ batched loads, byte bases), v3 (byte bases, sequential), v4 (+ one-group load
   pipelining: no gain over v3, so in-loop latency is not the limit).
The -1.5% fill is real and kept (root_hist_uniform_slots, default on). Same-binary e2e 300 x 2 with only this key off in the
stock arm: 1.0187 (off 5.244/5.226, on 5.133/5.145 ms), md5 identical; it overstates the gain over the parent's code, since
this binary's key-off path is compiled ~1.5% slower in the fill than the parent's loop.

hypotheses.falsification:
Same-binary nsys A/B root_hist_short_blocks on vs off (2 pairs): fill not lower by >= 2%, or ncu SM active cycles / elapsed not

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Blocks sized for many rounds of the resident blocks (short blocks) cut the end-of-kernel idle (about half a block per resident
slot) at a small per-block cost (setup, first tile without lead, flush); prefetching each block's second tile into L2 at its
start removes most of that cost. Predicted: SM active fraction up by ~2 points, fill -3..-4% (40-50 us/round), ratio vs parent
>= 1.007.
hypotheses.observation:
After v3 the fill is DRAM/latency-bound (DRAM 76.8%, issue 43%). Achieved occupancy 64.96% of 66.67% theoretical (parent ncu):
2668 equal-work blocks of 16 tiles (7.85 waves) start as slots free up, so they finish up to a block lifetime (~150 us) apart.
Tiles-per-block sweep (env override): 16: 1210 us, 32: 1240, 64: 1281, 8: 1174, 6: 1169, 4: 1175, 2: 1341: the fill tracks
~half a block lifetime of tail (~1.9 us per tile of block length); at 2 tiles the L2 lead never engages.
hypotheses.plan:
falcata_plan.h keys root_hist_short_blocks and root_hist_lead_start (default on); cuda_histogram_constructor.cu: the fused fill
launch picks the kernel first, takes the occupancy API's blocks per SM x SM count, tiles per block = clamp(ceil(tiles / (resident
x 32)), 4, 16) under the packed row bound; the kernel prefetches tile_first + tile_step into L2 after its first register load.

hypotheses.observation:
After the final level's apply (gap copy ends at +5428.5 us in round 30 of the parent trace) the GPU needs ~105 us to
reach AddPredictionToScore, of which it is busy ~27 us (map pass 20.4 us). The rest is host round trips: the final
level's InvalidateLeafCandidates uploads its 448-byte leaf list with a synchronous cudaMemcpy (the host blocks 131 us
in it until split-inner ends) and then synchronizes the device after a 0.9 us kernel, so the residual-leaf map pass
starts 16.6 us after the apply although nothing between them needs the host; at the tree end sync_node_counts reads
back the 1040-byte per-leaf counts (6.4 us host call + launch gap) that the host already holds exactly in
leaf_num_data_ (every level's batch-info readback) when every leaf came from the batched prefix.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
The deep-level gen-bit is bound by gather latency x loads in flight, not DRAM bandwidth: 8 rows per thread in
128-thread blocks (same 1024-row chunks, ballot words and block totals) doubles the gathers in flight per thread and
the resident chunks per SM -> deep-level gen-bit -20-30% (0.354 -> ~0.28 ms/round), split-inner unchanged or a bit
faster -> ratio >= 1.01 (e2e), nsys gen-bit kernel time <= 0.30 ms/round.
hypotheses.observation:
The batched level apply costs 0.58 ms/round (gen-bit 0.354 + split-inner 0.226, 9.5% of the 6.08 ms round). Gen-bit
grows from ~19 us (levels 1-3) to 54-56 us (levels 7-9) while the rows per level shrink: at deep levels each row's
split bin is a separate 32-B sector gather (one sector per row, ~4M rows per level). With apply_row_batch the kernels
run 256-thread blocks of 4 rows per thread (1024-row chunks): 4 dependent gathers in flight per thread.
hypotheses.plan:
include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: cuda_plan key apply_rows8 (default on). src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu:
LaunchSplitLevelBatchedKernels instantiates HybridGenBitVectorUpdateLeafIndexBatchKernel<8> and
HybridSplitInnerBatchKernel<8> with block_dim / 8 = 128 threads (static_assert whole warps per pass).
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Deep-level gen-bit is DRAM-bandwidth-bound (91% of peak, ~1 sector per row), not bound by gathers in flight.
1. Defect fixed and re-measured: the per-row branch-serialized bin load (SASS) was fixed by apply_bin_batch (loads now
   batched; no spills in any variant, 40/48/96 regs, 0 local); the unchanged split-inner was restored to 4 rows after
   its 8-row build measured +10%.
2. Deciding number: same-binary e2e A/B apply_bin_batch on vs off, 100 rounds x 2 pairs alternated: 1.0005 (same-arm
   spread 0.2%); nsys A/B x2 each: gen-bit -0.1%.
3. Mechanism: loads in flight moved (SASS), time did not; ncu shows DRAM at 91% of peak in both arms.
4. Three variants measured (8 rows both kernels; bin batch at 4 rows; bin batch + 8-row gen-bit), all <= 0.1% or slower.
Do not retry more rows/loads in flight for the apply gen-bit. Only fewer DRAM bytes per row would help there (one
sector per row at deep levels; e.g. reading the split bin from the compact view so the sector stays in L2 for the
next level's construct, measured nowhere).

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Encoding up to three consecutive compact columns per byte as the joint cell (b0*s1 + b1)*s2 + b2 (spans 5-6 give
125-216 cells; the byte is directly the cell of a per-group joint table, so the construct needs no decode at all) cuts
the row from 177 to 118 bytes: about 28% fewer DRAM sectors per gathered row. That makes the construct 20-26% faster
(shadow: -26%) and the fill writes 1/3 fewer bytes (-0.13 ms bound). Predicted ratio >= 1.10 (construct -0.6 ms, fill
-0.1 ms of 6.07 ms).
hypotheses.observation:
Both top kernels are at their bandwidth ceilings for their access patterns (parent profile): the pair-joint construct
(2.519 ms/round, 41.5%) gathers 177-178-byte nibble rows at ~1.1 TB/s (DRAM 62%, long_scoreboard 61%, issue 27.6%),
and the fused fill (1.503 ms/round, 24.7%) reads 970 MB and writes 972 MB per tree at DRAM 74%. Night-2 already found
the construct gather at its DRAM-efficiency ceiling: "only fewer bytes per row left". The nibble view spends 8 bits
on two 5-6-bin columns (25-36 combinations). perf-dead-ends.md re-opens denser codecs "when the construct is
read-bound again", which it now is (issue 27.6%). Atomics are not the limiter: the global flush uses 4.8% of L2 atomic
capacity, and shared atomics were already ruled out by c022 (cell-major tables neutral).
hypotheses.plan:
- `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h`: cuda_plan key `pair_triple` (default on).
- `cuda_histogram_constructor.cpp`: per tree, group layout (consecutive compact columns, greedy up to 3 while span
  product <= 256; tables padded to odd strides) and metadata upload. The fused root fill gets the metadata, and
  `compact_triple_` records that the live view holds group bytes. `EnsureNibbleCompactView()` reruns the plain tiled
  fill when any other reader needs nibbles.
- `cuda_histogram_constructor.cu`: fused fill write-out encodes the staged nibble tile into group bytes (row stride G).
  New `CUDAConstructDiscretizedHistogramTripleJointBatchedKernel` (the pair-joint prologue/grouping, cell = byte,
  3-digit marginals, same flush). The batched dispatch launches it, or calls EnsureNibble when the shape or flow does
  not allow it. EnsureNibble also runs before the per-leaf construct and graph capture.
- `cuda_single_gpu_tree_learner.cpp`: EnsureNibble before the split-view gathers, except the packed split read with
  colmajor_split, which reads the column-major store.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
The e2e hypothesis (ratio >= 1.10) is refuted. (1) The defects found in my own build were fixed and re-measured: the
fill encode went from 2.14 to 1.71 ms (v2), the per-block fixed cost was amortized (v3), occupancy was tried (v4) and
sector-aligned stores were tried (v5). (2) The deciding number is the same-binary A/B pair_triple off vs on: 0.9998
(3 pairs, 300 rounds, same-arm sd 0.027 / 0.012 ms), md5 identical. (3) Mechanism check (ncu, same binary, same
launches): L2 read sectors per launch fell 27-29% as predicted, but construct time fell only 8.6% on average (-21% at
level 1, +5..8% at levels 2-3). So the "construct time scales with bytes per gathered row" mechanism is refuted at
this occupancy: the 59 KB of joint tables drop resident warps 47% -> 31%, and 8-row blocks did not recover it. The
shadow's -26% was flattered: it read the same rows right after the real kernel. (4) Five real variants and two shadow
variants were measured (more warps through 8-row blocks or half-row blocks made the construct slower, 264 / 339 us);
the bound above covers the rest. Untried: a fill that stages group bytes directly (needs a shared-memory budget
rework of the fused fill), level-1 only use (the one level where the triple construct is clearly faster, -21%; it
would still pay the full fill encode).

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Synchronous D2H readbacks pay 2-6 us of copy-engine latency after the producing kernel; a default-stream copy kernel into mapped pinned memory plus a sync of that stream removes it from every level's critical path (~2.5-3 us x 20 readbacks per round).
nodes.falsification:

showing the producing-kernel -> host-wake gap per level not shrinking by >= 1.5 us, refutes it.

hypotheses.falsification:

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Doing the two per-level readbacks with an SM copy kernel on the same (legacy default) stream into the same pinned
buffers (now mapped), followed by a synchronize of that stream (the same blocking point cudaMemcpy had), removes the
copy-engine scheduling latency from the level's critical path: ~2.5-3 us per readback x 20 per round = 50-60 us per
round, i.e. ratio vs parent >= 1.008 (vs master ~1.115). Same bytes copied: bit-identical.
hypotheses.observation:
The parent round is 5.452 ms with the GPU idle 9% (0.494 ms/round). Most of the idle sits in the 10 levels' host
round trips: every level does two synchronous D2H readbacks on the legacy stream (best splits, 168 B per leaf; split
batch info, 72 B per split). The copy engine starts each copy 2-6.5 us after the producing kernel on another blocking
stream ends (Sync -> D2H 34 us/round, TreeStructure/GapCopy -> D2H ~25 us/round), and the host only then wakes.
A microbenchmark on this box: a sync pinned cudaMemcpy D2H waits 4.8 us more than a bare device sync after a
kernel on a blocking stream; a tiny copy kernel on the same legacy stream writing into mapped pinned memory plus a
sync of that stream waits only 1.9-3.3 us more.
hypotheses.plan:
- include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: key `readback_kernel` (default on).
- include/Falcata/cuda/cuda_utils.hu + src/cuda/*.cu: a launcher `CopyDeviceToMappedHostSync(dst_host, dst_dev, src, bytes)`
  (int4 body + byte tail kernel on stream 0, launch error checked, cudaStreamSynchronize(0)).
- cuda_best_split_finder.cu (SyncAllLeafBestSplitsToHost) and cuda_data_partition.cpp (FinishSplitBatch): pinned
  buffers allocated cudaHostAllocMapped, device pointer from cudaHostGetDevicePointer; copy kernel when the key is on
  and the mapping exists, otherwise the old cudaMemcpy.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Readback copy-engine latency was on the critical path, and the copy kernel moves it: the default-stream copy kernel into
mapped pinned memory starts ~0.6-1.7 us after the producer instead of 2.3-6.5 us, the best-split trip per level falls
14.74 -> 12.34 us, fill end -> root search 28.5 -> 21.9 us, and GPU idle per round 0.494 -> 0.43 ms (nsys). Deciding
number, same binary readback_kernel on vs off, alternated, 300 rounds: **1.0060 +- 0.0012** (mean per-pair ratio over
20 pairs from five batches: 1.0060 / 1.0082 / 1.0079 / 1.0037 / 1.0076; median pair 1.0073; 19 of 20 pairs favour on). The prediction (>= 1.008) is not
met on this workload: the per-level readbacks alone gave 1.0039, because the readback after the apply did not speed up
(the legacy-stream copy waits ~2 us on the partition stream either way) and the per-readback saving here is ~2 us,
not the ~3 us of the microbenchmark. Shapes with more readbacks per round gain more (same-binary on/off: higgs 1.017,
year 1.018, missing 1.037, covtype 1.075 at ~3 us x 168 readbacks per round). Quick check vs master 1.1134 / 1.1115,
md5 identical; guards, lattice 83/83 and 13 hand configs identical.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
(1) Sector-aligned column pitch engages the word path, plus a one-tile L2 lead (the tile after next prefetched into L2)
keeps two tiles per block in flight from DRAM -> fill -6% (c032 measured 1523 -> 1423 us on its lineage).
(2) Tiles per block derived from the shape (num_tiles over ~32 rounds of the resident blocks from the occupancy API,
4..16, packed-row bound still caps), with the block's second tile L2-prefetched at its start -> the tail shrinks from
~half a 16-tile block to ~half a 4-tile block: fill a further -3-4%.
Together: fill 1.489 -> ~1.35 ms (-9%), ~-140 us/round -> ratio vs parent >= 1.02.
hypotheses.observation:
The fused fill (CUDAFillCompactData4BitTiledRootHistKernel<1>) takes 1.489 ms/round (27.3% of 5.452 ms) at 73.6% DRAM
with long_scoreboard the top stall (26%). In this lineage the column-major store has an odd byte pitch (num_data odd),
so the fill's word-staging path (register prefetch of the next tile) is silently off and every tile's source is
gathered by dependent byte loads after the barrier. Blocks are fixed at 16 tiles: 2,668 blocks = 7.85 rounds of 340
resident blocks, so the tail idles about half a block lifetime (~95 us).

- src/io/cuda/cuda_row_data.cpp, include/Falcata/cuda/cuda_row_data.hpp: column stride in the store upload/verify.
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cpp/.cu: store stride, kernel L2 lead, block sizing in the launcher.
hypotheses.verdict_text:

column pitch) with 16-tile blocks. Sector-aligned column pitch (word staging + one-tile L2 lead) plus blocks sized from
the shape (tiles over 48 rounds of the resident blocks from the occupancy API, floor 2: 3 tiles here) moved DRAM
utilization 73.6% -> 83.2% (ncu) and the fill 1500 -> 1329 us (nsys, same binary). Deciding number: same-binary e2e
A/B, keys off vs on: 300 rounds x 3 pairs 1.0346 (same-arm spread <= 0.25%), 500 rounds x 6 pairs 1.0346; short
blocks alone 1.0167.
Predicted fill -9% and ratio vs parent >= 1.02: measured fill -11.4% and 1.035. Quick check vs master 1.1380-1.1414.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: The final level of a tree-completing prefix partitions child index windows nobody reads; writing only the row-to-leaf map there (after a full-sector clear that keeps its scatter in L2 instead of fetching every sector from DRAM) and skipping the gap copy and swap removes 25-55 us of GPU work per round.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Writing the map in the gen-bit kernel (which already holds each row's index and direction) and skipping the
final level's split-inner, gap copy and buffer swap removes ~75 us of kernels and two launches while adding the
map scatter (~20-50 us) to the gen-bit: -25 to -55 us/round, ratio vs parent 1.005-1.010 (same-binary key A/B).
hypotheses.observation:
Parent profile: the final batched level's HybridSplitInnerBatchKernel takes 69.5 us (other levels 15-19 us),
plus a 5.8 us gap copy; together 1.4% of the 5.45 ms round. At that level every child sits at max_depth and
(with skip_empty_tail) the tail is known empty, so the partitioned child windows it writes are never read: the
only live output is the row -> leaf map it scatters inline (~52 us of the 69.5 us).
hypotheses.plan:
New cuda_plan key final_map_only (include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h). cuda_data_partition.cu: gen-bit kernel gets a
write_leaf_map flag (same value the split-inner wrote); LaunchSplitLevelBatchedKernels skips split-inner, gap copy
when map_only; cuda_data_partition.cpp: no swap, gap tracking invalidated. Tree learner: engage only on a final
level with level_completes_tree_ && skip_empty_tail, no bagging, no linear tree, no quant leaf renewal, no NCCL,
single target, and an objective known (from RenewTreeOutput) not to renew leaf outputs.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Mechanism: the final level of a tree-completing prefix partitions child index windows nobody reads; dropping that
partition (map-only pass, no gap copy / swap) and clearing the map just before the pass, so its scatter hits L2
instead of fetching every sector from DRAM, removes ~35-39 us of GPU work per round.
Deciding number: same-binary A/B on the final commit 96de02d7, final_map_only off (stock) vs on, 300 rounds x 6
pairs alternated, tuner on, warmup 150: median ratio 1.0073 (-39 us/round); per pair 1.0076 / 1.0042 / 1.0095 /
1.0059 / 1.0108 / 1.0082 (all > 1); same-arm spread 0.27% (off) / 0.51% (on); md5 identical. Earlier 4-pair A/B on
the same code: 1.0068. Predicted -25 to -55 us (ratio 1.005-1.010): inside the range.
Mechanism check (nsys, same session as key off): final split-inner 67.3 us -> 33.0 us map-only pass + 7.0 us
clear, gap copy 7.1 -> 0, final gen-bit start -> map end 172.1 -> 136.8 us. The clear's role was isolated by V2
(same code without the clear: map pass 59.5 us) and V3-early (clear before the gen-bit: map pass still fast, gen-bit
slower). ncu DRAM counters are unavailable on this box (n/a); L2 write sectors of the final pass 3.9M -> 3.3M.
Quick checks vs master: 1.1134 (V1), 1.1158 (V3), 1.1187 (final), md5 identical. Parent's quick checks 1.1074-1.1094.
Variants measured: V1 gen-bit map write (-6 us, dropped), V2 map-only pass (-17 us), V3 + clear (-35 us, kept),
V3-early clear placement (-30 us), residual pass grid 16/8 blocks per leaf (no change). Untried: see ## Untried.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Raising the whole-row pair-joint construct's rows-per-thread floor from 64 to 400 (the large-leaf rate) on the capped
build cuts deep-level block counts 3-6x (L9: 160 -> ~26 blocks per pair) and with them the zero/flush work, while the
tuner's saturation floor keeps the device filled -> deep-level (L4-L9) construct time -8-15% (~130-230 us/round),
ratio vs parent >= 1.015.
hypotheses.observation:
The fused fill (1.328 ms/round, 25%) is at the copy ceiling: ncu shows its DRAM traffic equals the ideal bytes (1.945 GB
of L2 misses) at 1.467 TB/s, and a plain cudaMemcpy D2D of the same 970 MB on this GPU takes 1.321-1.343 ms (copy kernel
1.337-1.350): the fill's mechanism (staging, L2 lead, block shape) is exhausted at 4-bit source bytes.
The pair-joint construct is 2.118 ms/round (40%). On this lineage it runs the 48-register capped build in 2-row
whole-row blocks (177x2 threads), with grids sized by the generic 64 rows/thread floor: deep levels launch 714x16 (L5),
346x28, 371x43, 219x50, 160x51 (L9) blocks = 8,000-11,400 blocks per level for 510 resident slots; levels 4-9 take
1.58 ms/round. Every whole-row block zeroes and flushes all 17.8 KB of joint tables (~4.4K cells, ~1.8K global
atomics), i.e. at L9 ~8,160 x 1.8K = ~14M flush atomics for ~1M gathered rows. c036 (pair_deep_rows: floor at the
large-leaf rate NUM_DATA_PER_THREAD = 400) measured +1.03% on the pre-capped 5-row blocks; it was never ported here,
and the capped build's 2-row blocks have 2.5x more blocks per row, so the fixed cost per row is larger.

1.003 with the kernel drop in place means the kernel saving does not reach the round (e.g. hidden behind host gaps).

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Laying the positions out strided (lane l holds t = l and t = l + 4; inclusive prefixes from two 4-lane scans, integer
sums, same values) puts all four candidates of a 5-bin task in iteration 0, so iteration 1 is skipped by every warp
whose items all have <= 4 candidates (~85% of warps here: only NaN-bin columns have 5). The winner is unchanged: the
reductions are maxima under the total order (gain, then lower threshold), independent of which lane holds which
candidate. FP64 warp instructions per warp drop ~35% -> deep-level find time -25-35%, find total -0.035..-0.05
ms/round, ratio vs parent ~1.007-1.010 (find kernel nsys -25% or more).
hypotheses.observation:
The quantized level split finder FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel<4> costs 0.161 ms/round (3.0% of the
5.28 ms round; 10 launches, 8-31 us). ncu on my tree (real clocks): FP64 pipe 67-76% active at levels 6-10 (26-31 us,
331-1192 blocks), 52-56% at levels 1-5; warps active 8-28%. Each (task, leaf) item gets 4 lanes x 2 positions with
lane l holding thresholds 2l and 2l+1, so a 5-bin task (4 candidates, t = 0..3) uses lanes 0-1 only and the warp
issues both iterations of the double-precision prune and gain loops (prep: int->double unpack, count rounding;
gain: two DDIV) with half its lanes masked off.
hypotheses.plan:

- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.cu: WarpFindBest gets a STRIDED template flag (only G = 4, PPL = 2):
  position t = i * G + lane; per-iteration 4-lane inclusive scans plus earlier iterations' totals; winner lane
  = best_t % G. The level kernel gets the flag as a template parameter; the launcher picks it from the key.

tree-end last-apply -> Shrinkage span shrinks < 15 us with final_readback_first on.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Ordering the final level's readback before the leaf-map pass (the pass then runs while the host finalizes the
tree), dropping the invalidate's device sync, and memoising the capped-rows choice per shape (carveout attribute
set only when it changes) removes ~45-55 us of GPU idle per round: GPU idle per round falls >= 35 us (nsys, same
binary), e2e ratio vs parent ~1.008-1.010 (below the 1% e2e noise floor; the nsys idle number is the deciding one).
hypotheses.observation:
Parent nsys ([local artifact omitted], steady rounds): GPU idle 0.511 ms of the 5.278 ms round (9.7%). Of it,
~108 us/round sits at two per-tree points where the GPU waits on host work the next GPU op does not need:
(a) tree end: the final level's split-batch readback (4032 B) is issued after the early leaf-map pass and waits
20.5 us for it plus ~7 us copy latency; InvalidateLeafCandidates before it ends with a device sync nobody needs
(3.5 us + relaunch); last apply kernel -> Shrinkage launch = 102 us with the GPU busy 21 us of it.
(b) level 1: 27.5 us from the last apply kernel to the construct start (9 us at levels 2-9): 9.7 us of host-only
compute before the launch and 12.4 us launch -> start (3.5 us elsewhere). PairJointCappedRows' one-entry memo is
keyed by the joint-table bytes, which change with every tree's column sample, so every tree re-runs ~12 occupancy
queries and re-sets the capped kernels' carveout attribute (default, then the chosen percent).
hypotheses.plan:
- include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: keys `final_readback_first` (a: map pass launched after the final level's
  FinishSplitBatch; no device sync after the invalidate kernel) and `shape_memo` (b), default on.
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_single_gpu_tree_learner.cpp: move the early map launch behind FinishSplitBatch.
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.cu: InvalidateLeafCandidates without the trailing device sync.
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu: PairJointCappedRows memo as a small per-shape table; carveout
  attribute only re-set when the percent differs from the one last set.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Mechanism confirmed by its pre-registered nsys criteria; the e2e gain is smaller than predicted. (1) No defect left:
kernels unchanged (same per-kernel times on vs off), comments match the final ordering, md5 identical on the

1.0052 (3 pairs, V4) and 1.0039 (4 pairs, final variant: -20.3 us/round, same-arm sd 4-7 us, every cand run faster
than every stock run); one-key-off attribution runs (3 pairs each) 0.9963 / 1.0005, i.e. host jitter of +-0.4% on
this shared machine dominates single A/Bs. (3) Mechanism (nsys, same binary, 2 pairs per variant): tree end (last

us per round. (4) Five variants measured (V1, V3, V4, V5 + attribution). Predicted e2e 1.008-1.010; measured about

stays above 6 us. e2e same-binary A/B under 1.002 with the kernel drop in place: the saving does not reach the round.
hypotheses.hypothesis:
Loading every field of the winning split info (and the task's feature index) into registers before the first
store turns ~23 serialized round trips into ~1-2, and issuing the leaf/desc loads before the task fold overlaps them
with it: sync per level 8 us -> 3.5-4.5 us, -35..-45 us/round (all kernels -0.8%), e2e same-binary A/B ratio about
1.005-1.009. Same values written to the same fields: bit-identical.
hypotheses.observation:
After c056 the level split finder is 98 us/round; its consumer, SyncBestSplitForLevelUsedTasksKernel, costs 82
us/round (7.6-9.1 us per level, flat from 1 to 512 pairs, i.e. a single block's latency chain). The untried c056
variants (survivor compaction, lazy child outputs, NaN-task clustering) each bound at <= ~10 us/round of the find.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Per-level GPU idle comes from the readback round trip and the host's issue order: copying readbacks with a default-stream kernel into mapped pinned memory, issuing the partition's long apply chain before the tree's short split record, and dropping host waits nothing needs cut the round by 1-2%.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Copying each synchronous readback with a tiny kernel on the same default stream straight into mapped pinned host
memory (then that stream's sync) removes the copy-engine start latency and the pageable staging copy: ~3-5 us per
readback x ~24 readbacks per round = 70-120 us/round, i.e. ratio vs parent 1.010-1.020 (c052 measured 1.008 on the
c047 lineage). Mechanism: the same kernels, the same bytes, fewer microseconds between the producer kernel and the
host seeing the data.
hypotheses.observation:
The parent round is 5.347 ms on the GPU timeline with the GPU busy 89%. Steady-state idle is ~473 us/round, and 230+ us of it
sits in the two synchronous readbacks of every host-launched level: the copy engine starts the D2H 2-9 us after the
producing kernel (SyncBestSplit->memcpy2 37 us/round, TreeStructure/CopyDataIndices->memcpy2 26 us/round), and the
host's pageable cudaMemcpy returns ~4 us after the copy ends (part of memcpy2->memcpy1, 154 us/round over ~20
transitions). The tree end adds 4 more D2H readbacks (pooled tree slab, leaf counts) with ~50 us of idle around them.
The two biggest kernels are at their DRAM ceilings (construct, fused fill), so idle is the largest addressable item.

cuda_data_partition.{cpp,hpp}, cuda_leaf_splits.{cpp,hpp}, cuda_tree.{hpp,cpp}, cuda_single_gpu_tree_learner.{cpp,hpp},
falcata_plan.h. Then check in nsys which readbacks of this lineage still go through the copy engine and extend.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Uploading the two per-level descriptor arrays (partition apply descriptors on the partition stream, pair descriptors on
the histogram stream) from page-locked host memory lets the driver queue the DMA without staging the pageable source,
cutting API time and API->DMA start by ~1-2 us per upload: 20 uploads/round -> 20-40 us/round of idle, ratio vs parent
1.004-1.008. Further variants of the same mechanism (shorter host path between readback and upload: read the split infos
in place from the mapped staging, async root leaf-output upload) add 10-20 us/round.
hypotheses.observation:
Parent (a5d16d94) nsys, steady rounds: 328 us/round of GPU idle, ~200 us of it in the two per-level host round trips
(find readback -> GenBit 8.56 us median x 10 levels = 107 us/round; apply readback -> Construct 7.1-7.8 us x 9 = 90 us/round).
The sync itself returns 0.83 us after the copy kernel; the host then works 1.2-4.7 us and issues a pageable
cudaMemcpyAsync of the level's descriptors (2-10 KB; API 1.9 us), whose DMA starts 4.2-4.3 us after the API call. The
consumer kernel is already queued ~2 us before the DMA starts, so the pageable upload's latency is on the critical path.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
1. No defect in the build: the key engaged on both uploads (1200 pinned H2D copies per 60 rounds), no kernel or
   register change (host-only change).
2. Same-binary A/B key off vs on, 2 pairs alternated: 0.9997 (0.988 / 1.012), same-arm spread up to 0.085 ms.
3. Mechanism check: the quantity the hypothesis moves (API start -> DMA start of the per-level H2D, and the readback ->
   consumer-kernel gap) is unchanged: 4.2 us with a pinned source as with a pageable one, and equal to the idle-GPU
   kernel launch latency in the same trace (4.58 us API start -> GPU start). The pageable staging is not what delays
   the copy; the front-end issue latency is, and it is paid by any GPU operation the host issues after the readback.
4. Why iteration cannot help: every variant of "upload the descriptors differently" (pinned, mapped zero-copy read by a
   copy kernel, write-combined) still issues one GPU operation after the readback whose start is bounded by the same
   ~4.2-4.6 us issue latency; the only removable piece is the cudaMemcpyAsync API call itself (1.9 us of host time
   before the kernel launch) by passing the descriptors as kernel parameters: bound 1.9 us x 20 = 38 us/round (0.75%),
   on 5+ kernels per level whose descriptors are 2-10 KB (above the classic 4 KB parameter limit). Not built.
