hypotheses.hypothesis:
Same mechanism as c062 (fewer, fuller per-level apply kernels): each gen-bit chunk's thread 0, after storing its counts, does a
threadfence + one 64-bit atomicAdd on a per-split word (chunks done << 32 | left rows so far); the block that takes the split's
last ticket runs that split's aggregate (L2 reads, warp-striped tiled scan of the left counts, right offsets from the chunk row
counts and the known left total; same integers) and resets the word. This removes the aggregate launch + its launch gap per level
and runs most splits' aggregates while other splits still gen-bit. Expected: apply-chain span -25..-40 us/round on the GPU timeline
(aggregate 36 + ~10 gaps, minus the last split's in-kernel prefix and the per-chunk atomic), i.e. same-binary e2e ~1.005-1.008.
hypotheses.observation:
Parent profile (2f3cbf55): every host-launched level runs gen-bit (35.5 us avg) -> HybridAggregateBlockOffsetBatchKernel (3.6 us avg,
2.2-7.1 us, 10 launches/round = 0.036 ms/round) -> fused partition (24.5 us) on stream 0, all serial on the level's critical path.
The aggregate is one 1024-thread block per split: an in-place prefix over that split's per-chunk left/right counts plus 6 leaf
metadata stores. A split's counts are final as soon as its own last gen-bit chunk ends, not when the whole gen-bit grid drains.
hypotheses.plan:
- include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: key apply_aggregate_fused (default on).
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu: HybridGenBitChunk returns thread 0's left count; gen-bit kernel's flat path takes an
  optional per-split counter array and runs a block-wide aggregate device function in the last chunk's block; host launch passes the
  counters and skips the aggregate kernel when every split has >= 1 chunk.
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.{hpp,cpp}: counter buffer (num_leaves + 1 words, zeroed once, reset in-kernel).
hypotheses.verdict_text:
1. The one defect found (54 registers with K=8, 4 instead of 6 gen-bit blocks/SM) was fixed (K=4, 40 = master) before every
   measurement. 2. Same-binary nsys A/B, key off/on alternated, 2 pairs: apply kernels 637.7/636.2 -> 640.7/639.3 us/round, span
   650.4/659.9 -> 661.1/655.8 (same-arm spread ~10 us): no gain (predicted -25..-40). 3. Mechanism: the aggregate's 10 launches/round
   are gone (nsys), so the fusion engaged; the time moved into the gen-bit kernel instead (+42 us/round, +4..6 us at every level).
   4. Variants: v1 (fence + atomic), v2 (acq_rel atomic), v3 (timing-only relaxed bound), plus the K=2/4/8 register sweep. A
   last-block ticket inside a latency-bound gather kernel with ~5 waves of one-chunk blocks costs more than the launch it removes.
   Do not retry the last-block pattern on the gen-bit kernel; it may still pay in kernels of one wave (find -> sync), unmeasured.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Folding the per-leaf sync into the find kernel (the find block that completes a leaf's items, detected with a per-leaf arrival counter after a fence, runs the same sync body for that leaf) removes one launch per level and lets each leaf's reduction overlap the later leaves' searches; only the last leaf's tail stays exposed (~3-5 us instead of 8-9 us + gap). Expected: level find+sync time -40..-60 us/round, ratio >= 1.008 for the sync fold alone; with the same fold applied to the apply aggregate (gen-bit's last block per split scans that split's block counts) another -30 us/round, together ratio >= 1.012.
hypotheses.observation: The parent profile shows each of the 10 levels per round ending its split search with SyncBestSplitForLevelUsedTasksKernel, a 2 x pairs block kernel (2-102 blocks of 256 threads on 170 SMs) taking 7.2-9.1 us (0.081 ms/round, 1.3%) plus a 0.3-1.2 us launch gap, right behind FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel (8-30 us). The sync only reduces the find's per-task outputs per leaf; at shallow levels (1-4 pairs) it occupies 2-8 SMs serially, at deep levels it starts only after the whole find grid drains. The same shape holds for HybridAggregateBlockOffsetBatchKernel (num_splits blocks, 2.3-6.8 us, 0.036 ms/round) behind the gen-bit kernel.

Defects: V1's 12-spill codegen fixed in V2 (2 STL/LDL left in one branch of the search body; the key-off arm's find, same binary, is 165-167 vs the parent's 163.7 us/round, so the search body itself is unchanged within 2%); fences measured separately (V1 -> V2: -3 us/round). 2. Mechanism: the quantity was the level's find -> readback critical path and the sync launches: the launches went 10 -> 0 per round, but the path did not shrink because the sync's 7.5-9.2 us is the in-block latency chain of its body (fold of dependent loads over ~355 used tasks, 20-field winner copy), not the launch: the find -> sync launch gap was 0.3 us at 8 of 10 levels (4.0 us/round), and the chain cannot overlap the later leaves' search because every find launch fits in one wave (<= 1126 blocks of 128 threads vs 7 x 170 resident at 72 registers), so every leaf completes in the final wave and its tail runs after it, on a 128-thread block (3 fold passes instead of the sync's 2). 4. nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Storing the pair-joint cell as a 5-bit code (6 per word, 128-B sector-aligned rows) cuts the construct's DRAM sectors per gathered row by ~39% at equal occupancy, so the construct speeds up roughly in proportion and outweighs writing the code view next to the nibble view in the fused fill.
nodes.falsification:
Same-binary A/B (pair_code5 off vs on), nsys 60 rounds x 2 pairs: construct time must fall >= 20% and round time
(construct + fill) >= 4%; quick check vs master below 1.03 refutes the net effect.

hypotheses.falsification:

hypotheses.hypothesis:
The pair-joint construct's cell for a byte slot is lo * span(hi) + hi, which is < 32 whenever span(lo) * span(hi) <= 32
(5-value features: 25). Storing that cell as a 5-bit code, six codes per 32-bit word, makes the row 30 words, padded to
32 words = 128 B on a 32-byte boundary: exactly 4 sectors per gathered row instead of ~6.56 for the 178-B nibble row
(-39% DRAM sectors) with the same 25-cell joint tables (same occupancy) and one 32-bit load per thread per row instead
of a byte load. Gather rate ~ 1/bytes -> construct -30..-38% (2.52 -> ~1.65 ms/round). The fused fill writes the code
view next to the 4-bit view (+128 B/row = +0.70 GB/tree, fill ~+0.35..0.45 ms), so net ~ -0.4..-0.5 ms/round:
ratio >= 1.06 (quick check). (A follow-up can drop the 4-bit view where nothing else reads it: another ~-0.6 ms.)
hypotheses.observation:
- Parent: pair-joint construct 2.519 ms/round (41.5%), 9 launches; own nsys + model dump: 13.8 M gathered rows/round at
  4.5-5.6 G rows/s (L1..L9: 145 286 255 290 304 312 321 312 289 us for 0.73 1.55 1.43 1.58 1.58 1.54 1.55 1.42 1.30 M rows).
- Zero-code A/B colmajor_split off (split reads from the compact view, warming the next level's rows in L2): construct
  unchanged (2512-2525 vs 2515 us/round), GenBit 7x slower. L2 warming across kernels buys nothing.
- Standalone gather microbenchmark (same block shape, 16 rows in flight per thread, conflict-free shared histogram, 1.6 M
  rows of 64 leaves out of 5.46 M): rows/s is set by bytes per row, not by access count or order:
  96 B 9.67, 119 B 7.54, 178 B 4.93, 192 B (sector-aligned) 5.01 G rows/s; row-major instead of leaf-major order +3..7%.
  The kernel moves ~0.9 TB/s of row payload whatever the row size. (c051's triple packing was confounded by its
  125-cell tables cutting occupancy 47% -> 31%.)
hypotheses.plan:
- include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: cuda_plan key pair_code5 (default on).
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu: fused fill writes, per tile row, 32 words of 6 five-bit codes
  (code = lo * hi_span + hi from the staged tile byte; per-slot hi_span uploaded); new instantiation of the
  pair-joint batched kernel that reads word x/6 of the row and takes the code as the joint cell.
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cpp/.hpp: eligibility (fused fill one-run whole-row layout,
  every slot's span product <= 32, buffer fits), allocation, launch parameters.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Measured: the code view itself works as a mechanism and is bit-identical (V2 probe: md5 identical, e2e 1.0304 vs
master; ncu: DRAM misses -36%, construct -13..-17% per launch at equal occupancy). But the hypothesis as planned
(dual write, ratio >= 1.06) is refuted by a bound: writing the code view next to the nibble view adds 0.70 GB per
tree to a DRAM-bound fill (+525 us/round measured in A1, >= ~+430 us even with the cheaper V2 packing), more than
the construct's best measured gain (-301..-335 us/round), so every dual-write variant is a net loss (A1 nsys:
+222 us/round). The variant that wins (code view replacing the nibble write, +3.0% e2e) is not committable: about
20 other readers of the nibble view (non-whole-row construct paths, small-leaf and JIT kernels, the tree
learner's stored gather pointer used by the classic-split fallback and the packed split view, prefill swap) would
read an unwritten buffer on other configurations. Same-binary A/Bs were 1 pair per variant in nsys (same-arm
spread of construct time in this session ~0.5%: 2524.5 vs 2512.1 us), with 2-pair quick checks for A2/V2/V4. Nothing
committed.

hypotheses.observation:
The parent's tree boundary is GPU-packed (gaps 0.3-1 us between kernels from AddPrediction to the fill), so only
GPU work removed from that serial chain shortens the round (c066's mechanism). The tree start runs
GetGradientsKernel_RegressionL2 (49.8 us: reads scores + labels, writes 44 MB float grad/hess), then
ReduceMinMaxChunkWarpKernel (26.0 us) re-reads those same 44 MB only to produce per-1024-row-chunk min/max
partials, then ReduceBlockMinMaxKernel (3.2 us) folds them into the scales. GetGradients' 1024-thread blocks are
exactly the discretizer's 1024-row chunks.

  discretizer takes (consumes) them if the pointers, num_data and chunk count match.

The parent's tree boundary is GPU-packed (gaps 0.3-1 us between kernels from AddPrediction to the fill), so only
GPU work removed from that serial chain shortens the round (c066's mechanism). The tree start runs
GetGradientsKernel_RegressionL2 (49.8 us: reads scores + labels, writes 44 MB float grad/hess), then
ReduceMinMaxChunkWarpKernel (26.0 us) re-reads those same 44 MB only to produce per-1024-row-chunk min/max
partials, then ReduceBlockMinMaxKernel (3.2 us) folds them into the scales. GetGradients' 1024-thread blocks are
exactly the discretizer's 1024-row chunks.
nodes.plan:
- include/Falcata/cuda/cuda_gradient_minmax.hpp (new, header-only): a small mutex-guarded registry keyed by the
  (gradients, hessians) device pointers: the objective publishes "partials of these gradients are at P", the
  discretizer takes (consumes) them if the pointers, num_data and chunk count match.
- src/objective/cuda/cuda_regression_objective.{cu,cpp,hpp}: L2 gradient kernel variant with the block min/max
  partials into objective-owned buffers; publish after launch; drop entries in the destructor.
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_gradient_discretizer.cu: skip the chunk kernel when partials were taken;
  ReduceBlockMinMaxKernel reads partials from a source pointer set (== its own buffers otherwise).
- include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: key grad_minmax_fused (default on).

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: The GPU-bound tree-start chain spends ~40-60 us on work whose result is known (constant hessians read twice from a 22 MB array, zeroing histogram slots and slot halves that are never written); removing it shortens the serial chain one for one.

hypotheses.falsification: Shadow build: construct ms/round (nsys, 60 rounds) rises < 3% over the parent's 2.046 ms -> refuted.
hypotheses.hypothesis:
If the gradient gather misses L2 at deep levels, it costs up to ~13% of the construct's DRAM sectors; carrying the
packed gradient inside the compact row (written by the fused fill, which already reads it for the root histogram)
removes that sector for +1-2% row bytes -> construct -5..-10%, ratio >= 1.02. First check (bound): a shadow build that
adds one more gradient-like gather per row; if construct time rises < 3%, the gradient sector is not on the critical
resource and the mechanism cannot pay.
hypotheses.observation:
The pair-joint construct (2.046 ms/round, 43% of the round) is a DRAM-bound gather (70% DRAM cycles, L2 hit 33.6%).
Per gathered row it reads the ~178-byte compact row (~6.5 sectors) and, through a second random access, the row's
packed int32 gradient (22 MB array): at sparse (deep) levels one extra 32-byte sector per row, ~13% of the row bytes.
hypotheses.plan:
1. Shadow measurement build (not committed): extra gather of gradients at a shifted row index in ConstructPairRowBatch.
2. If it costs >= 5%: fill writes the gradient into a row tail, construct reads it from the row (cuda_plan key).
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Bound check of the mechanism: one more gradient gather per row adds 0% (-0.4%, within noise) to the construct, so
removing the existing one can save at most about as much; the row-embedded gradient (which also widens each row by
1-2%) cannot pay. 1. The shadow build had no defect (48 regs, no spill, loads present in SASS). 2./3. Deciding number
is the nsys kernel sum of the shadow vs parent (same capture setup); the quantity (gradient sectors in flight per
row) was doubled and time did not move. 4. Why iteration cannot help: the timing-only build bounds every variant of
"fewer gradient bytes per row" (int16 gradients, gradient in row, L2 hints) at <= 0.4% of the construct (< 0.2% e2e).

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Reading one hessian instead of 5.5 M (constant-hessian objectives without weights; same value, same expressions) and
zeroing only the slots that can be dirty (leaves before the tree-completing final level) removes ~22 MB x 2 of reads
and ~half of the memset from the tree start's critical chain: minmax 26 -> ~14 us, discretize 29 -> ~21 us, memset
26.6 -> ~14 us, i.e. ~30-35 us/round = 0.6-0.8% (ratio vs parent >= 1.005; nsys kernel sum -30 us).
hypotheses.observation:
The tree start is a GPU-bound serial chain on the default stream (parent nsys, round 30: GetGradients start -> fused
fill start 188 us, gaps <= 2.4 us). Two of its steps do work whose result is known without doing it:
- ReduceMinMaxChunkWarpKernel (26.0 us) and DiscretizeGradientsKernel (29.3 us) read the 22 MB float hessian array
  that the same round's L2 gradient kernel filled with the constant 1.0f (objective IsConstantHessian, no weights).
- The histogram pool memset (67.3 MB, 26.6 us) zeroes every slot of the previous tree's num_leaves, but slots of the
  leaves created by a tree-completing final level (about half of a depth-capped tree's leaves) are never written:
  no histogram is built after that level and the skip_empty_tail tail does not run.

- include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: keys const_hess_reads, dirty_final_slots (default on).
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_gradient_discretizer.{hpp,cu}: CONST_HESS instantiation of the warp min/max and the
  discretize kernels (hessian of row 0 for every row), taken when the learner reports constant hessians.
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_single_gpu_tree_learner.{cpp,hpp}: constant-hessian gate (is_constant_hessian and no
  dataset weights) passed to the discretizer; num_dirty_leaves = first leaf index of the tree-completing final level
  when the prefix completed the tree and the tail was skipped.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Measured: same-binary A/B of the three keys 1.0083 (6 pairs, every pair > 1; B4's two keys alone 1.0060, every pair
> 1, noise ~0.45%), predicted >= 1.005. Mechanism moved as stated: the hessian read traffic of min/max and discretize
halved (ncu L2 read sectors 1.37 M -> 0.68 M per launch each), the pool zeroing went from 312 full slots to 252
half slots (77.7 -> 27.8 MB), and the tree start's serial chain is 36 us shorter. Best variants B4 (warp-uniform
known-hessian branch) + B5 (half-slot zeroing); B2 slower, B3 neutral. A quick check vs master cannot resolve a
0.8% effect (1.268-1.276 vs the parent's accepted 1.281 [1.252, 1.311]).

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Load-first in the per-split block-offset prefix (registers, one store per entry, block sized to the split) removes its dependent global chains: aggregate kernel -10 us/round (root_apply_direct, H1, confirmed separately: root gen-bit 29.8 -> 16.4 us).

hypotheses.falsification: Same-binary nsys (root_apply_direct on vs off, 2 alternated pairs): if the root gen-bit + split-inner together drop by less than 10 us per round, or md5 differs, the hypothesis is refuted.
hypotheses.hypothesis: When the main index buffer still holds the identity of BeforeTrain (host-tracked: set by the index fill, cleared by every other writer and by the first batched apply), the batched level apply's gen-bit and split-inner compute row = leaf_data_start + position instead of loading it: the root gen-bit becomes a coalesced 2.7 MB column read (29.7 -> ~8 us) and the split-inner drops its 22 MB read (15.2 -> ~11 us). Expected -25 to -30 us per round, i.e. ~0.5-0.6% (ratio ~1.005 vs parent; below e2e noise, so judged by same-binary nsys kernel time of the root launches).
hypotheses.observation: Own nsys of the parent build: the root level's gen-bit takes 29.7 us and its split-inner 15.2 us, while level 1 (same 5.46M rows, two leaves) takes 18.9 us gen-bit. The root's index list is the identity written by FillDataIndicesBeforeTrain before the 1.33 ms fill, whose 1.9 GB stream evicts it from L2, so the root gen-bit reads 22 MB of indices from DRAM through an index -> bin dependent chain, and the split-inner reads the same 22 MB again. all_rows_direct reads position p as row p in the fused fill / root construct but its sibling, the root's partition apply, still gathers.

- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.{hpp,cpp,cu}: main_indices_identity_ flag (set after LaunchFillDataIndicesBeforeTrain; cleared wherever level_shared_gaps_valid_ is cleared and after each batched apply's swap).
hypotheses.verdict_text: root_apply_direct moves what it targets and is bit-identical, but it's small: root gen-bit 29.8 -> 16.4 us and root split-inner 15.2 -> 14.4 us (nsys, same binary, stable over 2 runs per arm). ncu: the root launch's L2 read sectors fell 89%. Kernel time per round dropped 19 us (-0.41%). Same-binary e2e A/B (300 rounds, 3 alternated pairs, key off in --plan-stock) gave 1.0049: stock 4.837/4.833/4.847 ms vs cand 4.813/4.812/4.821 ms, within-arm spread 0.010-0.013 ms. Quick check vs master: md5 identical, 1.2131. This is below the predicted -25..-30 us: the root gen-bit is latency x waves bound (V2/V3 show the shape matters more than the bytes once the index chain is gone). It is above the 10 us falsification threshold.

hypotheses.falsification: Same-binary nsys (key on vs off): aggregate kernel time per round falls by less than 5 us -> refuted; md5 differs -> rejected.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Loading each thread's entries into registers before any store, doing the local prefix in registers, and storing every entry once (the sync_copy_batched pattern), with a block sized to the level's largest split (64-1024 threads, at most 8 entries per thread), removes the dependent chains and most of the scan cost at deep levels: root 6.8 -> ~3 us, levels 1-3 -> ~2.5-3 us, deep levels -> ~2 us; about -10 us per round (-0.2%). Integer prefix sums of the same entries: bit-identical.
hypotheses.observation: HybridAggregateBlockOffsetBatchKernel (one block per split, on the apply chain between gen-bit and split-inner) costs 36 us per round (c066: same). Per level: 6.8 us at the root (5337 chunk entries, 1024 threads, ~5.2 entries per thread), 5.9 at level 1, 4.1, 3.8, then 2.3-3.0 at deep levels (tens of entries per split, still 1024-thread blocks and two block-wide scans). The time scales with entries per thread: the per-thread local prefix and the final offset add are global load -> add -> store chains (the left and right buffers may alias, so nothing is batched), about 1.3 us per entry per thread.
hypotheses.plan:
- include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: cuda_plan key aggregate_load_first (default on).
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu: HybridAggregateBlockOffsetLoadFirstKernel (8 entries per thread max) plus a shared __device__ leaf-metadata tail; LaunchSplitLevelBatchedKernels takes it when the largest split's entries fit 1024 x 8, otherwise the original kernel.
hypotheses.verdict_text: aggregate_load_first cuts the aggregate kernel from 36.4 to 26.3 us per round (nsys, same binary, 2 pairs per variant, stable to 0.1 us): root 7.0 -> 4.7 us, deep levels 2.6 -> 1.6 us. That beats the 5 us falsification threshold, but in e2e it can't be told apart from root_apply_direct alone (combined same-binary A/B 1.0048 vs 1.0049 for root_apply_direct by itself). The two mechanisms together are worth ~30 us of kernel time per round, about 0.5% e2e.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Running each split's aggregate inside the gen-bit kernel, in the block that finishes that split's last chunk (per-split
atomic arrival counter, threadfence-reduction pattern), removes the aggregate launch and one dependent kernel boundary
per level; the per-split prefix overlaps the other splits' gen-bit chunks, so only the last finishing split's
prefix (~1-3 us) stays exposed. Expected: apply chain -35..-50 us/round (aggregate kernel 36 us + 10 gaps - exposed
tails), ratio vs parent ~1.006-1.009 (below the 1% e2e noise: decided by same-binary nsys A/B).
hypotheses.observation:
Parent nsys (22b8573e, 60 rounds): every host-launched batched level runs gen-bit -> aggregate -> split-inner back to
back on one stream. HybridAggregateBlockOffsetBatchKernel is a separate launch of one 1024-thread block per split that
only prefix-sums the gen-bit's per-chunk left/right counts of its split and writes the children's leaf windows:
0.036 ms/round of kernel time (3.6 us avg, 2.0-7.2 us; 6.9 us at the root where one block scans 5336 chunk counts),
plus two ~1 us launch gaps per level (gen-bit -> aggregate -> split-inner), i.e. ~55 us/round (1.0%) of serial
GPU time on the level's critical path. Its input (one split's chunk counts) is complete as soon as that split's last
gen-bit chunk is done, while other splits' chunks are still running.

- include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: cuda_plan key aggregate_in_genbit (default on).
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu: the aggregate body as a __device__ function shared by the original
  kernel and the gen-bit kernel's flat path (L2 loads for counts written by other blocks); per-split arrival counter
  (reset by the last block); host launch skips the aggregate kernel when the key is on, the flow is single-GPU and
  every split has rows (a split without chunks would never reach its aggregate).
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cpp/.hpp: counter buffer, min chunks per split passed to the launcher.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Measured: V2 (defect-free) same-binary e2e 0.9971 (3 alternated pairs, spread <= 0.4%); V3 1.0029 (neutral, -3.6
us/round in nsys); V1 0.992. 1) V1's defect (dependent L2 round trips in the fused prefix) was fixed in V2 and
re-measured; V2's shallow-level contention (thousands of chunks on one arrival counter) was removed in V3 and
re-measured; no spills (gen-bit 40 regs). 2) Deciding numbers are same-binary A/Bs of aggregate_in_genbit on vs off,
3 alternated pairs each, with the spread above. 3) Mechanism: the targeted quantity moved fully (aggregate kernel
36.1 -> 0 us/round and one launch per level gone in V2), but the gen-bit kernel grew by more (346.5 -> 410.3
us/round): the per-chunk completion signal (threadfence + arrival atomic + block barrier) holds every gen-bit block
~1-2 us longer, which costs 3.6-5.5 us per deep level and 8-14 us per shallow level against the 3.3-4.5 us (kernel +
launch gap) it removes. Where the per-split chunk count is small enough for the signal to be cheap (V3), the saving
is ~1-2 us per level. 4) Three variants measured. Do not retry last-block folding of the aggregate on this GPU; a
launch of ~1 us between queued kernels is cheaper than a device-scope completion signal per chunk.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Loading the level apply's single-use streams (split-bin sectors, the partition's last read of the old index list) with evict-first priority keeps the index lists L2-resident, so the deep gen-bit (and the construct) stop re-reading them from DRAM.
nodes.falsification:

(below the run-to-run spread), or e2e same-binary A/B < 1.003.

hypotheses.falsification:

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Loading the split bins (read once per split) and the split-inner's read of the old index list (its last use) with
evict-first priority keeps the index lists L2-resident through the apply chain: the split-inner's index read and the
next level's gen-bit/construct index reads hit L2 instead of DRAM. Expected: split-inner -15..-30% at deep levels,
gen-bit -5..-15% at deep levels, about -40..-80 us/round, ratio >= 1.008 (same-binary A/B).
hypotheses.observation:
Parent profile (nsys, round 30): the level apply runs per level gen-bit (30 us root, 18.7-27.5 us levels 1-4, 35-51 us
levels 5-10; 0.349 ms/round) -> aggregate -> split-inner (17-22 us per level, 0.173 ms/round). ncu (this worker,
--cache-control none, 30 launches): the deep-level gen-bit reads 77-86 MB through L2 per launch (about 20 MB of index
list + ~60 MB of split-bin sectors of the column-major store, one sector per row) with a 2-8% L2 hit rate, and the
split-inner that follows re-reads the same 22-23 MB index list with a 1-3% hit rate. A microbenchmark on this 5090
shows the L2 does keep a 22 MB buffer across kernels (cold read 18.1 us vs warm 8.2-8.8 us), also after a 400 MB
__ldcs (evict-first) stream, i.e. reuse is lost only to normal-priority streams. The only normal-priority bulk stream
of the level loop is the gen-bit's split-bin loads (the construct's row loads are already __ldcs, the gradients sit in
the l2_policy persisting window); the 74 MB normal L2 portion cannot hold 60 MB of bins + 20 MB of indices + the
split-inner's 22 MB of written indices.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Freeing the registers the next-index prefetch holds (load the next batch's indices at the top of the next batch, with
an L1/L2 prefetch of their sector issued a batch ahead, or a smaller batch where all loads fit) lets every gradient and
row-byte load of a batch issue back to back, so a batch costs ~one DRAM latency: construct -8..-15% (0.16-0.3 ms/round),
e2e ratio vs parent >= 1.03.
hypotheses.observation:
The pair-joint construct (CUDAConstructDiscretizedHistogramPairJointCappedKernel<0,15,48>) is 2.046 ms/round = 43% of
the round, long_scoreboard 40% of stalls, DRAM at 1.24 TB/s (69.6%; the fill streams 1.49 TB/s). In its SASS the
48-register cap cannot hold the 15 gradients, 15 row bytes and 15 prefetched next-batch indices at once, so ptxas sinks
the gradient loads behind the row-byte loads and issues them in groups gated by the atomics: each 15-row batch costs a
DRAM round trip plus ~3 dependent L2 round trips.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
One thread per 32-bit word of the existing nibble row (4 bytes = 4 pair cells per thread; unaligned rows rebuilt
from two aligned word loads + funnel shift) cuts LSU warp-instructions per row from ~22 to ~11 (1.4 warps x
idx + grad + 2 loads + 4 atomics). With occupancy-chosen block heights at <=48 registers, construct time falls
25-35% (2.05 -> ~1.4 ms/round), i.e. e2e ratio >= 1.10, memory-neutral, no fill or view change.
hypotheses.observation:
The pair-joint construct is 2.045 ms/round (43% of the round). It runs one thread per byte of the 178-byte
row-interleaved nibble row, so each row costs ~5.6 warps x (index load + gradient load + byte load + shared atomic)
= ~22 LSU warp-instructions; ncu shows mio_throttle + lg_throttle = 28% of stalls, issue 37%, DRAM 69%.
kevo/c079 showed on a different (5-bit code) view that the construct is LSU-issue-bound: one thread per word cut it 37%.

  choice PairJointNibbleWordRows (occupancy API), launch at gathering whole-row levels when key on.

hypotheses.verdict_text:
One thread per word of the nibble row cuts the construct's LSU instructions in half but makes it 10-25% slower. On
this 177-byte unaligned nibble view the per-byte kernel is bound by the DRAM row gather, not by LSU issue.
1. Defects fixed and re-measured: grid underfill (the 400-rows-per-thread target gave ~4x fewer warps per level,
   171 -> 152 ms); the second word load (A6 removes it: 154.7 ms, no gain); no spills in any build (LOCAL:0).
2. Same binary, key on vs off, alternated, 2 pairs each (nsys 60 rounds): construct 152.2 / 152.3 ms on vs
   123.6 / 123.6 ms off. Same-arm spread is 0.1 ms. Steady round 5.22 / 5.23 vs 4.75 / 4.74 ms. Earlier pre-fix
   quick check vs master: 0.856, md5 identical.
3. Mechanism (ncu, real clocks): LSU instructions -51% and MIO/LSU throttle stalls gone, so the quantity moved;
   time did not fall. Refuted for this view: c079's win needs the 128-byte-aligned code rows (fewer bytes, one line
   per warp) together with fewer LSU instructions.
4. Variants: 4-byte units at batches 2/3/4/6/8, 8-byte units at batches 2/4/4@64, aligned single loads at batches
   3/4/8, the per-word bank pad, before and after the grid fix: 17 builds or configurations measured.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
The partial last wave of equal-row blocks (0.57 wave at level 1, 0.1-0.6 elsewhere) leaves SMs idle for a block
lifetime. A smaller rows-per-thread target in the pair-joint grid (more, shorter blocks: several full waves, a small
tail) cuts the first level's construct by 20-40% (~30-50 us/round). If it helps at every level, the construct falls
>= 5% (ratio >= 1.02).
hypotheses.observation:
Per-level construct times (nsys, key-off build, rounds 10-59) are 132 / 258 / 229 / 251 / 255 / 252 / 246 / 225 /
193 us. Grids at 3 resident 12-warp blocks per SM (510 per wave) are 800 / 2663 / 1838 / 2246 / ... blocks. The
single-pair first level (the root's smaller child, ~640k rows) runs 800 blocks = 1.57 waves at ~0.86 TB/s of row
bytes. The 2-pair level runs at ~1.46 TB/s, the fill's streaming rate. The grid comes from the formula's 400
rows-per-thread target (y_full_rate dominates); the saturation floor is capped at min_grid_dim_y = 160.
hypotheses.plan:
Pass a rows-per-thread target to HybridBatchedConstructGridDimY(Quant) (default 400 = NUM_DATA_PER_THREAD, every
other caller unchanged). The pair-joint launch and its in-kernel per-pair replica both use it. Sweep it with a
temporary env knob (single-pair levels / all levels); a winner would become a cuda_plan key.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
The 400 rows-per-thread target is already the optimum for the pair-joint construct; shorter or longer blocks are
slower.
1. No build defects: same registers, no spills; only the grid moved.
2. Same binary, alternated: default 125.7 / 124.8 ms vs single-level target 100 at 127.8 / 127.2 ms (2 pairs). The
   all-level targets 200 / 100 / 800 (132.5 / 171.5 / 126.9 ms) are far outside the 0.9 ms same-arm spread.
3. The mechanism quantity (blocks per level: 2x-4x more, or 2x fewer) moved; the construct did not get faster.
4. Five targets x two scopes measured.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: The per-tree hist memset is the only serial tree-start GPU work no kernel needs in full; zeroing only sampled-feature bins cuts ~0.03 ms/round.
nodes.falsification: If the timing-only build (memset removed) shows a per-round kernel-time gain below 0.5% in nsys, or the e2e A/B differs by less than the same-arm noise, the mechanism is refuted at this size.

hypotheses.falsification: If the timing-only build (memset removed) shows a per-round kernel-time gain below 0.5% in nsys, or the e2e A/B differs by less than the same-arm noise, the mechanism is refuted at this size.
hypotheses.hypothesis: The per-tree histogram zeroing (66 MB, 26.5 us/round, 0.56% of the round) is the only serial GPU work of the tree start that no kernel needs in full: zeroing only the bins of features sampled this tree (feature_fraction 0.1 -> ~10% of bins) would cut it to ~3 us, i.e. ratio about 1.005. This is a bounded, small mechanism; the expected e2e gain is below the ~1% noise.
hypotheses.observation: Parent steady round 4.73 ms: construct 2.045 ms (43%), fused fill 1.330 ms (28%, DRAM 83%), kernels 4.417 ms total; GPU-idle 0.359 ms/round (7.6%), mostly host readback round trips (CopyToMappedHost -> next kernel, 7-20 us each, ~200 us/round). Between tree-start kernels the GPU runs a 66.2 MB cudaMemset of the dirty histogram slots (26.5 us/round) right before InitValues.
hypotheses.plan: Timing-only build (not committed) that skips the memset, to measure the true upper bound; then, if worth it, a masked zeroing kernel in src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.{cpp,cu} keyed by a cuda_plan key (hist_zero_used_bins).

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: The fill's root-histogram shared atomics are a real share of its time: halving them with a joint (code-cell) histogram cuts the fill by 10-15% (~0.15 ms/round), i.e. ratio >= 1.03. Mechanism: fill is LSU-issue-limited (LSU 76%) and the root-hist atomics are the largest LSU consumer beside the staging.

hypotheses.falsification: Timing-only fill time falls by less than 3% vs baseline (same session, nsys kernel time, 60 rounds): refutes the joint root histogram as a route to >= 3%.

Mechanism: fill is LSU-issue-limited (LSU 76%) and the root-hist atomics are the largest LSU consumer beside the staging.
hypotheses.observation: Fused fill 1.258 ms/round (27.8%), code-word construct 1.273 ms/round (28.1%), GPU idle 0.92 ms/round (20%). The fill has 2 shared atomics per slot per row (356 per row, slot-major, conflict-free), and its DRAM is at 73% of peak. The operator's untried list names a joint root histogram (one atomic per slot per row on the code cell, halving the fill's atomics).
hypotheses.plan:
Timing-only build (not committed): drop the root-histogram shared atomics of the CODE5 fill (loads kept alive by a never-taken conditional), nsys fill time vs the same tree's baseline in the same session. The joint variant removes at most this cost (it halves the atomics), so its gain is bounded by this number. Only if the bound is >= 3% is a joint histogram built (smem growth needed: the joint table is ~25 cells x 178 slots = 17.8 KB vs 7.7 KB now).
Files: src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu (the root-hist loop of the fused kernel).
hypotheses.verdict_text: The root-histogram atomics can give at most ~1.5% of the round even if removed cheaply. Measured: T1 fill -10.9% for removing all of them (kernel-only, see caveat). A joint histogram can reach at most half of that. No joint variant was implemented, so the mechanism is bounded, not A/B-refuted.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Evict-first stores push the code view's tail out of L2 before the first whole-row construct reads it. With plain stores, the L2 (96 MB) keeps the last written rows (tens of MB of the 700 MB view), so the first level's construct reads them from L2 instead of DRAM. Expected effect: ~20-50 us/round (0.5-1.1% of the round), i.e. ratio 1.005-1.011. Not a 2.5% effect; the combine is what this step buys.
nodes.falsification: Same-binary A/B, alternated, >=2 pairs (nsys kernel time of the fill + first-level construct, or e2e with the key off): if the sum does not fall by at least the noise (spread between same-arm runs, ~0.5%), refuted for this mechanism. Also ncu L2 hit rate on the first level's construct must move; if it does not, the implementation did not engage it.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Accumulating the root histogram in a joint [cell][slot] table (cell = lo * span(hi) + hi, the value the code pack
already computes per byte) instead of two marginal tables halves the shared atomics per row (354 -> 178) and the
root-histogram shared byte loads stay; the marginals are produced at the block flush (each joint cell adds to its low
and high local bins: same integer sums, bit-identical). Expected: the shared pipe drops from 77% to ~60% of peak so
DRAM becomes the limiter again at ~83-85% as in the nibble fill: fill 1193 -> ~1050-1100 us (-100..-150 us/round),
round -2..-3%, e2e ratio vs parent >= 1.02.
Cost: the joint table (up to 32 cells x 192-cell stride x 4 B = 24.6 KB) replaces the 9.2 KB marginal table; to keep
2 blocks per SM (102.4 KB) the CODE5 instantiation drops its unused destination tables and flush bins (2.8 KB), the
launch opts into > 48 KB dynamic shared memory and takes the joint table only where the occupancy API gives it at
least as many resident blocks as the marginal variant.
hypotheses.observation:
The fused code-view fill is 1.213 ms/round (26.5% of the round). Its top unit is the shared/L1 pipe (Mem Pipes Busy
77%, L1/TEX throughput 77.6%) above DRAM (74%, 1.3 TB/s); issue slots busy 69%. Per staged row it issues 354 shared
atomics (two per byte slot: low column bin, high column bin) plus 178 byte loads for the root histogram, against
178 staging byte stores and ~60 word loads for the code pack. The nibble -> code view change cut the fill's DRAM
bytes 14% (1.96 -> 1.69 GB) but its time only 10%: the fill is no longer purely DRAM-bound.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: The per-block flush (and zeroing) of the code-word construct is >= 5% of its time (>= 1.4% of the round); a cheaper flush (fewer global atomics per block, or fewer blocks per pair at the deep levels) would recover most of it.
nodes.falsification: Construct time with 1/6 of the flush within 3% of the full flush (per level, comparable grids) refutes the flush as a lever; the zeroing is at most 19 stores per thread and is not measured separately.

hypotheses.falsification: Same-binary A/B (key on vs off, nsys construct time per 60 rounds, 2 alternated pairs): construct not at least 4% lower with the key on (noise ~1-2%) refutes it; mechanism check: nsys level-1..4 construct launches show more blocks and shorter time; ncu achieved occupancy / DRAM% up on a level-2 launch.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Deriving the whole-row construct's grid floors from the device's resident block count for the launched shape (SMs x occupancy-API blocks per SM) instead of the 160-block constants doubles the warps in flight at the shallow levels; the gather there runs at the deep levels' ~1.6 TB/s: construct -80..-120 us/round, ratio vs parent >= 1.02 (same-binary key on vs off), quick check vs master >= 1.21.
hypotheses.observation: The code-word pair-joint construct (1.273 ms/round, 28%) launches 160-273 blocks of 20 warps at levels 1-4 (586 us/round) on a device that holds 340 such blocks (2 per SM x 170 SMs, occupancy API). Its grid floor constants (min_grid_dim_y_ = 160 per pair, saturation floor 160 per level) date from 32-warp blocks. Level 1 is a single pair and is capped at 160 blocks = 1 block per SM (47% of resident warps); level 5 with 360 blocks runs the same gather at ~1.6 TB/s against ~1.0-1.3 TB/s at levels 1-4. ncu: DRAM 65%, long_scoreboard 43%: a latency-bound gather whose bandwidth follows the warps in flight.
hypotheses.plan:
- include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: key pair_grid_resident (default on).
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu: for the code-word (and capped whole-row) pair-joint launch, min grid per pair and the level saturation floor := max(current, resident blocks of the launched shape); the same values go to the pair_block_map host prefix and to the kernel's per-pair row-grouping replica (already kernel arguments), so host and device agree on every block's rows. Integer atomics: bit-identical.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
1. No defect in the build: the kernel code is unchanged (48 registers, same binary as the parent's kernel); only the host grid floors changed, and the nsys grids confirm they engaged exactly as designed (L1 162 -> 340 blocks, L2 231 -> 332, deep levels 236-326 -> 308-412).
2. Deciding number: same-binary A/B, key on vs off, 2 alternated pairs of 60-round nsys captures: construct 1374.6/1376.6 us/round ON vs 1268.2/1268.6 OFF (+8.4%, noise 0.15%); quick check vs master 1.182 (md5 identical) against the parent's 1.194.
3. Mechanism check: the quantity the hypothesis moves (blocks / warps in flight per level) moved at every level; time fell only at L1 (88 -> 80 us: 99 MB gathered at 1.13 -> 1.24 TB/s) and rose 5-17% at L2-L9. The gather sits at the random-row DRAM-efficiency ceiling (1.1-1.3 TB/s at every level), not at a warps-in-flight limit; extra blocks add per-block fixed cost and, past the resident count, a tail wave. The mechanism is refuted.
4. Variants: the two floors raised together (A1, measured). Not measured: raising only the per-pair cap (L1-only effect, bounded by L1's -8 us = 0.2% of the round, under noise); a "fill only if the level leaves half the device idle" rule (same bound). Why iteration cannot help: L1 is the only under-filled level and its whole gain is 8 us/round (0.2%); every other level loses with more blocks.

Do not retry: more construct blocks / warps in flight at levels >= 2 (DRAM-efficiency-bound gather). The key stays in the tree defaulting OFF only if committed; nothing is committed from H1.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Writing the readback data into the mapped pinned staging from inside the producing kernels (the same bytes the copy
kernel would copy) and waiting with one device-wide synchronize removes the copy kernel and its cross-stream wait from
both per-level round trips: the host wakes ~2.5 us earlier per readback, ~50 us/round, i.e. round time -1.0% (nsys
GPU-timeline round 4.73 -> ~4.68 ms), e2e ratio ~1.01.
hypotheses.observation:
Each of the 10 levels of a numerai53bench-deep-stoch tree reads back twice: the level's best splits (written by
SyncBestSplitForLevelUsedTasksKernel on the find stream) and the split batch info (18 ints per split, written by the
split-inner/tree-structure kernel on the partition stream). Each readback is a CopyToMappedHostKernel on the legacy
default stream followed by cudaStreamSynchronize(0). In the parent nsys trace the copy kernel starts 1.5 us
(SyncBest) / 1.8 us (split-inner) after its producer ends (legacy-stream implicit wait on another stream) and runs
1.1-1.6 us: ~2.8 us x 20 = ~56 us/round of GPU idle on the serial chain, before the host even wakes (0.84 us).
hypotheses.plan:
New cuda_plan key `readback_fused` (include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h). cuda_best_split_finder.cu: SyncBestSplitForLevelUsedTasksKernel
mirrors each leaf entry it writes (whole struct, after a block barrier) into the mapped best-split staging;
SyncAllLeafBestSplitsToHost then device-syncs and reads the staging. cuda_data_partition.cu: the split tree-structure
body mirrors its 18 ints into the mapped split-info staging; FinishSplitBatch device-syncs and reads it. Engaged only
in the classic hybrid level loop (every entry of the tree's leaves is written by a mirrored SyncBest), single GPU, no
feature-parallel, scalar leaves, no compact prefill (non-blocking side stream).
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Writing the two per-level readbacks into their mapped staging from the producing kernels removes the copy kernel and
its cross-stream wait from both host round trips of every level: ~3.1 us per readback (median producer end -> next
upload 9.8 -> 6.7 us and 8.7 -> 5.6 us), -54..-64 us per round on the nsys GPU timeline (3 alternated same-binary
pairs, same-arm spread 11-13 us), same-binary e2e 1.0076-1.0081 (6- and 3-pair A/B; paired saving 1.11%, CI95
0.38-1.85%), quick check vs master 1.0095 (V1) / 1.0104 (V2), md5 identical everywhere. Predicted ~50 us/round and
~1.01: met. Variants measured: V1 (kept), V2 (changed-entries host read: no gain, dropped); V3/V4 bounded, not built.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Accumulating the fused fill's root histogram as a joint [cell][slot] table (cell = lo * span(hi) + hi, one shared atomic per byte slot per row, flushed as the construct's marginal sums) instead of two nibble cells per slot halves the fill's shared atomics (356 -> 178 per row) and cuts its MIO operations ~25%; the fill is partly MIO-issue bound (40% MIO stalls at 62.5% issue), so the fill drops 4-8% (45-90 us/round): quick-check ratio vs parent ~1.012-1.024 (vs master >= 1.235, parent 1.224). Variant A2 (atomics issued inside the pack2 loop from the codes it already holds, deleting the histogram loop's 178 byte loads per row) can reach the c083 bound (~-10% fill, ratio vs parent ~1.03). Same rows, same packed gradient added once per slot per row, integer wrapping sums: the marginal sum of a slot's cells equals the nibble cell's sum bit for bit.
hypotheses.observation: The fused fill CUDAFillCompactData4BitTiledRootHistKernel<1,1> takes 1.121 ms/round (29.4% of the 3.812 ms round; 1142 us per launch, one per tree). ncu: DRAM 79.5% (970 MB column-major read + 700 MB code view written per tree ~ 1.4 TB/s), issue slots 62.5% busy, stalls short_scoreboard 24% + mio_throttle 16% (shared-memory pipe), occupancy 2 blocks/SM (shared-memory limited). Per row of 178 byte slots the slot-major root-histogram loop (one warp per row, lane per slot, cuda_histogram_constructor.cu:945-975) issues 178 shared byte loads and 356 shared atomics (one per nibble: low column cell and high column cell of every byte slot), about 70% of the row's MIO operations. c083 bounded the atomics at -10.9% of the fill (all removed, timing-only). The construct already accumulates the same pair cells as a joint table (lo * span(hi) + hi) and flushes marginals, and the fill's code pack already computes that joint cell per byte.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Sizing each code-word launch from the device's resident-block capacity (occupancy API x SM count) instead of the
constants -- rows per thread chosen as the smallest that keeps the level's blocks (pair_block_map count) within the
whole waves the default sizing needs, so an under-filled wave is filled with shorter blocks and no level runs one block
per SM -- raises resident warps / DRAM throughput on the under-filled levels: construct -5..-12% (-60..-150 us/round),
i.e. ratio vs parent >= 1.02 (quick check vs master >= 1.24).
hypotheses.observation:
The code-word construct is 1.266 ms/round (33% of the round). Its per-level launches are sized by constants tuned for the
per-byte kernel (400 rows/thread target, a 160-block saturation floor/cap): with 20-row x 32-word blocks at 2 blocks/SM
(340 resident on 170 SMs) the levels launch 160-338 blocks (0.47-0.99 waves: 1 block on many SMs, ~20 of 48 warps) or
360-381 blocks (1.06-1.12 waves: a 20-41 block tail wave). ncu: 287 blocks -> 68% achieved occupancy, DRAM 77%;
381 blocks -> DRAM 59%, 241 us.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: H1: conflict-free shared atomics shorten the per-batch atomic phase and raise DRAM utilization (construct -12..-20%); H2: more rows in flight per SM (rows per warp, warps per SM) raise the latency-bound gather's DRAM utilization from ~71% to 85-90%.
nodes.falsification: cuobjdump: > 48 registers or spills = defect (then 5 rows). Same-binary e2e A/B key on vs off, 2 alternated pairs: below 1.02 refutes the quantified effect; ncu DRAM% on vs off: unchanged with time unchanged = mechanism refuted (bytes in flight are not the limit); DRAM% up without time down = impossible here (same bytes).

hypotheses.falsification: Same-binary A/B (key on vs off, nsys 60 rounds, 2 alternated pairs): construct kernel time per round not lower by at least 5% refutes the quantified effect; ncu on vs off: l1tex LSU wavefronts per launch not falling by >= 40% means the layout did not engage (defect); fallen but time unchanged (DRAM% unchanged) means the atomic phase was not on the critical path: mechanism refuted.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Mechanism: a lane-major joint-table layout for the code-word construct (cell c of lane k's table j at (local_off(k, j) + c) * blockDim.x + k, blockDim.x a multiple of the warp size, so every lane of an atomic instruction addresses its own bank) makes each of the six shared atomics per row one wavefront instead of ~3.5. The atomic phase between batches shrinks ~3x, the LSU data pipe drops from ~64% to ~25-30% busy, loads of the next batch issue sooner, so more code-row bytes are in flight per SM and DRAM utilization rises from 78% towards 88-92%. Expected: construct -12..-20% (1.264 -> 1.02-1.11 ms/round), i.e. round -4..-6%, quick-check ratio vs the parent 1.04-1.06 (vs master >= 1.27). Same cells, same packed-gradient integer adds, same marginal sums: bit-identical.
hypotheses.observation: The code-word construct is 1.264 ms/round (33% of 3.796 ms). ncu (parent profile): DRAM 78% (launch 0) / 59% (launch 1), L1 LSU data-pipe wavefronts 64% / 47%, issue 55% / 41%, long_scoreboard 5-7 cycles per issued instruction, short_scoreboard 1.8-1.9, wait 2.5. Each row costs a warp one 128-B coalesced load and six shared atomics into byte-major joint tables (byte b's 25 cells at offset 25b): lane k's atomic for slot j hits bank (22k + 25j + code) mod 32, a random scatter of 32 lanes over 32 banks, ~3.5 wavefronts per atomic instruction, ~21 shared wavefronts per row per warp. Per warp a 4-row batch completes every ~5000 cycles, 2-3x a loaded DRAM latency: the serialized atomic phase (24 atomics x ~3.5 wavefronts x ~33 warps per SM through one shared pipe) is comparable to the DRAM latency and delays the next batch's loads.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The construct's ~24 us/level intercept is mostly synchronized non-streaming phases (prologue before the first gather, epilogue marginals + flush, launch stagger), not DRAM. Issuing the first batch's loads before the prologue's zeroing/sync (load-first), parallelizing the epilogue over all 1024 threads (one (slot, marginal) item per thread instead of 6 serial slots over ~12 of 32 y-threads) and de-synchronizing the flush (per-block rotation of the item order so simultaneous blocks hit different addresses/slices) cut the intercept from ~24 to ~14-16 us/level: construct -70..-90 us/round (-7..-8% on the c095 build), ratio 1.02-1.025 over the c095 port, i.e. >= 1.08 vs master in total (c095 port alone 1.06).
hypotheses.observation: Master's code-word construct is 1.268 ms/round (33.5% of 3.788 ms). c095 (not in master, branch kevo/c098 = master's ancestor + 2 commits, clean merge) cut it to 1.089 ms/round (e2e 1.063, md5 identical). On that build the per-level time fits 24 us + 71 ns per 1000 rows (L1-L6): the marginal row streams at DRAM peak (1.80 TB/s), so ~215 us/round (9 levels x 24 us, 5.7% of the round, 20% of the construct) is row-independent per-launch cost. Its known parts: block tail ~3% (ncu sm__cycles_active avg/max 0.969, ~6 us/level); the epilogue's synchronized flush (all 170 blocks finish together, each fires ~2160 64-bit REDs; L2 atomic unit max slice 2.5% of elapsed = ~5 us/level; c095's no-flush build bounds it at 1.2-1.6% of the round); the prologue (table zeroing + metadata loops before the first load is issued) and the launch stagger of 170 1024-thread blocks (not yet measured; c098's instrumentation exists for exactly this, never run). During prologue and epilogue the SM's DRAM stream is idle, and because every block has equal rows these phases are level-wide synchronized, so they add to the makespan instead of overlapping.
hypotheses.plan:
1. Port c095 first (its own measured 1.06 is the floor of this candidate): `git merge kevo/c098` (commits 0c0eefb9 pair_code5_slots, 6c70ce2b pair_code5_tall; touches only include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h and src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu; merge-tree reports no conflict). Build, install, quick check: expect md5 identical and ~1.06 (c095 got 1.063 same-binary; its quick check vs the master of its night was higher). Commit.
2. Measure the intercept's split once (throwaway build, NOT committed): apply c098's uncommitted diff (`git -C ../c098 diff > [local location omitted]`, `git apply`), build, run under gpu_run.sh `FALCATA_C5DBG=[local location omitted] ... workloads.py numerai53bench-deep-stoch --rounds 60` (the dump happens at code-word launch 360 = ~round 40; file columns t0 t1 t2 t3 rows smid blockIdx.y, ns). Group rows into launches by t0 gaps > 20 us; per launch report: spread of t0 (launch stagger), median t1-t0 (prologue), max(t2)-median(t2) (tail), median t3-t2 and max(t3)-max(t2) (epilogue incl. flush), max(t3)-min(t0) vs nsys duration. nodes.hypothesis: The construct's ~24 us/level intercept is mostly synchronized non-streaming phases (prologue before the first gather, epilogue marginals + flush, launch stagger), not DRAM. Issuing the first batch's loads before the prologue's zeroing/sync (load-first), parallelizing the epilogue over all 1024 threads (one (slot, marginal) item per thread instead of 6 serial slots over ~12 of 32 y-threads) and de-synchronizing the flush (per-block rotation of the item order so simultaneous blocks hit different addresses/slices) cut the intercept from ~24 to ~14-16 us/level: construct -70..-90 us/round (-7..-8% on the c095 build), ratio 1.02-1.025 over the c095 port, i.e. >= 1.08 vs master in total (c095 port alone 1.06).
nodes.observation: Master's code-word construct is 1.268 ms/round (33.5% of 3.788 ms). c095 (not in master, branch kevo/c098 = master's ancestor + 2 commits, clean merge) cut it to 1.089 ms/round (e2e 1.063, md5 identical). On that build the per-level time fits 24 us + 71 ns per 1000 rows (L1-L6): the marginal row streams at DRAM peak (1.80 TB/s), so ~215 us/round (9 levels x 24 us, 5.7% of the round, 20% of the construct) is row-independent per-launch cost. Its known parts: block tail ~3% (ncu sm__cycles_active avg/max 0.969, ~6 us/level); the epilogue's synchronized flush (all 170 blocks finish together, each fires ~2160 64-bit REDs; L2 atomic unit max slice 2.5% of elapsed = ~5 us/level; c095's no-flush build bounds it at 1.2-1.6% of the round); the prologue (table zeroing + metadata loops before the first load is issued) and the launch stagger of 170 1024-thread blocks (not yet measured; c098's instrumentation exists for exactly this, never run). During prologue and epilogue the SM's DRAM stream is idle, and because every block has equal rows these phases are level-wide synchronized, so they add to the makespan instead of overlapping.

hypotheses.hypothesis:

hypotheses.observation:
The column-major store (colmajor_bin_, built by colmajor_direct's EnterCompactRegime) is 9,184 MiB of the 11,348
MiB VRAM peak (packing_density.md section 6). It is nibble-packed (4 bits/value) although every column of this
workload has bin span <= 6 (3,465 columns hold values 0-4, 60 hold 0-5, the NaN bin). The fused
root-hist fill (CUDAFillCompactData4BitTiledRootHistKernel) that reads it is 1.110 ms/round = 29.3% of the 3.788 ms
round, DRAM 79.5% busy (parent profile). The codebase already has a lossless, compile-time-proven base-6 codec
(PackRadix6x32 in include/Falcata/cuda/pack_codecs.hpp: 12 digits/word via magic-division, 2.667 bits/value) used
today only for the per-tree compact view (pack_radix6 plan key, off by default, not on the hot kernel's path).

hypotheses.observation:
The code-word pair-joint construct (1.268 ms/round, 33.5%) and the code-view fused fill (1.110 ms/round, 29.3%) are
the two biggest kernels and both exist only behind the gate `lo_span * hi_span <= 32` with a hard-coded 5-bit code
(six codes per word, mask 31, `Code5RowWords = ceil(slots / 6)` rounded to 8 words). The fitness dataset passes it on
every pair (bins 5 on all used columns, product 25). The numerai v5.3 NaN datasets (round-1230 binary behind the
guard `numerai53-example-stoch` and the `numerai53-deep-*` workloads) have 6 bins on 1,972 of 3,555 columns, so a
tree holds ~55 six-by-six pairs (product 36 > 32) and NEVER takes the code view: every level runs the nibble-view
capped construct (217 us/launch vs 144 us code-word in the parent profile) and the nibble fill (1,324 us vs 1,132 us).
The parent profile itself shows that slow path once (tree 44 of 60: +850 us, +22% of a round for that tree).

hypotheses.hypothesis:
The construct's remaining slack is per-launch fixed cost, not gather bandwidth (bytes per row are at the 4-sector
floor; DRAM 79-85% after the slot grid). (1) One wave of the tallest blocks removes the partial-wave and per-block
zero/flush cost: construct -10% (1.20 -> ~1.08 ms/round), round -3.5%, quick check vs master >= 1.05. (2) Flattening
the epilogue so every (slot, marginal) item is one thread's work (1920 items over 1024 threads: ~2 per thread, all
warps busy, one partition walk per item instead of six per lane) cuts the epilogue from ~7-8 us to ~2-3 us per launch:
-40..-50 us/round, construct another -4%, round -1.2%. Together: construct ~1.03-1.05 ms/round, quick check >= 1.06.
hypotheses.observation:
The code-word pair-joint construct is 1.202 ms/round, 32.1% of the 3.743 ms round (8.85 launches, 136.5 us each;
40 registers, 32x24 blocks, 2 per SM = 340 slots, generic grid of 160-381 blocks: 0.5-0.9 waves, DRAM 64-78%).
Two measured pieces of its per-launch fixed cost are not in this tree:
1. The grid shape. c102 composed this flat kernel with c095's slot-sized grid of tallest blocks (one 1024-thread
   block per SM, every level exactly 170 blocks): same binary, construct 1250 -> 1121 us/round (-10.3%), round -3.5%,
   DRAM 79-85%, quick check vs master 1.0589, md5 identical, lattice 224/224. Never evaluated: the driver hung.
   Its commit 2ec9ee10 applies cleanly here (`git apply --check` ok).
2. The epilogue. c101's globaltimer split on the slot-grid build: per launch the flush (marginal sums over the joint
   tables + one global atomic per marginal) takes 6.5-8.5 us median and 4.9-7.8 us more for the last block, the
   largest piece of a ~14-24 us per-level intercept; all 170 blocks reach it together, so it adds to the makespan.
   The flush loop runs 6 serial slot passes per lane, and in each pass only lo_span + hi_span (10 of 32) y-threads
   have a marginal to sum; every pass re-walks the partition table from global memory. c101 wrote the flat form
   (44 registers, no spill) but never ran it.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Loading the gen-bit's split-column bytes evict-first keeps the compact view's resident tail (and the gradient/index working sets) in L2 for the following constructs.
nodes.falsification: Same-binary nsys A/B, 60 rounds, key off vs on: construct ms/round not lower by >= 1.5% (the 60-round same-arm spread) refutes it; ncu hit rate at launches 2-5 not up by >= 3 points: the mechanism did not engage.

hypotheses.falsification: Same-binary nsys A/B (key on vs off, 60 rounds, alternated, >= 2 pairs): construct ms/round not lower by >= 3% with the L2 hit rate (ncu lts__t_sector_hit_rate on the construct) not up by >= 5 points refutes variant 1; if the hit rate moves but time does not, the mechanism is refuted. Quick check (e2e, tuner on, rounds 150-300) below 1.01 after the best variant: refuted at the e2e level.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Mechanism: cross-level L2 reuse of gathered code rows. Loading the code words at normal L2 priority (plain `__ldg`) instead of evict-first keeps the most recently gathered rows resident across the level boundary, so the next level's construct hits L2 for a fraction of its rows (bound: ~50% of rows have a constructed parent x ~40-60% still resident = 20-30% of the gather bytes; competing traffic lowers it). Expected: L2 hit rate of the construct up by >= 10 points, construct time -5..-10%, round -1.7..-3.4%, i.e. ratio 1.02-1.03 if the gradient/index hits are not lost in exchange. Risk: the rows now compete with the 22 MB gradient array, whose gathers hit L2 today; a net loss there refutes the plain-load variant and motivates an evict_last policy for the gradients (variant 2).
hypotheses.observation: The code-word construct is 1.268 ms/round (33.5%), DRAM-bound on random 128-B row gathers (ncu DRAM 68.5%, L2 hit 24-28%). Its row loads are `__ldcs` (evict-first), so a level's gathered rows leave L2 at once. At level L+1 the smaller child of a pair whose parent was itself the constructed (smaller) child at level L re-gathers a subset of exactly those rows: about half of the level's gathered bytes are rows that were gathered one level earlier. Between the two constructs the gen-bit, partition and find stream ~90 MB (deep levels) through the L2; the device L2 is tens of MB, a deep level's gather ~150 MB.
hypotheses.plan:
- `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h`: key `pair_code5_keep_rows` (bool, default on where measured positive).
- `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu`: a template bool on `ConstructDiscretizedHistogramPairJointCode5WordInner` / `CUDAConstructDiscretizedHistogramPairJointCode5WordKernel` choosing `__ldg` vs `__ldcs` for the code-word loads; the host picks the instantiation by the key. Same rows, same integer sums: bit-identical.
- Variants: (1) plain loads for the rows; (2) rows plain + gradient loads with an L2 evict_last policy (sm_80+ createpolicy with a plain fallback); (3) level-consistent gather order (block = band of data indices, alternating direction per level) so the rows gathered last at level L are gathered first at L+1.
hypotheses.verdict_text: Same-binary nsys A/B (60 rounds, key off vs on): construct +5.9%, gen-bit +16.5%, round +3.3%; ncu shows the construct's L2 hit rate unchanged (within 0.2 points at every launch), so the cross-level row reuse never engaged, and the competing rows cost the small working sets' hits. Each of the four conditions: (1) no defect in the build (48 registers, 0 stack, same shape; the kernel's own sector counts equal); (2) same-binary A/B, 1 pair of 60 rounds plus the per-launch ncu pairs, the difference (3.3%) far outside the ~1% spread of same-arm 60-round runs; (3) mechanism quantity (next-level L2 row hits) did not move while time moved the wrong way; (4) one variant measured, the other two bounded above.

hypotheses.falsification: Same-binary nsys A/B, 60 rounds, key off vs on: construct ms/round not lower by >= 1.5% (the 60-round same-arm spread) refutes it; ncu hit rate at launches 2-5 not up by >= 3 points: the mechanism did not engage.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Loading the gen-bit's split-column bytes at evict-first priority (`__ldcs` in HybridLoadBin) keeps the fill's resident tail alive for more levels, so the level 2-5 constructs hit L2 for up to 14% of their rows instead of a decaying share: construct -20..-40 us/round (levels 2-5 gather ~5.5M rows; 14% of their 128-B rows = ~100 MB/round at most, half of it already hit), i.e. ratio ~1.005-1.01 (below the quick check's noise; the nsys construct time and the ncu hit rate at launches 2-5 are the deciding numbers). This is c071's apply_evict_first with a new argument (c071 argued gradient protection and measured e2e-neutral, consistent with a ~1% effect).
hypotheses.observation: The ncu launches above show the construct's L2 hit rate at 18-19% for the first three launches of a round (levels 1-3) and 8-11% deeper. The extra hits at levels 1-3 are the fill's resident tail (pair_code5_l2_store: the last ~96 MB of the 700 MB code view, 14% of the rows): the level-1 launch hits 1.06M sectors, i.e. the smaller child's share of the resident rows, and levels 2-3 still hit part of it. The tail erodes level by level under the plain-priority streams between constructs: the gen-bit's split-column sectors (2.7 MB per split column, ~2.3M sectors = 74 MB at deep levels) and the partition's index traffic.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Balancing rows across the code-word construct's one-block-per-SM wave (per-pair block counts and rows per thread) removes the 10-20% per-SM idle time and shortens each launch by about 10%.
nodes.falsification:
Host-side timers (steady_clock around each section, printed at exit) must show the targeted sections at >= 2 us/level
before the change and < 1 us after; same-binary A/B at 300 rounds cannot resolve 1%: the deciding number is the
30k-round score or a 6-pair nsys idle measurement (GPU idle us/round from the trace union, as computed above).

hypotheses.falsification:
- Mechanism: ncu on the new build, key on vs off: sm__cycles_active.avg / sm__cycles_elapsed.avg must rise from ~0.80
  towards >= 0.90 and min/max spread shrink. Not moving: the host allocation did not engage (defect). Moving without

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Allocating the 170 slots to the level's pairs so that every block carries about the same number of rows (each pair
gets b_p blocks, rows per thread R_p = max(ceil(n_p / (32 b_p)), min knob), the greedy that always gives the next
block to the pair with the largest R_p, which is optimal for the min-max objective) removes most of the per-SM idle
time: makespan from ~454K cycles to ~avg + ramp ~410K, construct -8..-10% (1.10 -> ~1.00 ms/round), round -3%,
same-binary key on vs off >= 1.02, quick check vs master >= 1.09. Same rows per pair, other block grouping, integer
sums in the same tables: bit-identical.
hypotheses.observation:
The code-word construct is 1.101 ms/round (30.6%), 8.85 launches of one 170-block wave each (one 32-warp block per
SM). ncu on this kernel (c104's capture, launches 201-202): sm__cycles_active min 96K / avg 365K / max 411K of 454K
elapsed; the second launch 57K / 405K / 444K of 498K. The level's pairs share ONE rows-per-thread R
(pair_code5_slots), so a pair of n rows takes ceil(n / (32 R)) blocks and its last block holds n mod 32R rows: at
deep levels (1-2 blocks per pair) most blocks are partial, the launch waits for the fullest block, and ~20% of all
SM time per launch is idle (ncu's own imbalance estimate: 8.9% of the launch). DRAM runs at 80-83% averaged over the
elapsed time, i.e. near the ceiling while the SMs are busy.
hypotheses.plan:
- include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: key `pair_code5_balance` (default on; composed with pair_code5_slots and pair_block_map).
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu: PairJointBlockPrefix gets `per_pair_grid` (0: the level grid;
  1: each pair's grid y is its own block count start[p+1]-start[p]); PairJointBatchedBody takes the pair's grid from
  the prefix in that mode (dim_y = b_p * blockDim.y, so the inner's num_data_per_thread = max(ceil(n_p / dim_y),
  min_rows) is R_p). Host (the pair_code5_slots branch of the level launch): when num_pairs > 1 and the key is on,
  the greedy allocation over the host copy of the smaller-leaf counts, each pair at least ceil(n_p / (32 max_rows))
  blocks (packed-cell cap), prefix from the blocks actually used (ceil(n_p / (32 R_p)), which the kernel's formula
  reproduces exactly), launch grid y = total, pair_min_rows_per_thread = the knob.
- Variants: V1 greedy min-max as above. V2 if the tail shows: cap b_p so no pair exceeds the slots a leaf needs for
  its own rows at the knob (fewer blocks for tiny leaves). V3: the same balance applied to the level's single-pair
  launch (L1) is already balanced (one leaf, uniform R); nothing to do there.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Mechanism engaged (min block lifetime 3x, ncu, key on vs off, same binary) with no change in launch time (nsys/ncu
per-launch elapsed within 1-2%, e2e same-binary 0.991 over 2 alternated pairs, md5 identical). Defect-free build (40
registers, no spill, grid as designed). Variants beyond the greedy allocation are bounded by the 6-13% remaining SM
idle, which the DRAM-bound gather makes free; not iterated further.

The host compute on the two round trips (84 us/round, 2.3%) and the pageable memcpyAsync API cost (35 us/round) are

search over the pair counts, the 2 KB block map). Expected: 40-60 us/round, ratio 1.01-1.015 (below the quick check's
noise; visible at 30k rounds).

The round has 311 us/round of GPU idle (8.8%; nsys parent trace, union of busy intervals over rounds 7-59). Per level

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Giving every code-word construct block the same row count across pairs removes the per-pair partial-tail blocks of the one-wave grid and recovers 20-40% of the deep launches if their tail is bound by the per-SM gather rate.
nodes.falsification: Same-binary nsys A/B (pair_code5_balance on vs off, 60 rounds, alternated, 2 pairs): construct ms/round not lower by >= 3% refutes it, provided ncu shows the deep launches' DRAM throughput rising (mechanism check); DRAM% already >= 80% at the deep launches with the key off means the tail is DRAM-bound and the mechanism is refuted.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Giving every block the same number of rows of the level's concatenated (pair, rows) sequence, letting a block straddle pairs (flush, re-zero, continue), removes the per-pair rounding: the fullest block shrinks from 32R ~ N/(170 - P/2) to ceil(N/170) rows. If the tail of a level is bound by the per-SM gather rate (fewer active SMs than the DRAM needs), the deep launches lose 20-40% of their time: construct -80..-130 us/round, round -2..-3.5%, quick check vs parent >= 1.02 (vs master >= 1.09). If the level is DRAM-bound to its end regardless of how many SMs are active, the mechanism does nothing (refuted by the mechanism check).
hypotheses.observation: The code-word construct (30.6% of the round) launches one wave of exactly 170 tall blocks per level (trace: GrdY 170 at all 9 launches of every steady round). The slot sizing picks one R for the level, the smallest with sum_i ceil(n_i / (32 R)) <= slots, so each pair's last block is partial; with P pairs the rounding wastes about P/2 blocks of capacity, and the level's time is the time of a full 32R-row block while the SMs of the partial blocks idle (one block per SM, no next wave). Deep launches (P = 32..170 pairs) take 102-137 us each, 5 of the 9 launches.
hypotheses.plan:
- include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: key pair_code5_balance (default on).
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu: PairJointBlockPrefix gets a balanced mode (start[b] = first pair of block b, grid_y = rows per block c); the host computes c = clamp(ceil(N / slots), 1, block_rows x max_rows_per_thread) over the valid pairs' counts and B = ceil(N / c) blocks; PairJointBatchedBody's WORDS path, in balanced mode, finds its first pair's row prefix (warp sum of the valid pairs before it), then loops over the pairs its row range covers, calling the code-word inner with an explicit (start, count) segment and a __syncthreads between the flush and the next zeroing. Same rows into the same pair tables and the same integer atomics into the same bins: bit-identical.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
1. Defects: the 56-register merge of both paths was fixed (separate instantiation, per-pair kernel back at 40 registers, balanced one at 48 with no stack) before measuring; V2 removed the one suspected per-block overhead with no change.
2. Deciding number: same-binary nsys A/B, alternated, 2 pairs: construct 1.213/1.213 (on) vs 1.103/1.101 (off) ms/round, spread within an arm 0.002 ms; the key on loses 10% of the construct (~3% of the round). Quick checks vs master: 1.036 with the key on, 1.077 and 1.089 without it.
3. Mechanism: ncu at the deep launches: DRAM 76.8/74.9% (off) -> 72.0/70.8% (on): the quantity the hypothesis said would rise fell; the per-pair tail was not DRAM-idle.
4. Two variants measured plus the numeric bound above (<= 0.8-1.7% for any variant of this mechanism).
Not committed (slower). Patch kept at [local artifact omitted]

Letting one block construct several leaf segments in turn (each segment zeroes its joint tables, gathers its rows,
flushes into its own leaf's histogram) lets the host pack the level into the device's slots with a near-ideal
largest block: chunks of at most L rows per leaf, remainders first-fit decreasing, L the smallest that fits the
slots. Summed largest-block rows over the levels fall 6.9% (levels 7-9: -10..-24%). With ~300-500 rows of extra
block time per extra segment, construct -4..-6% (-45..-65 us/round), round -1.2..-1.8%: same-binary e2e (key off
vs on) >= 1.01, quick check vs master >= 1.06.
hypotheses.observation:
The code-word construct is 1.101 ms/round (30.3% of 3.635 ms), 8.85 launches of one wave of 169-170 tall blocks
(one 32x32 block per SM). Measured on this build's own trees (600-round training, trees 150/299/450/599): the
slot grid's row efficiency (level rows / (170 x largest block's rows)) is 0.97-1.00 at levels 1-4 but 0.92-0.93 at
level 6, 0.87-0.92 at level 7, 0.82-0.86 at level 8 and 0.75-0.85 at level 9 (41-63 smaller leaves of 10k-240k rows).

   rows), so while small-leaf blocks finish early the remaining blocks get their bandwidth; the row-imbalance

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Each partition block is a dependent latency chain (descriptor binary search, descriptor, block offsets, bit words and
indices from L2, serial warp scan, stores) with one 1024-row chunk per block; with 32 resident warps per SM the kernel
is latency-bound. A register-capped build of the same kernel (40 registers, `__maxnreg__`, taken only where the
occupancy API gives it strictly more resident blocks than the default build) fits 6 blocks = 48 warps per SM, 1.5x the
chains in flight -> split-inner -20..-30% (-35..-50 us/round), round -1..-1.4%; quick check ratio vs master >= parent's
+1%. Same code, other register allocation: bit-identical.
hypotheses.observation:
Parent profile (nsys 60 rounds): `HybridSplitInnerFusedBatchKernel<4,0,1>` 0.172 ms/round (4.7% of the 3.635 ms round),
17.1-21.2 us at EVERY level (5.3k blocks of 256 threads, 4 rows each), whatever the depth: it moves ~5.4M row indices
that are L2-resident (just read by the gen-bit), i.e. ~2.3 TB/s of L2-level traffic, not DRAM-bound. Its sibling
gen-bit kernel (same chunk mapping, same descriptor binary search) runs levels 2-4 in ~19 us at 40 registers.
The fused partition kernel is compiled under `__launch_bounds__(1024)` (SPLIT_INDICES_BLOCK_SIZE_DATA_PARTITION) and
gets 64 registers, the cap of a 1024-thread block, because the rarely-run fused tree-structure body (one warp per
split, FP64 leaf outputs) and gap copy share its allocation. It is launched with 256-thread blocks
(apply_row_batch), so 64 registers allow 4 blocks = 32 warps per SM where sm_120 holds 48 (1536 threads).

hypotheses.verdict_text:
The partition kernel was bound by rows in flight per SM, which its register allocation capped: under the 1024-thread
launch bound it took 64 registers at 256-thread blocks (4 blocks/SM). Register caps that spill (v1 40, v2 48) moved
active warps (29 -> 37) but added local-memory traffic and lost (+66%, +20%): defective builds, not the mechanism. With
blockDim.x a compile-time constant the same body at 8 rows/thread needs 48 registers without spills (v3): ncu 4 -> 10
blocks/SM, ~2.35x the rows in flight, L2 throughput 56-63% -> 74-80%, kernel -29..-31% (nsys 172 -> 119 us/round,
2 alternated pairs, same-arm spread < 0.2 us). The same transformation on the gen-bit (v4) gives -3.5% (shallow
levels only; deep levels are DRAM-bound). Deciding numbers: nsys same binary GPU timeline 3.653/3.639 -> 3.591/3.591
(inner rows) and 3.591/3.605 -> 3.576/3.573 (gen-bit rows) ms/round; same-binary e2e (tuner on) 1.016 (300 rounds x 2)
and 1.015 (1500 rounds x 3); quick check vs master 1.0868, md5 identical; guards and lattice (209/209) green.

slower).

hypotheses.hypothesis:
A pageable cudaMemcpyAsync costs the host ~1.6-2.3 us (driver staging copy + pinned-bounce DMA) before the next launch
can be issued; a cudaMemcpyAsync from a pinned, already-populated host buffer returns in ~0.5-0.8 us and the DMA of
a few KB starts at once. Writing the level's descriptors straight into pinned host memory (no extra host memcpy) and
uploading from there removes ~1.0-1.5 us from each of the two per-level critical gaps (Sync->GenBit and
SplitInner->Construct) and from the tree-boundary uploads: -20..-35 us/round of GPU idle = 0.6-1.0% per round
(parent 1.073 vs master -> ~1.080-1.083). Same bytes land on the device before the same kernels in the same stream
order: bit-identical. This is at the noise floor of the quick check (1.5%); the deciding number is the same-binary
gap measurement (Falsification).
hypotheses.observation:
Parent profile (30e384b8, nsys 60 rounds): round 3.595 ms, GPU busy 91%, idle 317 us/round, all of it host round trips
between levels. The largest: SyncBestSplitForLevelUsedTasksKernel end -> apply-descriptor H2D start, 9.3 us x 10 levels
= 92.5 us/round (2.6%). Its host timeline (API trace, t=0 = sync kernel end): wake +0.7, host decisions to +2.4,
cudaMemcpyAsync of host_apply_descs_ from PAGEABLE memory +2.4..+4.0 (the call blocks the host while the driver stages
the bytes), cudaStreamWaitEvent +4.1..+4.4, cudaLaunchKernel +4.6..+6.4, GPU H2D +6.8..+7.2, gen-bit start +8.0.
The second trip (split-info readback -> construct, 12.2 us x 9 = 108 us/round) has the same shape: pageable
cudaMemcpyAsync of the pair descriptors 1.8 us, then host grid planning 2.3 us, then two launches. All 37 H2D copies per
round are pageable (memkind "Pageable" in trace_cuda_gpu_trace.csv), 2.3 us of host time each (85 us/round), about 20
of them on the critical gaps. The two big kernels are at their DRAM floors (PROFILE.md), so this host chain is the
largest cost left that is not bandwidth.

nodes.verdict_text:
Every defect check passes (no spills: no new kernel touched; lattice.py --check 224/224; md5_identical true on
every quick check and every same-binary A/B run); the deciding number is 3 independent same-binary A/B runs (2, 2
and 3 alternated pairs) all statistically indistinguishable from 1.0 (0.9997, 1.0013, 1.0006 with Welch p=0.81);

changed to "Pinned") but did not move (API duration unchanged at ~1.7-2.0 us regardless of memkind), which is a
direct refutation under the task's own rule, not a missing-engagement defect; and two engineered variants were
measured (apply-descriptor mirror alone, then apply+pair mirrors together) plus a numeric bound covering every
remaining site of the same mechanism (<=1.4% theoretical ceiling, already realized as ~0%). Measured:
same-binary e2e_speedup 0.9997 / 1.0013 / 1.0006 (key on vs off), p=0.81. No commit (Finish step 2: "if nothing you

were already present via this branch's parent c103.
