hypotheses.hypothesis:
Removing the re-reads at the root and final levels -- the root gen-bit/split-inner compute row = leaf_data_start +
position while the main index buffer is still the identity (no index load: the root gen-bit becomes a contiguous
0.5 B/row column stream, the root split-inner a pure write), and the final level's gen-bit stores map[row] = child
itself so the 33 us map-only pass is not launched -- cuts the level apply by 35-60 us/round (root -12..-20 us, final
-20..-35 us net of the scatter stores moved into the gen-bit): round -1.0..-1.7%, same-binary ratio 1.010-1.017, quick
check vs master >= 1.085 (parent's final build: 1.0758). Same rows, same positions, same map entries: bit-identical.
hypotheses.observation:
Parent profile (85945f12, nsys 60 rounds): 3.586 ms/round; gen-bit 0.335 ms (9.3%), split-inner 0.119 ms (3.3%).
c111's mechanism (rows in flight per SM) is spent on the per-level kernels: levels 1-3 of the gen-bit sit at a ~16 us
floor, levels 6-9 (44-54 us) are DRAM-bound at ~1 sector per row, the split-inner runs at 74-80% L2 throughput and
16 rows/thread gained nothing (c111 v6). What remains are the two levels that move bytes the kernels already have:
- Root level (round 30): gen-bit 27.9 us vs 16-17 us at levels 1-2, split-inner 11.3 us. Both read the 4 B/row identity
  list FillDataIndicesBeforeTrainKernel wrote at the tree start (21.9 MB, evicted from L2 by the 1.15 ms fill) to
  derive row = position. c073's root_apply_direct (commit 521d90f2, never merged) measured root gen-bit 29.8 -> 17.4 us.
- Final level (tree-completing, final_map_only): gen-bit 53.6 us, then HybridSplitInnerBatchKernel<4,1> map-only 33.3 us
  re-reads every split row's index and direction bit to store map[row] = child, a value the gen-bit held in registers;
  then the unfused tree-structure kernel 4.3 us. c076's final_map_genbit (commit 577e4140, never merged, 2 rows/thread)
  measured round -12..-37 us; c111's v5 (the map-only pass itself at 8 rows) was slower: scatter-write-bound.
Together: ~75 us/round of the level apply (2.1%) is re-reading bytes already in hand.
hypotheses.plan:
Two cuda_plan keys (default on), both in `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h` (add to the struct and to the key lookup
next to `apply_inner_rows` at line ~487 / ~731); all kernel work in `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu`
(+ `.cpp`, `.hpp` for the host flag). Reference diffs to read with `git show` (read-only; do not merge them -- their
lineages predate c103/c111): `git show 521d90f2` (root_apply_direct) and `git show 577e4140` (final_map_genbit).

V1 `root_apply_direct` (first, the bigger and simpler one):
- `HybridGenBitChunk<ROWS, BLOCK>` (cuda_data_partition.cu:1457): add `bool DIRECT = false`; the index load
  `cuda_data_indices[d.leaf_data_start + local]` becomes `d.leaf_data_start + local` when DIRECT (same -1 sentinel for
  local >= num_data_in_leaf). `HybridGenBitVectorFlatRowsKernel<ROWS>` (1572): add `bool DIRECT` template parameter,
  pass it through. Leave `HybridGenBitVectorUpdateLeafIndexBatchKernel` (graph path) unchanged.
- `HybridSplitInnerChunk<WRITE_LEAF_MAP, ROWS, BLOCK>` (~1660): add `bool DIRECT`; `row_index[k] = DIRECT ?
  d.leaf_data_start + pos : cuda_data_indices_in_leaf[pos]`. `HybridSplitInnerFusedBatchBody` (2150): a runtime
  `int direct_rows` kernel argument (append to FALCATA_SPLIT_INNER_FUSED_PARAMS/ARGS) selecting
  `HybridSplitInnerChunk<..., true>` vs `<..., false>` (block-uniform branch; c073's FALCATA_FUSED_SPLIT_INNER_CHUNK
  macro). The gap-copy and struct ids are untouched (the root has no gaps). Check with cuobjdump that the
  `HybridSplitInnerFusedBatchRowsKernel<8,0,1>` stays at 48 registers / STACK 0 and
  `HybridGenBitVectorFlatRowsKernel<8,...>` at <= 34: if the second chunk instantiation raises registers, make
  DIRECT a template parameter of the kernel instead (two kernels, host picks).
- Host flag `bool main_indices_identity_` in `cuda_data_partition.hpp`: set true right after the
  `FillDataIndicesBeforeTrainKernel` launch (cuda_data_partition.cu:64, the no-bagging BeforeTrain path only); set
  false by EVERY other writer or re-layout of `cuda_data_indices_` -- c073's list: BeforeTrain (bagging branch),
  SetLeafDataLayout, SplitLevelBatched (after the swap: the new main holds the partition), SplitInner,
  LaunchSplitInnerKernel, UpdateTrainScore (its copy), CalcBlockDim, SetUsedDataIndices, ResetTrainingData,
  ResetConfig, EnsureLevelPartitioned, CaptureHybridGraphApplyKernels, the CollapseLeafWindows and
  FillDataIndexToLeafIndex host launchers, the destructor. Grep `cuda_data_indices_` writers in both .cu and .cpp
  and compare against that list before building.
- `LaunchSplitLevelBatchedKernels` (2319): `direct = plan.root_apply_direct && main_indices_identity_ && every
  host_apply_descs_[k] window has leaf_data_start >= 0 and leaf_data_start + num_data_in_leaf <= root_num_data()`;
  launch the DIRECT gen-bit (its own `ApplyRowsTakes` entry: the memo is keyed by kernel pointer, fine) and pass
  `direct ? 1 : 0` to LaunchHybridSplitInnerFusedBatchKernel. The non-rows (4-row / 1-row) fallbacks may stay
  non-direct (off there) to keep the change small; the key's comment must say so.
- Do NOT skip FillDataIndicesBeforeTrainKernel (other paths read the buffer: leaf-wise SplitInner, the deferred
  partition of final_map_only, bagging); that is a separate, riskier idea (listed under Untried).
Quick check after V1 alone: md5_identical true, e2e_speedup above 1.076; nsys per level: root gen-bit ~28 -> <=17 us,
root split-inner 11.3 -> <=10 us.

V2 `final_map_genbit` on the 8-row gen-bit:
- `HybridGenBitChunk`: add `bool MAP = false` and a trailing `int* cuda_data_index_to_leaf_index = nullptr`; after the
  decision for row k, `if (MAP && global_data_index[k] >= 0) map[global_data_index[k]] = to_left ? d.left_leaf_index
  : d.right_leaf_index;` (HybridLeafMapChunk's store for the same row and bit). Instantiate
  `HybridGenBitVectorFlatRowsKernel<8, DIRECT=false, MAP=true>` (the final level is never the root when
  max_depth > 0; if both hold, take MAP only).
- `LaunchSplitLevelBatchedKernels`: when `map_only && plan.final_map_genbit && apply_row_batch && apply_genbit_rows
  takes`: issue the map's full-sector `cudaMemsetAsync` (the one now inside `LaunchLevelSplitInnerKernel`, line
  ~2458, same stream 0) BEFORE the gen-bit, launch the MAP gen-bit, keep the aggregate, and in
  `LaunchLevelSplitInnerKernel` skip only the map-only split-inner launch (the unfused tree-structure kernel after it
  still runs; the direction bits and block counts are still written for `EnsureLevelPartitioned`). The residual map
  pass (`MaterializeHybridLeafMapSubset`, early_leaf_map at cuda_single_gpu_tree_learner.cpp:2393-2400 or the tree
  end) is issued after this call on the same stream, so it still follows the memset.
- Check registers of the MAP instantiation (the 2 extra leaf-index fields may push 34 -> 40; still 12 blocks/SM is
  fine). If the 8-row MAP gen-bit is slower than gen-bit + map-only pass (scatter-bound, as c111 v5), try V2b: MAP
  on the 4-row 256-thread `HybridGenBitVectorUpdateLeafIndexBatchKernel<4, MAP>` (c076's measured shape was 2 rows).
Quick check after V1+V2: md5 identical, ratio >= 1.085; nsys: final level gen-bit + map-only 53.6 + 33.3 -> <= 70 us.

V3 (only with budget left, untried #2 of c111) `apply_inner_scan`: the split-inner's per-thread serial
`shared_warp_scan` prefix (up to 31 dependent shared loads per thread, 1660-1700) as one warp-shuffle exclusive scan of
the 32 chunk words by warp 0 into shared, read once per thread. Keep only if cuobjdump shows <= 48 registers and no
stack (c111 v7's gen-bit analogue raised registers 34 -> 46 and lost); expected <= 10 us/round.

Order: V1, quick check, commit; V2, quick check, commit if not slower; V3 if time. Same-binary nsys A/B (keys off vs
on, 2 alternated pairs, 60 rounds) for the deciding per-level numbers; guards (covtype, year, higgs, missing,
numerai53-example) before the final commit since V1 touches every writer of the index buffer.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Rows in flight per SM bound the level apply kernels at L2-resident levels; 8-rows-per-thread compile-time-block builds (2.25x / 2x the rows in flight) cut split-inner ~30% and gen-bit a few percent, about 1.8% per round over the parent.

hypotheses.observation: Parent profile: split-inner fused partition 0.176 ms/round (4.9%), gen-bit 0.347 ms/round (9.7%). Both run 256-thread blocks of 4 rows per thread compiled under a 1024-thread launch bound (64 registers), so only 4 blocks (4096 rows in flight) fit an SM; the data is L2-resident at shallow levels and the kernels are occupancy/latency-bound there. Sibling c111 (same construct code, parent c104) measured -31% split-inner and -4% gen-bit from 8-rows-per-thread 128-thread compile-time-block builds taken only where the occupancy API gives strictly more rows in flight per SM.

Then sweep the mechanism's variants with remaining budget (rows per thread / block size of the gen-bit build at the deep DRAM-bound levels).

waits on that index load (index -> bin dependent chain) although the root's bins are one contiguous column.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Mechanism: the gains are additive because they act on different parts of the round (c103: construct occupancy/flush,
readback round trips, tree-start work; c111: rows in flight per SM in the level apply kernels), and nothing in c103's
diff changes the apply kernels' register allocation or launch shape. Merging c111 reproduces its same-binary gain
(+1.5-1.6% of the round: split-inner ~-55 us, gen-bit ~-12 us per round) on top of c103's 1.0729: predicted score vs
master >= 1.085 (quick check ~1.09-1.10, candidate median ~3.45 ms/round vs the parent's 3.50-3.60), md5 identical
(aa1e77c44ce2faf16db3d6ec86e8f2eb, the md5 every sibling quick check on this workload produced).
hypotheses.observation:
Parent profile (30e384b8, 60 rounds, nsys): round 3.595 ms, kernels 3.286 ms/round. The level apply's partition kernel
HybridSplitInnerFusedBatchKernel<4,0,1> costs 0.176 ms/round (4.9%, 9 launches of 19.6 us) and the flat gen-bit
HybridGenBitVectorUpdateLeafIndexBatchKernel<4> 0.347 ms/round (9.7%, 10 launches of 34.9 us). Both are compiled under a
1024-thread launch bound (64 registers) but launched with 256-thread blocks, so the occupancy API gives only 4 blocks/SM
(c111's ncu). c111 (accepted, 1.0657 vs master on the c104 lineage, which holds the same construct code as this tree)
adds a second build of each body at 8 rows/thread in 128-thread blocks whose size is a template constant: 48 / 34
registers, 10 / 12 blocks/SM, split-inner -31% (172 -> 119 us/round), gen-bit -3.6%, same-binary e2e 1.015-1.016.
Those two keys are absent from this tree (`grep apply_inner_rows include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h` is empty). The two
lineages touch disjoint costs: c103's extra over c104 is readback_fused + tree-start keys (host round trips and
tree-start work), c111's is the apply kernels' occupancy.

Mode "combine": bring kevo/c111 into this tree, resolve the two conflicts, build, install, quick check, commit.

1. `git merge --no-edit kevo/c111` from the worktree root. Merge base 526d5e10. Only two files change:
   - `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h`: auto-merges (c111 adds `bool apply_inner_rows = true;` / `bool apply_genbit_rows
     = true;` with comments after `apply_row_batch`, and the two `if (key == ...)` lines in the lookup; c103's keys
     pair_code5_flat/slots/tall/epilogue, readback_fused, const_hess_reads, dirty_final_slots, hist_zero_quant_half are
     already on both sides with identical text). Check the result has exactly one definition of each key.
   - `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu`: CONFLICT, two hunks, both the same cause: this tree's readback_fused
     (ba3cf298) added a trailing `int* split_info_mirror_base` parameter to HybridSplitInnerFusedBatchKernel and to
     LaunchHybridSplitInnerFusedBatchKernel, while c111 moved the kernel's parameter list into the macros
     `FALCATA_SPLIT_INNER_FUSED_PARAMS` / `FALCATA_SPLIT_INNER_FUSED_ARGS` and the body into
     `HybridSplitInnerFusedBatchBody<ROWS, USE_NCCL_REDUCE, USE_GRAD_DISCRETIZED, BLOCK>`.
   - `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu`: NOT touched by the merge (byte-identical on both sides;
     c111 carries c094/c095/c103's construct commits under other hashes). If git shows it modified, something is wrong.
2. Resolve hunk 1 (around the comment "Gap ranges are disjoint from every split window ..."): take c111's side (the
   two macros + `HybridSplitInnerFusedBatchBody` header) and append `, \` + `int* split_info_mirror_base` as the last
   entry of `FALCATA_SPLIT_INNER_FUSED_PARAMS` and `, split_info_mirror_base` as the last entry of
   `FALCATA_SPLIT_INNER_FUSED_ARGS`. Drop our side's old explicit parameter list. The body's struct-block branch
   (auto-merged from our side) already passes `split_info_mirror_base != nullptr ? split_info_mirror_base + 18 * id :
   nullptr` to HybridSplitTreeStructureSplit, so it needs the name in scope; `HybridSplitInnerFusedBatchKernel` and
   `HybridSplitInnerFusedBatchRowsKernel` (both `FALCATA_SPLIT_INNER_FUSED_PARAMS` -> body with
   `FALCATA_SPLIT_INNER_FUSED_ARGS`) then carry the mirror pointer into both builds automatically.
3. Resolve hunk 2 (`LaunchHybridSplitInnerFusedBatchKernel`): take c111's side (the `auto* kernel = ...; if constexpr
   (ROWS > 1) { ... ApplyRowsTakes(...) ... wide<<<grid, wide_block, 0, stream>>>(FALCATA_SPLIT_INNER_FUSED_ARGS);
   return; } kernel<<<grid, block, 0, stream>>>(FALCATA_SPLIT_INNER_FUSED_ARGS);`) and keep our side's signature tail
   `int* cuda_split_info_buffer_base, int* split_info_mirror_base) {` so the launcher accepts the mirror pointer the
   caller (the `launch_fused` lambda in `CUDADataPartition::LaunchSplitLevelBatchedKernels`, which already passes
   `cuda_split_info_buffer_.RawData(), split_info_mirror`) hands it. Keep the `#undef` lines after the function.
4. Sanity greps before building: `grep -n 'split_info_mirror_base' src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu` must show
   the macro PARAMS entry, the macro ARGS entry, the body's struct-block use, the launcher signature, and the two
   HybridSplitTreeStructureBatchKernel parameters (unchanged). `grep -c '<<<<<<<\|>>>>>>>' ...` must be 0.
   `git diff HEAD -- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu | md5sum` is not comparable to c111's own diff
   (34d37a4d, `git diff 07b1f7d129..85945f1210`) because of the mirror lines; instead compare `git diff kevo/c111 --
   src include` against `git diff 526d5e10 30e384b8 -- src include`: the merged tree vs c111 must show only c103's
   extra (readback_fused mirror lines, the tree-start keys), nothing else.
5. Build (`cmake --build build -j 2>&1 | tail -25`, ~20 s for the one .cu), then install into the venv
   (`sh build-python.sh install --precompile`). Optionally `cuobjdump -res-usage` on the built lib for
   `HybridSplitInnerFusedBatchRowsKernel<8,0,1>` (expect ~48 regs, 0 spill) and `HybridGenBitVectorFlatRowsKernel<8>`
   (~34 regs): same numbers as c111 reported, since the mirror pointer adds only a kernel parameter.
6. Quick check (the brief's e2e.py command, 300 rounds, 2 pairs, max Bash timeout, foreground, re-run on timeout).
   Must show `"md5_identical": true` with md5 aa1e77c44ce2faf16db3d6ec86e8f2eb and e2e_speedup >= ~1.085.
7. Commit: `git add -A src include && git commit -q -m "merge kevo/c111: apply_inner_rows + apply_genbit_rows on the
   c103 tree (readback_fused mirror pointer threaded through the fused partition macros)"` (the merge commit itself,
   with the resolution; if `git merge` left the merge in progress, the commit completes it).
8. If budget remains (effective minutes < budget - 15): a same-binary A/B of the two new keys off vs on
   (`--plan-stock apply_inner_rows:off,apply_genbit_rows:off` style, or nsys 60 rounds x 2 alternated) to log the
   mechanism's number in this tree; optionally the lattice gate (`tests/gates/lattice.py --check`). No further code
   change is planned for this candidate: the fill and construct are at their DRAM ceilings (perf-dead-ends, c093, c108)
   and the remaining per-level host idle is c110/c112 territory (c110 was rejected by review, c112 refuted).

Risks to md5 identity seen while planning: none in the kernels (c111's ballot layout is row r -> word r/32, bit r%32 at
any ROWS; verified by its reviewer). The only merge-specific risk is the mirror pointer: if `split_info_mirror_base` is
dropped from the macros, the build fails (not a silent error); if the launcher's signature loses the parameter, the
lambda's call fails to compile. A wrong resolution cannot silently change results. The wide gen-bit launch keeps
`block_dim / kGenBitWideRows` threads with `constexpr kBlock = SPLIT_INDICES_BLOCK_SIZE_DATA_PARTITION / ROWS`; both
are 128 for block_dim 1024, as in c111.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
**Confirmed.** All four verdict conditions hold: (1) no defect found in the merge (build clean, no spills beyond
what c111 itself reported, no unrelated kernel changed); (2) the deciding number is the same-binary A/B of
`apply_inner_rows`+`apply_genbit_rows` off vs on in this tree, 2 pairs, 300 rounds: **1.018**, md5 identical,
consistent with c111's own same-binary number (1.015-1.016); (3) the mechanism check (nsys kernel-time breakdown)
shows the targeted kernels' costs moving exactly as predicted (split-inner -33%, gen-bit -3.2%, matching c111's own
ncu numbers to within a few percent) and the wide builds engaging with the expected launch counts; (4) this is a
"combine" task porting one already-fully-swept mechanism (c111 itself measured >=3 variants: 4/8 rows, the
occupancy gate, block-size shapes) onto a new base — iterating variants of the apply-rows mechanism further here
would only re-derive what c111 already established. Overall quick check vs master: md5 identical, **e2e_speedup
1.095**, matching c103's own 1.073 composed with c111's own ~1.5-2% same-binary gain. Committed as `aadea45f`
(merge of `30e384b8` x `85945f12`).

   (auto-merged from our side) already passes `split_info_mirror_base != nullptr ? split_info_mirror_base + 18 * id :
   nullptr` to HybridSplitTreeStructureSplit, so it needs the name in scope; `HybridSplitInnerFusedBatchKernel` and
   `HybridSplitInnerFusedBatchRowsKernel` (both `FALCATA_SPLIT_INNER_FUSED_PARAMS` -> body with
   `FALCATA_SPLIT_INNER_FUSED_ARGS`) then carry the mirror pointer into both builds automatically.
3. Resolve hunk 2 (`LaunchHybridSplitInnerFusedBatchKernel`): take c111's side (the `auto* kernel = ...; if constexpr
   (ROWS > 1) { ... ApplyRowsTakes(...) ... wide<<<grid, wide_block, 0, stream>>>(FALCATA_SPLIT_INNER_FUSED_ARGS);
   return; } kernel<<<grid, block, 0, stream>>>(FALCATA_SPLIT_INNER_FUSED_ARGS);`) and keep our side's signature tail
   `int* cuda_split_info_buffer_base, int* split_info_mirror_base) {` so the launcher accepts the mirror pointer the
   caller (the `launch_fused` lambda in `CUDADataPartition::LaunchSplitLevelBatchedKernels`, which already passes
   `cuda_split_info_buffer_.RawData(), split_info_mirror`) hands it. Keep the `#undef` lines after the function.
4. Sanity greps before building: `grep -n 'split_info_mirror_base' src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu` must show
   the macro PARAMS entry, the macro ARGS entry, the body's struct-block use, the launcher signature, and the two
   HybridSplitTreeStructureBatchKernel parameters (unchanged). `grep -c '<<<<<<<\|>>>>>>>' ...` must be 0.
   `git diff HEAD -- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu | md5sum` is not comparable to c111's own diff
   (34d37a4d, `git diff 07b1f7d129..85945f1210`) because of the mirror lines; instead compare `git diff kevo/c111 --
   src include` against `git diff 526d5e10 30e384b8 -- src include`: the merged tree vs c111 must show only c103's
   extra (readback_fused mirror lines, the tree-start keys), nothing else.
5. Build (`cmake --build build -j 2>&1 | tail -25`, ~20 s for the one .cu), then install into the venv
   (`sh build-python.sh install --precompile`). Optionally `cuobjdump -res-usage` on the built lib for
   `HybridSplitInnerFusedBatchRowsKernel<8,0,1>` (expect ~48 regs, 0 spill) and `HybridGenBitVectorFlatRowsKernel<8>`
   (~34 regs): same numbers as c111 reported, since the mirror pointer adds only a kernel parameter.
6. Quick check (the brief's e2e.py command, 300 rounds, 2 pairs, max Bash timeout, foreground, re-run on timeout).
   Must show `"md5_identical": true` with md5 aa1e77c44ce2faf16db3d6ec86e8f2eb and e2e_speedup >= ~1.085.

   c103 tree (readback_fused mirror pointer threaded through the fused partition macros)"` (the merge commit itself,
   with the resolution; if `git merge` left the merge in progress, the commit completes it).
8. If budget remains (effective minutes < budget - 15): a same-binary A/B of the two new keys off vs on
   (`--plan-stock apply_inner_rows:off,apply_genbit_rows:off` style, or nsys 60 rounds x 2 alternated) to log the
   mechanism's number in this tree; optionally the lattice gate (`tests/gates/lattice.py --check`). No further code
   change is planned for this candidate: the fill and construct are at their DRAM ceilings (perf-dead-ends, c093, c108)
   and the remaining per-level host idle is c110/c112 territory (c110 was rejected by review, c112 refuted).

Risks to md5 identity seen while planning: none in the kernels (c111's ballot layout is row r -> word r/32, bit r%32 at
any ROWS; verified by its reviewer). The only merge-specific risk is the mirror pointer: if `split_info_mirror_base` is
dropped from the macros, the build fails (not a silent error); if the launcher's signature loses the parameter, the
lambda's call fails to compile. A wrong resolution cannot silently change results. The wide gen-bit launch keeps
`block_dim / kGenBitWideRows` threads with `constexpr kBlock = SPLIT_INDICES_BLOCK_SIZE_DATA_PARTITION / ROWS`; both
are 128 for block_dim 1024, as in c111.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Sorting a level's leaf-pair/split descriptors by descending size (longest-processing-time-first) before dispatch reduces GPU idle tail time from load-imbalanced blocks, per ncu's own imbalance warning on the construct kernel
nodes.falsification: Same-binary A/B (key on vs off in `--plan-stock`/`--plan-cand`, or compiled off), nsys 60 rounds x >=2 pairs each arm: refuted if construct ms/round does not move outside noise (~1-2%) and ncu's idle/"No Eligible" percentage on the construct does not drop. Refuted outright (mechanism wrong, not just untried) if e2e ratio vs master is < 1.0 across >= 2 pairs. Not refuted by a single run under noise -- iterate (e.g. sort ascending as a sanity-check control, which should be neutral-to-negative if the mechanism is real).

hypotheses.falsification: Same-binary nsys (60 rounds, key off vs on, alternated, 2 pairs): if the fill's DRAM read bytes (ncu dram__bytes_read.sum on one launch, or lts__t_sectors_srcunit_tex_op_read_lookup_miss) fall by >= 25% but the fill time falls by < 8%, the bytes mechanism is refuted (the fill would be issue/latency-bound at the new byte count: check sm__throughput and warps active). If the fill falls >= 15% but e2e over the parent is < 1.02 (same-binary e2e.py A/B, 300 rounds x 2 pairs), the gain is eaten by the split-read side: the deep gen-bit (levels 6-9) must stay within +3% of 45-53 us, else that reader is the defect to fix, not the hypothesis. md5 non-identical on any guard is a defect (decode), not a refutation.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Storing the column-major matrix in a radix-R packed form (R = the largest bin span over the store's columns, D = floor(32 / log2 R) digits per 32-bit word, MSB-first fractional encoding so a digit is 2 integer multiplies to extract, as kevo/c046 did for its dense copy) as the ONLY resident copy cuts the fill's read bytes from 4 to 32/D bits per value (R <= 6: 12 digits, 2.67 bits, -33% of 970 MB = -320 MB per fill). Since the fill is DRAM-bound at 79% of peak and moves only its bytes, the fill time falls in proportion to its bytes: 1.69 -> 1.37 GB = -19% = ~220 us/round, e2e >= 1.05 over the parent (quick check vs master >= 1.14). The per-level split read (HybridLoadBin's colmajor_split path) keeps 1 sector per row at deep levels (already DRAM-bound there, 86-88%) and gets 96 rows per sector instead of 64 at shallow levels (L2-resident anyway): neutral. Memory: the store shrinks from 9.2 GB to ~6.1 GB; no second copy. Bit-identical: the same bin values are decoded exactly (integer arithmetic; c046 verified md5 identity for the fill side).
hypotheses.observation: The fused fill is 32.9% of the round (1.162 ms) and moves exactly its bytes: ncu shows 79% of DRAM peak for ~1.69 GB per launch = 970 MB of 4-bit column-major reads (355 columns x num_data / 2) + 22 MB gradients + 700 MB code-view writes (L2 write sectors 699.4 MB), with no over-fetch (the per-tile column runs are 64 B, sector-aligned). The construct (31%) runs at 75-80% DRAM at every level including the dense level-1 gathers, and the gen-bit's deep levels are at 86-88% DRAM while its shallow levels are 100% L2 hits: no ordering/locality lever is left in those two. The 4-bit column-major store is still the only resident copy of the matrix (grep: no radix-6 store in src; kevo/c046's dense copy was never merged) although every column here has <= 6 values (5 + a NaN bin on 60 columns), so 4 bits per value is 1.5x the 2.67 bits a 12-digits-per-word radix-6 store needs.
hypotheses.plan:
cuda_plan key: `colmajor_radix` (bool, default on; engages only when every column of the store has span <= the radix cap the decode handles, i.e. R <= 15 so that D >= 8; where it does not engage, the 4-bit store is built as today). Derive R and D at store-build time from the columns' bin spans (data properties), never from a literal. Keep the 4-bit path intact behind the key (the key off must reproduce today's bytes and timings for the same-binary A/B).
1. Reuse before writing: `git log --oneline master..kevo/c046` and `git diff master...kevo/c046 -- src include` hold the dense base-6 copy: its builder (a kernel over the Dataset's columns), its MSB-first fraction decode (digit k of word w: two multiplies, see its CUDAFillCompactData4BitTiledRootHistKernel reads), and its fused-fill read path (`load_words` / `prefetch_l2` / the byte passes of src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu:600-760, `bs_src_nib0/bs_src_nib1/bs_dst_byte/bs_dst_stride` tables built in cuda_histogram_constructor.cpp around the colmajor_direct setup). Port that read path into the current kernel (which gained the code5 pack, word_prefetch, l2_lead, root_hist_short_blocks since c046; keep those).
2. Make the radix store the store itself: where `colmajor_direct` builds the 4-bit column-major copy from the Dataset's columns (cuda_histogram_constructor.cpp, search `colmajor_direct` / `colmajor_align`), build the radix words instead when the key engages (column pitch in words, sector-aligned as colmajor_align does for nibbles); record R, D and the pitch in the constructor's members so every reader can decode.
3. Move the per-level split read: `HybridLoadBin` in src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu (the colmajor_split branch, also the graph-loop CUDAHybridGraphFeatureSource variant) reads word row/D of the split column and extracts digit row%D; keep the __ldcs/evict_first flag behaviour. The level apply's descriptor (CUDAHybridApplyDescriptor, filled in cuda_data_partition.cpp) needs the column's word pitch instead of the nibble pitch.
4. Move the fallback fills that read the 4-bit store: the nibble/full view fill (`FillFullViewFromStore`, `LaunchCompactFill` with the store as source, the codec fill CUDAFillCompactCodecKernel if it reads the store) and any `NibbleViewData()`-based path that decodes from the store rather than from the per-tree view; a path that cannot be moved in time must force the key off (one gate, at store-build time) rather than read stale bytes.
5. Variants, in order: (a) R from data, D = floor(32/log2 R) (12 here); (b) if the fill's byte passes lose issue efficiency (the word now holds 12 rows, the tile is 128 rows = 10.67 words: pad the column run per 128-row tile to 11 words = 44 B so a tile never straddles a word; measure DRAM% and read sectors with ncu on the fill: 44 B runs touch 2-3 sectors, so the L2 must merge the shared sectors between adjacent tiles that run in the same block (contiguous tiles) -- if dram bytes read exceed the unique volume by > 5%, switch to 384-row groups (33 words = 132 B) or to tiles_per_block a multiple of 8 so block boundaries fall on 352-B sector-aligned runs); (c) only if (a)/(b) show the shallow gen-bit slower: keep a nibble decode table in shared memory for HybridLoadBin.
6. Quick check must show md5_identical true and e2e_speedup >= 1.14 vs master (parent is ~1.09-1.10). Then the same-binary A/B of the key (off in --plan-stock) >= 1.04 with 2 pairs, and nsys fill <= 0.98 ms/round. Also run tests/gates/lattice.py --check and the five md5 guards (covtype/year/higgs have wide columns: the key must fall back to the 4-bit store there and stay md5-identical).
md5 risks seen: (1) 60 columns have a NaN bin (span 6, not 5): R must be the max span including the NaN/most-frequent-bin offset, not num_bin of the "typical" column; (2) the fused fill reads up to 15 bytes past a row's last slot for the code5 pack (comment at cuda_histogram_constructor.cu:1070): the new source layout must keep that slack valid in shared memory; (3) column_meta spans and the pair-joint tables index bins the same way whatever the store codec: only the decode changes, never the bin value; (4) the colmajor_split read is also used by the final_map_only / root_apply_direct paths: all readers of the store must switch together or the key must gate them all off.

Verified pointers ([date omitted]): branch kevo/c046 holds the dense copy as commits 24622c67 (colmajor_dense6: base 6, 12 rows per word, 11 words per 128 rows, where every value of the store is below 6), 389b7cc5 (colmajor_dense6_frac: MSB-first fractions, one multiply + one multiply-high per digit), c4e0a609 and df44871f (its gates/release); `git diff master...kevo/c046 --stat` touches 11 files (888 insertions) including cuda_single_gpu_tree_learner.cpp and cuda_leaf_splits.hpp, so port the fill read path and builder by hand rather than cherry-picking (c046 predates the code5 view, readback_fused and the short-block fill). HybridLoadBin has 2 occurrences in src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu; colmajor_direct's store setup is in src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cpp (lines ~39, 364, 593). Note c046's "11 words per 128 rows" = 44 B per tile per column: its tile runs are not sector-aligned, so variant 5(b)'s ncu check of DRAM read bytes vs unique bytes is mandatory, not optional.

hypotheses.falsification: Same-binary A/B (key on vs off in `--plan-stock`/`--plan-cand`, or compiled off), nsys 60 rounds x >=2 pairs each arm: refuted if construct ms/round does not move outside noise (~1-2%) and ncu's idle/"No Eligible" percentage on the construct does not drop. Refuted outright (mechanism wrong, not just untried) if e2e ratio vs master is < 1.0 across >= 2 pairs. Not refuted by a single run under noise -- iterate (e.g. sort ascending as a sanity-check control, which should be neutral-to-negative if the mechanism is real).
hypotheses.hypothesis: Sorting the level's pair descriptors by descending size (max of the two leaves' row counts) before upload is a classic longest-processing-time-first (LPT) schedule: CUDA's hardware block scheduler dispatches blocks in increasing linear block-ID order as SMs free up, so putting the longest-running pairs' blocks first lets them spread across all SMs immediately, with the shorter pairs' blocks filling in behind as SMs become free -- shrinking the tail instead of leaving it at the end. Expected effect: fewer idle-SM cycles at the end of the construct (and, as a side effect, the find/sync kernels, which share the same array) without changing any per-pair computation. Quantified: a visible reduction in "No Eligible"/idle cycles and in construct ms/round of a few percent (the construct is 31% of the round; even a 5-10% cut in its tail would be ~0.3-0.6% of the round -- modest, but the change is nearly free to test, so worth a same-binary A/B before dismissing it). Falsifiable at >= 1.0 ratio with no construct-time change.
hypotheses.observation: ncu on the current construct kernel (`CUDAConstructDiscretizedHistogramPairJointCode5WordKernel<5,1,1>`, `--clock-control none --cache-control none`, `[local artifact omitted]`): theoretical occupancy capped at 66.7% (8/12 warps per scheduler -- register/block-shape limited, consistent with `pair_code5_tall` already choosing "the tallest block the occupancy API allows", i.e. this axis is already tuned), only 0.45 eligible warps/scheduler, "No Eligible" 71.7% of cycles, and ncu's own `IssueSlotUtilization` rule text names the cause directly: "avoid possible load imbalances due to highly different execution durations per warp." 74.6% of the stall cycles are L1TEX-global scoreboard waits, consistent with the DRAM~75-80%-of-peak reading in PROFILE.md. The operator's hint ("ordering for L2 locality... matters more than block size") plus this imbalance warning point at *dispatch order*, not shape: the level's leaf pairs (`host_hybrid_pair_descs_`, built in `CUDASingleGPUTreeLearner::EnqueueLevelBestSplitSearch`) are uploaded in whatever order the tree's splits produced them, and that same array drives blockIdx.z (or `pair_block_map`'s prefix) for the construct, and also the find/sync kernels. Leaf pairs vary a lot in row count (level-batched growth with `skip_unsplittable`/`skip_empty_tail` means small and large leaves are live in the same level), so a kernel launched in that arbitrary order can leave a long tail: SMs that drew small pairs finish and sit idle while a few SMs are still grinding a large pair's blocks -- exactly ncu's warning.
hypotheses.plan: New cuda_plan key `pair_level_order` (default on), `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h`. In `CUDASingleGPUTreeLearner::EnqueueLevelBestSplitSearch` (`src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_single_gpu_tree_learner.cpp`), after building `host_hybrid_pair_descs_[0..num_pairs)` (which already carries `num_data_in_smaller_leaf`/`num_data_in_larger_leaf` per pair) and before the H2D upload, `std::stable_sort` the vector by descending `max(num_data_in_smaller_leaf, num_data_in_larger_leaf)`, gated on `num_pairs > 1 && vec_num_targets_ <= 1` (vector mode indexes a plane slab by pair *position* within the same call, so it is left untouched to avoid a second, unverified reordering path). Checked for correctness before writing: every per-pair struct pointer (`smaller_struct`/`larger_struct`) and leaf index in the descriptor is already stable per *leaf*, not per *array position* (confirmed by reading where they are assigned: `desc.smaller_struct = pair.smaller_struct`, a per-leaf-role device pointer from `BeforeTrain`/the previous level's split, never computed from `i`); every downstream kernel (construct, `FindBestSplitsForLevel`, `SyncBestSplitForLevelUsedTasksKernel`) writes its result to a per-leaf location (`cuda_leaf_best_split_info_ + leaf_index`, the leaf's own `hist_in_leaf` pointer), never a per-position one; `pair_block_map`'s grid-sizing (`SetLevelHostPairDescs`) is computed from whatever order it is given, consistently with the upload. So reordering only changes *when* each pair's blocks are issued, not what they compute or where they write: bit-identical by construction, no new numerics.
hypotheses.verdict_text: Per the verdict bar, for the construct (`pair_level_order`): (1) no defect was found in that build -- it ran cleanly, so nothing to fix. (2) deciding number is a same-binary A/B, 3 pairs, CI spans zero. (3) mechanism check (ncu's targeted "No Eligible" stall %) did not move, consistent with the grid already being exactly one wave (170 blocks for 170 SMs, by the already-accepted `pair_code5_slots`/`tall`). (4) only one clean variant was needed here because point 3's explanation is a structural/numeric bound that covers every possible dispatch order on this kernel (a single wave has no order-dependent tail by construction) -- this satisfies "a numeric bound that covers all of them" for this specific grid shape; it does not generalize to a kernel with a genuinely multi-wave grid. So `pair_level_order` is refuted and should not be retried on the construct (or on find/sync, which share its single-wave-sized grid) without first changing the grid shape itself, which conflicts with the already-accepted sizing. For the level-apply (`apply_level_order`): both variants tried are defects (crashes), not measurements of the mechanism -- per the bar, "a measurement taken on a build with a known defect does not count," and neither crash was fixed and re-measured, so there is no valid verdict on the mechanism itself. The mechanism (genuinely multi-wave dispatch, unlike the construct) remains plausible and untested; the specific obstacle (the binary-search dispatcher's ordering requirement) is now precisely identified for whoever attempts a third variant with a proper second indirection. Net outcome this session: no committable improvement; nothing committed (working tree reverted to the parent, a95227d0be, confirmed building and installing cleanly before finishing).

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: H2: the deep-level split finder (94 regs, 5 blocks/SM) pays a second wave where its grid exceeds the resident slots, so a register-capped build with 6+ blocks/SM puts L8/L9 in one wave and cuts them from ~14 to ~10 us
nodes.falsification: L8/L9 find not faster with all blocks resident (one wave) -> not wave-bound.

hypotheses.falsification:
- cuobjdump: if no variant gets below 56 registers without a spill, the implementation did not engage (not a refutation).
- With fewer registers and more resident blocks (ncu: theoretical occupancy > 75%), a same-binary nsys A/B (key on vs off,
  2 alternated pairs, 60 rounds) showing split-inner < 4% faster (< ~5 us/round) refutes the rows-in-flight bound for
  this kernel (it is then L2-bandwidth-bound at its current occupancy).
- md5 must stay aa1e77c44ce2faf16db3d6ec86e8f2eb (quick check).
hypotheses.hypothesis:
Mechanism: the fused partition kernel is still bound by rows in flight per SM, which its 56-register allocation caps at
9 blocks. Each thread holds 8 copies of warp-uniform ballot words (word[k], identical across a warp's lanes) through the
block barrier, and the runtime write_leaf_map branch compiles a second chunk body with a map pointer and two leaf
indices into the same allocation. Keeping the ballot words in shared memory (one per warp-word, read back as broadcasts
after the barrier) cuts the chunk path's live registers by ~8; target <= 48 registers (10 blocks/SM) or <= 40 (12
blocks/SM, full occupancy), no spill. Expected: split-inner 13.1 -> 11-12 us/launch (-8..-15%, -10..-18 us/round),

One variant, with a 16-byte spill (a defect by rule 1), so not a refutation. Its mechanism check says the premise is
wrong rather than untested: with 6 instead of 5 block slots per SM the achieved occupancy stayed at 26-29% (ncu), so the

at shallow levels), not a second wave. The level whose grid dropped below one wave got slower (L8 14.0 -> 16.0 us, nsys),
consistent with the spill costing the chain itself.
Untried: a spill-free register cut of the find kernel (94 -> <=80 without the min-blocks bound); more useful by the ncu
above: what lengthens a deep-level block's chain from ~9 us to 14-16 us (per-item work, load latency under the
concurrent SplitBatch / gen-bit traffic, item imbalance within a block) -- e.g. a per-block duration histogram with
%globaltimer stamps, or items sorted so a block's 32 items have similar work.
Nothing from H2 is committed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mechanism: the level apply's remaining non-floor time is serialized or redundant memory traffic at fixed points of the chain, not rows in flight (which c116 exhausted: 16-row builds were slower, gen-bit moved -3% at 2x rows in flight). Removing the root level's identity index reads (gen-bit and split-inner compute row = leaf_data_start + position when the host knows the main array is still the identity) cuts the root gen-bit by ~11 us and the root split-inner by ~2 us, and a load-first, single-store, 64-bit-packed aggregate prefix in a block sized to the largest split cuts the aggregate by ~12 us/round: together -25 to -45 us of the 3534 us round, ratio 1.007-1.013 over the parent (quick check vs master >= 1.10). Secondary variant of the same mechanism: the wide fused split-inner at 48 registers (10 instead of 9 resident blocks, L2 throughput 73% -> higher) is worth at most 6 us/round and is measured only if the first two land.
hypotheses.observation: The level apply chain is 0.489 ms/round (13.8%): gen-bit 0.335 ms (10 launches), fused split-inner 0.118 ms (9 x 13.1 us), aggregate 0.036 ms (10 launches, 6.9 us at the root, 2.5 us deep). Per level (parent trace, [local artifact omitted]): gen-bit L0 = 28.3 us but L1 = 16.1 us although L1 has nearly the same rows; the root is the one level where the main index array is the identity permutation the tree start wrote, so the L0 gen-bit's 21.8 MB index read (and the L0 split-inner's re-read, 11.1 us) is a load of a known value. L1-L2 gen-bit sit at the DRAM floor of the 4-byte index read (~14 us), L5-L9 at one 32-B nibble sector per row (c116 ncu: 88-91% DRAM). Split-inner at L7/L8 (my ncu): L2 throughput 73%, L2 hit 100%, DRAM 6%, 3.1-3.4 waves of 128-thread blocks at 75% theoretical / 65% achieved occupancy: an L2-bandwidth kernel over all rows (active + newly terminal), <= 27 us/round of headroom. The aggregate (36 us/round) is one 1024-thread block per split doing a global load -> add -> store chain per entry (6.9 us for the root's 5337 chunk entries). Sibling branches measured both fixes on neighbouring lineages but neither is in this tree: kevo/c115 (commit c4657d50, parent c111 = the same wide builds as this tree) root_apply_direct, same-binary A/B 1.0084, root gen-bit 29.5 -> 17.2 us and root split-inner 17.2 -> 15.2 us; kevo/c114 (commit 498ebe2b, parent c103) aggregate_load_first, aggregate 36.1 -> 24.4 us/round.

Port, in this order, each as its own commit, each gated by its existing cuda_plan key (both default on; no new literal constants are needed: both are already parameterised, see the review notes in their commit messages):

Expected nsys: gen-bit L0 28.3 -> ~17 us, split-inner L0 11.1 -> ~9 us.
2. `aggregate_load_first` from kevo/c114 commit 498ebe2b (files: include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h key after root_apply_direct's; src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu: new HybridAggregateBlockOffsetLoadFirstKernel<kPerThread> next to HybridAggregateBlockOffsetBatchKernel at line ~1597, the launch choice replacing the launch at line ~2390 in LaunchSplitLevelBatchedKernels: block = smallest multiple of 32 covering the level's largest num_blocks + 1 entries at kPerThread per thread, tiers 1/3/6 entries per thread, splits above the cap keep the original kernel). `git apply -3` leaves conflicts in falcata_plan.h (key list: insert the two lines) and in cuda_data_partition.cu near the fused kernel's `__launch_bounds__` line (~2161, context only: keep this tree's line) and at the aggregate launch (keep c114's if/else around this tree's launch arguments, which include `cuda_level_smaller_counts_.RawData(), nullptr`). The per-level max num_blocks is already known on the host (descs are built in cuda_data_partition.cpp ~line 475; `max_num_blocks` is a parameter of LaunchSplitLevelBatchedKernels, currently `(void)`-ed). Expected nsys: aggregate 36 -> ~24 us/round. Note the second launch site at line ~2561 (the single-split path) stays unchanged.
3. Quick check after each step (300 rounds, md5 identical required); deciding number: same-binary A/B with `--plan-stock root_apply_direct:off,aggregate_load_first:off` (see [local artifact omitted] for the invocation shape), 300 rounds x 2 pairs; then the lattice gate (both keys change which kernel runs on every dataset with the hybrid batched apply, so the 50-round guards matter: c115 ran covtype/year/higgs/missing/numerai-example md5-identical).
4. If both land with budget left, the secondary variant: `HybridSplitInnerFusedBatchRowsKernel` with a template `MIN_BLOCKS` in `__launch_bounds__(BLOCK, MIN_BLOCKS)`, instantiated for MIN_BLOCKS = 0 and for the device-independent maximum `kMaxThreadsPerBlockLimit / BLOCK` candidates chosen at runtime: the host queries cudaFuncGetAttributes (numRegs, localSizeBytes) and cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor for each instantiation and takes the one with the most resident rows per SM among those with localSizeBytes == 0 (no spill), under a new key `apply_inner_minblocks` (default on). c116 measured MIN_BLOCKS = 10 at 48 registers with an 8-byte stack: that instantiation would be rejected by the spill check, so this variant may select nothing on this GPU; it is then a documented no-op, not a failure.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mechanism: the kernel is bound by uncoalesced single-byte global loads (one 32 B sector per useful byte), not by bandwidth. Staging the row-major tile through shared memory so that a warp reads 32 consecutive columns of a row (one sector per 32 bytes), then binning and packing from shared memory with the group-major output written coalesced, cuts the kernel from 28 ms to <= 8 ms per chunk (1040 ms -> <= 300 ms). Once the GPU is no longer the co-critical stage, BinChunk becomes host-bound at about the staging + scatter sum (~1.5 s): BinChunk 2.05 s -> <= 1.6 s, construct 5.6 s -> <= 5.15 s, ratio >= 1.08.
hypotheses.observation:
- Parent profile: CUDADenseBinChunkKernel 1040 ms over 37 launches (28 ms each) = 18% of the 5690 ms construct; GPU busy 33%.
- My timers on master (3 constructs, stderr PROFBIN): BinChunk total 2.05 s of a 5.6 s construct: input staging of row-major int8 rows into pinned h_in 0.87 s (19.4 GB), wait on D2H 0.41 s, host scatter into bin storage 0.58 s (9.6 GB), remainder ~0.2 s.
- The kernel's row-major int8 path (LUT) gives each lane one byte per load: a warp's 32 threads read 32 different rows (stride ncol bytes), so one load instruction touches 32 sectors for 32 useful bytes, and the grid is 3525 groups x pairs/256 blocks of tiny threads.
hypotheses.plan:
- include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h: new key `dense_bin_tile` (default on; off restores the per-lane kernel).
- src/io/cuda/cuda_dense_binner.cpp: ctx flag tile_ok_ = key on && LUT dtype && every group has exactly one column (multi-column groups keep the per-lane kernel: last-non-skip-wins across columns); col->group table (new device array, -1 for unused columns); BinChunk uses the tile kernel for row-major input only (column-major reads are already coalesced).
- src/io/cuda/cuda_dense_binner.cu: CUDADenseBinTileKernel<T> (tile 256 rows x 32 cols in shared memory, 256 threads, pair index fastest for the output writes), same parity/validity/width semantics as CUDADenseBinChunkKernel; LaunchCUDADenseBinTileKernel.
- src/io/cuda/cuda_dense_binner.hpp: declarations, tables gets col_group.
hypotheses.verdict_text:

Mechanism check (timers before/after on the numerai build): the GPU wait inside BinChunk fell 0.41 s -> 0.00 s and BinChunk 2.05 s -> 1.75 s; the kernel itself was not measured with nsys (the untried step), so the kernel-time part of the mechanism is inferred from the wait disappearing.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Staging a [64 rows x 128 columns] tile through shared memory with coalesced row reads (threads walk consecutive columns of one row), then binning from shared memory with the original pair-per-thread output writes, cuts the kernel from ~1040 ms to ~100-150 ms of GPU time per construct. The H2D/bin/D2H pipeline then stops being GPU-bound at ~1.0 s of span; the expected construct ratio vs master is >= 1.10 (on top of k007's pool work the GPU side would no longer be the limit). hypotheses.observation:
- Parent profile: CUDADenseBinChunkKernel<signed char,1,1> = 1040 ms of 1888 ms GPU busy (17.4% of the 5991 ms construct), 37 launches, 28.1 ms each.

- Cause (source): thread = row pair, group = one column; each thread's `in[row*ncol+col]` loads 1 byte at a 3555-byte stride from its neighbours, so each warp touches 32 sectors for 32 useful bytes.
- H2D 822 ms, D2H 365 ms, cudaHostAlloc 63.7 s summed over threads (per-group bin buffers; k007 owns that).

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Page-locking the caller's own buffer directly (`cudaHostRegister`, once per
`BinChunk` call, covering that call's rows) and DMA'ing the H2D upload
straight from it removes this 19.4 GB host memcpy entirely for the row-major
host-input path, replacing N per-chunk memcpy's with one process-wide
page-table operation. If the page-table cost of registering ~19.4 GB is
smaller than the memcpy it replaces, construct wall time should drop by a
double-digit percentage of the ~2041 ms host-only share -- expect e2e ratio
(stock/candidate) >= 1.08 (i.e. candidate construct time <= 93% of stock).
hypotheses.observation:
Parent profile (3759 ms construct wall, numerai53bench-construct): GPU busy
only 46% (1718/3759 ms). H2D copies total 19.47 GB, matching the full raw
int8 matrix read exactly once by the DMA engine. But before every one of the
37 chunk uploads, `CUDADenseBinnerCtx::BinChunk` (row-major, host-resident
branch) first runs an OMP-parallel `StreamMemcpy` of that chunk from the
caller's plain numpy buffer into a pinned `h_in_[b]` staging block, because
`cudaMemcpyAsync` needs a page-locked source to be truly async/fast. For a
row-major chunk this copy does no reshaping at all -- the source bytes are
already exactly the layout the device wants -- so this is a second,
CPU-bandwidth-bound 19.4 GB pass over the whole matrix whose only purpose is
page-locking.
hypotheses.plan:
- `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h`: new `cuda_plan` key `construct_pin_direct`
  (bool, default on), gated like the other GPU-construct keys.
- `src/io/cuda/cuda_dense_binner.hpp` / `.cpp`: in `CUDADenseBinnerCtx::BinChunk`,
  when `!data_is_device && is_row_major && construct_pin_direct`, try
  `cudaHostRegister` on the caller's buffer for this call's row range; on
  success, skip the per-chunk `StreamMemcpy` into `h_in_[b]` and
  `cudaMemcpyAsync` straight from the registered caller pointer into
  `d_in_[b]`; `cudaHostUnregister` after the final stream syncs (before the
  caller may reuse/free the buffer). On registration failure, clear the error
  and fall back to the old staging-copy path unchanged. `EnsureInputStaging`
  split so `h_in_` (staging) is only allocated when actually needed;
  `d_in_` (device buffer) is always allocated for the host-input path as
  before. No bytes or layout change: bit-identical by construction (same
  bytes DMA'd to the same device buffer).
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Mechanism, by construction (read from the committed code, not just inferred):
when `pin_direct` resolves true, the branch that runs the 19.4 GB OMP-parallel
`StreamMemcpy` into `h_in_[b]` is the `else if (is_row_major)` arm of an
`if (pin_direct) / else if (is_row_major) / else` chain -- provably not taken
-- replaced by exactly one `cudaHostRegister` + one `cudaHostUnregister` per
`BinChunk` call (one call total on this one-shot path) instead of 37
multi-threaded memcpy's. H2D/D2H byte totals and the kernel are unchanged (same
bytes, same device buffer), so this is the only mechanism the change touches.
Falsification bar (>=1.08, same-binary A/B) is cleared: measured 1.119. The
stock-vs-candidate ratio (1.201) is close to and above that, as expected (it
also carries whatever small, unrelated build-to-build drift exists between
the two venvs/binaries). md5-identical on both the targeted workload, its
construct guard (covtype-construct), and the full 224-cell lattice gate
(dtypes, bagging, categorical, sparse, multi-output, reference datasets).
Three variants measured directly (stock-vs-candidate e2e, same-binary A/B,
covtype guard) plus the lattice gate; the fourth (live byte-count/host-time
instrumentation) could not be collected in reasonable time because of GPU
queue contention from unrelated workers, not because of any problem with the
change -- noted under Untried rather than guessed at.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mechanism: generalise the pair-code view from a fixed 5-bit code (6 codes per 32-bit word) to a code width chosen per tree from the largest joint cell count of its byte slots: 5 bits where max(lo_span*hi_span) <= 32, 6 bits (5 codes per word) where <= 64, 8 bits (4 codes per word) where <= 256 (every 4-bit pair). The fill writes the view at that width, the code-word construct reads it with one thread per word, the per-byte code-view reader decodes at that width. Expected effect: on numerai53bench-nan-deep-stoch the construct moves from the 244-us generic kernel to the word kernel reading 160-B rows (178 slots -> 36 six-bit-code words padded to 40; vs 128 B at 5 bits, +25% bytes at a kernel ~70% of DRAM peak): ~170-185 us/launch, i.e. construct 2.20 -> ~1.6 ms/round, and the fill writes 160 instead of 178 B/row and takes the CODE5 branch (1.34 -> ~1.2 ms as deep-stoch's 1.13): round 5.04 -> ~4.3 ms, cell ratio ~1.12-1.17. numerai53bench-deep-stoch: the 5-bit path stays byte-for-byte the same code (ratio 1.00). covtype, higgs: no compact view, 1.00. Hidden cells with 4-bit columns of 6-16 bins or with missing bins gain the same way; cells already at <= 5 bins or at 8-bit groups are untouched. No compile cost (templates, AOT). Predicted score (4 visible): ~1.03-1.04; with hidden NaN/6-16-bin cells more.
hypotheses.observation:
- numerai53bench-nan-deep-stoch runs 5.04 ms/round against 3.79 ms for numerai53bench-deep-stoch on the same rows and columns; the difference is almost entirely the construct (2.20 vs 1.27 ms/round) and the fill (1.34 vs 1.11 ms/round).
- On the NaN cell the construct runs `CUDAConstructDiscretizedHistogramPairJointBatchedKernel<0,0>` (per-byte nibble gather, 244 us/launch, 540 launches per 60 rounds) and the fill its nibble instantiation `<1,0>`; on deep-stoch the code-word kernel `...PairJointCode5WordKernel<4>` (144 us/launch) and the CODE5 fill `<1,1>`.
- The reason is the shape gate `lo_span * hi_span <= 32` (`src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cpp:1150`): 6-bin columns (5 values + missing bin) paired together give 36 joint cells, which do not fit the 5-bit pair code. One such pair anywhere in the tree's sampled columns disables the code view for the whole tree. 55% of the NaN cell's columns are 6-bin, so no tree gets it.
- covtype and higgs (255-bin columns) build no 4-bit compact view: unaffected.
hypotheses.plan:
cuda_plan key: `pair_code_wide` (bool, default true; `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h` next to `pair_code5`, with its `Lookup` entry). Off = today's gate (5-bit only), on = the width chosen per tree. The same-binary A/B is this key on vs off on the NaN cell.

Files and functions (all in `src/treelearner/cuda/`):
1. `cuda_histogram_constructor.hpp:173-181`: `Code5RowWords(row_bytes)` -> `Code5RowWords(row_bytes, code_bits)` with codes per word = `32 / code_bits` (6, 5, 4), same 8-word padding (`kCode5RowWordAlign`). Add member `int code5_bits_ = 5;` next to `code5_row_words_` (line 1183). Every caller of `Code5RowWords` (grep: .cpp:1155, .cu:2956, .cu:3110, .cu:5725) passes the width.
2. `cuda_histogram_constructor.cpp:1126-1163` (the gate in the fused fill setup): instead of `code5 = lo_span*hi_span <= 32 && (...)`, track `max_cells = max(lo_span*hi_span)` over all slots and `odd_hi_ok = ((k % 6) % 2 == 0 || hi_span <= 7)` over all slots; then `code_bits = max_cells <= 32 && odd_hi_ok ? 5 : (pair_code_wide ? (max_cells <= 64 ? 6 : 8) : 0)`; `code5 = code_bits > 0`. Keep the rest of the gate (one-run layout, buffer fit: `code_row_words = Code5RowWords(total_byte_slots, code_bits)`; the `<` nibble-bytes check stays, so 8-bit codes engage only when the padded code row is shorter than the nibble row, i.e. rarely: that is fine, 6-bit is the target). The code table stays `span(hi) | has_hi<<5` (span < 32 holds for 4-bit columns). Pass `code_bits` into `LaunchCompactFill` (its signature around .cu:1060-1131) and store `code5_bits_ = code_bits` next to `code5_row_words_` (line 1229). Extend the `Log::Info` at line 1186 with the width (the diag line the quick check of engagement reads).
3. `cuda_histogram_constructor.cu` fill kernel `CUDAFillCompactData4BitTiledRootHistKernel<SLOT_MAJOR, CODE5>` (line ~533): change `bool CODE5` to `int CODE_BITS` (0 = none, 5 = today's two dp4a pair branches unchanged, bit for bit); for CODE_BITS 6 and 8 take ONLY the third branch (line ~918, the scalar per-slot pack: `code = (b & 0xf) * (e & 31) + (has_hi ? b >> 4 : 0)`) generalised to `kCodes = 32 / CODE_BITS` slots per word and `code << (CODE_BITS * j)`. Instantiate `<SLOT_MAJOR, 0|5|6|8>` in the launcher at line ~1080 (switch on `code_bits`); the `+16` shared slack and `code5` bools there become `code_bits > 0`.
4. `cuda_histogram_constructor.cu` code-word construct: `Code5WordAdd` and `ConstructDiscretizedHistogramPairJointCode5WordInner` (3065-3180), the `__global__` kernel at 3371 and `PairJointCode5WordKernel`/`PairJointCode5WordRows` (3469-3500): add template `int CODE_BITS` (kCodes = 32/CODE_BITS, `joint_base[kCodes]`, `valid_mask` over kCodes, slot `b = kCodes*k + j`, mask `(1u << CODE_BITS) - 1`, `row_words = Code5RowWords(row_bytes, CODE_BITS)`). The kernel-function selector takes `code5_bits_`; `PairJointCode5WordRows` memo key gains the width (its `cudaFuncGetAttributes` is per instantiation).
5. `cuda_histogram_constructor.cu:2831-2850` and `2948-2960` (`ConstructPairRowBatch<N,PREFETCH,CODE5>` and its caller: the per-byte gather over the code view; the instantiation is `CUDAConstructDiscretizedHistogramPairJointCappedKernel<false, 12, 48, true>` = `PairJointCapped().gather_code5` at ~3436-3448, its last template bool becomes the width 0/5/6/8; used when the word kernel does not launch, e.g. a grid-y overflow): `data + 4 * (byte_idx / kCodes)`, `row_stride = 4 * Code5RowWords(row_stride, bits)`, `row_hi = bits * (byte_idx % kCodes)`, cell mask `(1u << bits) - 1`. Simplest: pass `code_bits` as a kernel argument through the existing `hi_span`-style parameters (it is runtime-uniform), or template it like the word kernel; the per-byte path is rare on these cells, a runtime value is acceptable there.
6. Level dispatch `.cu:5717-5745`: `Code5RowWords(compact_row_bytes_, code5_bits_) == code5_row_words_`, pass the width to `PairJointCode5WordRows` and pick the instantiation by `code5_bits_`. Grep every `% 6`, `/ 6`, `* 5`, `& 31u`, `[6]` in the CODE5 comments/code of the .cu (listed by `grep -n "code5\|Code5" ...cu`) and make each width-generic; `EnsureNibbleView` (.cpp:1309-1325) rewrites the nibble view from the column-major store, not from the code view, so it needs nothing.

Variants, in order:
- V1: 6-bit via the scalar per-slot fill branch (above). Quick check on the NaN cell alone first (`--cell numerai53bench-nan-deep-stoch@500`), then all four.
- V2: if the NaN fill got slower than 1.34 ms (the scalar pack costs ~5 ops/slot vs ~2.3 for the dp4a pair trick; the fill is 62% issue-busy): a per-slot dp4a pack for width != 5: per word, two funnel-shifted source words (8 bytes cover 5 slots), `lx/hx` nibble split as in the 5-bit branch, per slot j `code_j = Code5Dot4(hx[j>>2], has_hi<<8*(j&3), Code5Dot4(lx[j>>2], span<<8*(j&3), 0))`, `w |= code_j << (CODE_BITS*j)`; keeps `pair_code5_pack2`'s 8-byte stores.
- V3: the block row at 6 bits is 40 words (blockDim.x = 40, warps straddle two rows: no idle lanes, but each warp's code load spans two 160-B rows instead of one 128-B row, and the padding to 8 words wastes 4 of 40 words = 10% of the bytes read). If the construct's gain per launch is below ~20%, try (a) padding only to 2 words (8-byte stores) for width != 5 so 36 words = 144 B/row, or (b) `kCode5RowWordAlign` = warp size so a row is whole warps.
- V4 (shape extension): the 8-bit width for 9-16-bin columns engages only when the padded code row is < nibble row; drop the padding for width 8 (row words = ceil(slots/4)) so it fits exactly in the live buffer, and check the gate `<=` there.

Quick check must show: md5_identical true on all four cells; NaN cell ratio >= 1.08. Engagement check: cells.py runs with verbose -1 (the `Log::Info` at .cpp:1186 is silent), so run the nsys command of the brief on numerai53bench-nan-deep-stoch --rounds 20 and confirm `...PairJointCode5WordKernel` appears and the fill is the `<1, 6>` (or `<true, 6>`) instantiation; a temporary `fprintf(stderr, ...)` of the chosen width is fine during development but must not be committed. Also run the lattice gate (`tests/gates/lattice.py --check`) before committing: it covers other 4-bit shapes (2-16 bins, missing bins); deep-stoch, covtype, higgs within noise (same code paths).

Risks to md5 identity seen:
- The code must equal the joint cell the per-byte kernel uses (`lo * span(hi) + hi`, `hi = 0` without a high column); the word kernel's `joint_base[j]` must index slot `kCodes*k + j` with the same partition walk as today (the per-byte-slot partition offsets). Integer joint sums are order-free; wrong slot or wrong width mapping is a wrong histogram, caught by the md5 run.
- Slots past the row (`slot >= num_slots`) must pack 0 and must not be in `valid_mask` (a non-zero code there would add to joint 0).
- The 5-bit dp4a pair branches have the `(k % 6) % 2 == 0 || hi_span <= 7` precondition; the generalised gate must keep it for width 5 only.

nodes.observation:
- numerai53bench-nan-deep-stoch runs 5.04 ms/round against 3.79 ms for numerai53bench-deep-stoch on the same rows and columns; the difference is almost entirely the construct (2.20 vs 1.27 ms/round) and the fill (1.34 vs 1.11 ms/round).
- On the NaN cell the construct runs `CUDAConstructDiscretizedHistogramPairJointBatchedKernel<0,0>` (per-byte nibble gather, 244 us/launch, 540 launches per 60 rounds) and the fill its nibble instantiation `<1,0>`; on deep-stoch the code-word kernel `...PairJointCode5WordKernel<4>` (144 us/launch) and the CODE5 fill `<1,1>`.
- The reason is the shape gate `lo_span * hi_span <= 32` (`src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cpp:1150`): 6-bin columns (5 values + missing bin) paired together give 36 joint cells, which do not fit the 5-bit pair code. hypotheses.hypothesis:
Splitting a mixed-width dataset's tasks, once at Init (static per-feature bin width, not re-split per tree),
into a <=32-scan-position bucket and a wider bucket, and launching the narrow bucket through a new kernel
instantiation that never compiles the 8-position-per-lane body (a compile-time branch on a new template bool
`NARROW_ONLY`, confirmed by `cuobjdump` to drop register use 96 -> 64) raises that bucket's occupancy ceiling
and should shorten the levels where it dominates. Quantified: covtype's 44/54 columns are narrow, so most of
the kernel's item-work moves to the cheap instantiation -- expect a double-digit percent cut of this kernel's
time on covtype (over 40% of the round), single-digit-percent e2e on covtype; near-zero change on higgs and
numerai (higgs has no narrow columns to split off; numerai never reaches this kernel at all). Compile cost:
none (AOT template, no NVRTC).
hypotheses.observation:
`FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel<32,...>` (the warp-per-task level split finder's wide-bin
catch-all, used whenever a dataset is not uniformly <=8-bin) is 41.5% of covtype-deep-fixed's round and
15.5% of higgs-deep-stoch's round (nsys, 60 rounds each), vs 2.5% on numerai53bench-deep-stoch (parent
profile, which stays on the few-bin G=4/G=8 paths). ncu shows it is not bandwidth- or compute-bound on
covtype (Memory Throughput 1-3%, Compute (SM) Throughput 1.6-37% across levels 0-9) but occupancy-capped:
Theoretical Occupancy is pinned at 41.67% at every level regardless of grid size, and Achieved Occupancy
never exceeds 24.2% even at the deepest, best-populated level. `cuobjdump` shows why: the only existing
G=32 instantiation uses 96 registers/thread (vs 64 for the all-narrow G=8 kernel) because it must be able to
scan 8 positions per lane (`PPL=8`) for its widest task, via a *runtime* branch -- so every item pays the
96-register cost even when its own task only ever takes the cheap 1-position-per-lane path. covtype mixes
44 binary (2-bin) and 10 numeric (up to 255-bin) columns in one dataset; "all or nothing" dispatch sends
every task, including the 44 narrow ones, through the 96-register kernel because of the 10 wide ones.
higgs is uniformly 255-bin (no narrow columns to separate out), consistent with its smaller share despite
being the larger dataset.
hypotheses.plan:
- `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h`: new key `warp_find_split32` (default on).
- `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.hpp`: static host/device index buckets
  (`host_narrow32_task_indices_`, `host_wide32_task_indices_`, `cuda_narrow32_task_indices_`,
  `cuda_wide32_task_indices_`, `num_narrow32_tasks_`, `num_wide32_tasks_`).
- `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.cpp`: `UpdateWarpFindEligibility` buckets every eligible task
  by its static scan-position count (<=32 vs >32) and uploads the two index lists once (same call sites that
  already rebuild `warp_find_max_positions_`).
- `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.cu`: new template bool `NARROW_ONLY` (default false, so every
  existing instantiation/call site is byte-for-byte unchanged -- `if constexpr(false)` is eliminated before
  codegen); `LaunchFindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelKernel` gains a branch, between the existing
  `warp_find_all_narrow_` (G=8) check and the generic G=32 fallback, that launches the narrow bucket through
  `FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel<32,false,false,true>` and (only if non-empty) the wide bucket
  through the unchanged `<32,false,false>` kernel, each over its own item count -- instead of one launch over
  every task. Gate: `!compact_tasks` (feature-sampled trees keep today's single generic launch unchanged,
  since the buckets are static over the whole task list, not this tree's sample) and
  `num_narrow32_tasks_ > 0`. Both buckets write the same `cuda_best_split_info_` buffer at the same
  task-indexed offsets as today: no computation changes, same scan, same exact-first-maximum selection ->
  bit-identical by construction (confirmed: `UpdateWarpFindEligibility`'s per-task scan-width arithmetic is
  copied verbatim from the existing `warp_find_max_positions_` loop).
hypotheses.verdict_text:
1. The one defect-adjacent risk (an extra launch when feature sampling is active, which could have doubled
   overhead unpredictably per tree) is closed by construction: the path is gated off whenever
   `compact_tasks` is true, so sampled trees are provably unaffected (confirmed: numerai/nan ratios are
   noise-band 1.0 in the full quick check, and numerai/nan never reach this dispatch branch at all since
   they stay on the few-bin G=4/G=8 paths).
2. Deciding number: same-binary `warp_find_split32:off` vs `:on` A/B on covtype (the only visible cell where
   the path ever engages), 2 pairs, md5 identical: **0.931** (unconditional) and **1.0007** (gated to
   well-populated levels only) -- both outside or at the edge of the ~0.5% within-arm noise observed, neither
   showing a win.
3. Mechanism check: `cuobjdump` shows the predicted register drop (96 -> 64) really happens; nsys shows the
   predicted per-task item-work really moves to the leaner kernel. The quantity the hypothesis says should
   move (occupancy ceiling) moved exactly as predicted, but kernel TIME did not improve -- the mechanism
   (register pressure limiting occupancy) was real but not binding; the actual binding cost (fixed per-launch
   overhead) is a different mechanism this change could not address, and in variant 1 made worse by doubling
   the launch count.
4. Three measured points covering the design space (unconditional split; split gated to the best-case deep
   levels; the implicit "no split" baseline) plus the numeric bound above, which covers every further
   variant (any other num_pairs threshold, or any finer narrow/wide bucketing) since the floor scales with
   launch count, not bucket composition.

Not committed (`git status` after revert: clean) -- no measured improvement on any cell. Recorded here so a
later worker does not re-attempt kernel-splitting on this finder without first addressing the per-launch
floor itself.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Mechanism: add two intermediate PPL tiers (2 and 4) to the G=32 generic warp-find template's existing per-task runtime
dispatch, chosen from the task's own `num_positions` (already computed at cu:5909, a per-task runtime value): PPL=2
for num_positions <= 64, PPL=4 for <= 128, PPL=8 otherwise (unchanged). `WarpFindBest` is already generic in PPL (the
prefix-scan, prune and warp-wide reduction loops are `#pragma unroll for (i < PPL)` and the final cross-lane reduction
loop already handles any PPL via `off >= (PPL == 1 ? 8u : 1u)`, cu:5724): only the dispatch macro and the
`static_assert` need to accept the new tiers (the assert already allows `G == 32` for any PPL). Expected effect:
cuts the serial lane work for every task whose true width is 33-128 by 2x-4x (same ALU and shuffle instruction count
per position scanned, just fewer unused positions carried through the unrolled loop and the prune/gain pass).
