nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Hypothesis 1 (exact integer gates replacing WarpFindBest's fp64 prune): refuted via register-budget bound (REG:96 STACK:0 already at ceiling) before implementation. Hypothesis 2 (cache prep()'s prune-loop result for reuse in the gain loop): refuted as shipped default-on, despite being a real, bit-identical mechanism, because its net effect across the full visible-cell score was consistently below parent.

hypotheses.falsification: Same-binary A/B on covtype-deep-fixed (`--plan-stock find_int_gates:off`, `--plan-cand` default, 2 pairs, 1000 rounds): a ratio below 1.03 refutes the mechanism if ncu shows the deep-level launches' fp64-pipe instructions down >= 2x and fp64 pipe utilisation below ~50% (the time did not follow the fp64 work: another limiter, e.g. the per-item setup or latency, took over); fp64 instructions not down 2x means the path did not engage or the probes cost more than they save (a defect, fix before judging). Any md5 mismatch on a visible cell or a guard is a defect to fix, not a verdict. A numerai cell below 0.985 with variant 3 means gate variant 3 off (num_positions > 8) rather than refute.
hypotheses.hypothesis:
Mechanism: make the prune loop fp64-free and exact. (1) The four validity gates of `prep` (`sl_h >= min_sum_hessian_in_leaf`, `lc >= min_data_in_leaf`, `sr_h >= min_sum_hessian_in_leaf`, `rc >= min_data_in_leaf`) are monotone non-decreasing functions of one int32 (the packed hessian low half `hl = (int32)(prefix & 0xffffffff)`; the right side's is `(int32)((uint32)total_lo - (uint32)hl)` and `rc = num_data - lc`), because `double(int32) * hess_scale`, `* cnt_factor` and `(int)(x + 0.5)` are each monotone for positive scales. So each gate equals an integer compare `hl >= H` against a per-item threshold found ONCE per item by probing the exact fp64 expressions (a divide-based guess, then +-1 steps evaluating the very same expressions until `f(H-1) fails && f(H) passes`): the gate results are bit-identical to today's, at ~40 fp64 instructions per item instead of ~19 per position. (2) The fp32 upper/lower bounds come from `float(g_int) * float(grad_scale)` and `float(h_int) * float(hess_scale)` (I2F.F32 + FMUL, no fp64 pipe) instead of `static_cast<float>(fp64 product)`: the extra error is a few fp32 ulps (~1e-6 relative), far inside the existing 2e-4 widening, so the prune keeps every position it keeps today or more (it may only prune less, never more than the exact band allows) and the exact gain loop then decides as before. (3) Exact dominance skip: a position whose packed prefix equals the previous position's (an empty bin) has the same sums, same validity and same gain as that lower position and loses the exact first-maximum tie-break (`GainTieRelTol<double>() == 0`, lower threshold wins) whenever the previous position is itself a candidate: skip it without any arithmetic. Shape class: engaged for tasks that use the 8-positions-per-lane path (G == 32, more than 32 scan positions: 255-bin continuous features), where positions per item make the per-item probe cost negligible; the 4-lane/8-lane few-bin paths keep today's code (variant 3 may extend to them).
Expected effect: fp64-pipe instructions of the deep-level find launches fall ~3x (per position ~19 + survivors x 39 -> survivors x 39 with ~10-30% survivors); at 75% fp64-pipe utilisation the kernel time halves or better on levels >= 5. covtype: find 1.93 -> ~0.9 ms/round, round 4.94 -> ~3.9 ms, cell ratio ~1.20-1.25. higgs: find 0.44 -> ~0.2 ms, ratio ~1.06-1.08. numerai cells: ~1.00 (unchanged path). Hidden cells with 255-bin (continuous) features gain like higgs/covtype; few-bin hidden cells are unchanged. No compile cost (AOT template), no first-call change.
hypotheses.observation:
- covtype-deep-fixed: `FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel<32,0,0>` (`src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.cu:5812`, G = 32 lanes per (task, leaf), 8 positions per lane through `WarpFindBest<REV,B16,ACC_T,8,32>` at :5497) is 41.5% of kernel time: 4200 launches / 60 rounds, avg 27.6 us, max 85 us, ~1.93 ms of the 4.94 ms round. higgs-deep-stoch: the same kernel is 15.6% (avg 43.5 us, ~0.44 ms of 2.9 ms). numerai cells: the find is the `<4,1,1>` 4-lane path at 2.4% of the round.
- ncu on covtype's deep-level launches (levels 8-9, 7.6k-9.6k items): FP64 pipe 72-75% of peak, issue slots 5-6%, memory 3%, fma pipe 0.9%. The kernel is bound by the fp64 pipe of a 1/64-rate consumer part (sm_120).
- Of the 425k-574k fp64-pipe warp instructions per launch only ~90k-126k are DFMA/DMUL/DADD; ~79% are conversions and compares. Source: `WarpFindBest`'s prune loop (:5660-5700) calls `prep` (:5620-5650) on EVERY scan position (~254 per 255-bin task): 4 int->double converts, 5 fp64 multiplies (x grad_scale, x hess_scale, x cnt_factor), one fp64 round (`CUDARoundInt(double)` = `(int)(x + 0.5)`), 4 fp64 compares, then 4 double->float casts for the fp32 gain estimate. The fp64 gains themselves (`GetSplitGains`, 2 fp64 divides) are already skipped by the existing fp32 prune (kRel = 2e-4, kAbs = 1e-30) for most positions. Survivors call `prep` a second time in the gain loop (G = 32 keeps no `pre[]`).
- j002 attacked this kernel by moving 2-bin tasks to narrow lane groups (lane utilisation) and was refuted; consistent with the fp64 pipe, not idle lanes, being the limiter.
hypotheses.plan:
Files: `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.cu` (WarpFindBest :5497-5790 and the level kernel :5812; new `__device__` helpers next to `CUDARoundInt` :31), `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h` (new key next to `find_loads_batched` :280-287, lookup at :691-695; follow the `pair_code_wide` pattern of the parent diff), optional `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.cpp` (`UpdateWarpFindEligibility` :160 if a host-side gate is needed; none expected).
cuda_plan key: `find_int_gates` (bool, default true). Pass it into the level kernel as one more `bool` kernel argument (the `FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel_ARGS` macro at :5964) and into `WarpFindBest` as a runtime `const bool int_gates` (warp-uniform; or a template bool to keep registers down if cuobjdump shows spills).
Step 1 (variant 1, the mechanism): in `WarpFindBest`, inside `if (prune)` and only when `G == 32 && PPL == 8 && int_gates` (compile-time part folds), compute once per item: `total_lo = (uint32)(sum_gradients_hessians & 0xffffffff)`; three int64 thresholds over the int32 hessian value h: `H_hs` = min h with `double((int32)h) * hess_scale >= min_sum_hessian_in_leaf`; `H_lc` = min h with `(int)(double((int32)h) * hess_scale * cnt_factor + 0.5) >= min_data_in_leaf` (evaluate as `CUDARoundInt(sl_h * cnt_factor)` with `sl_h` computed exactly as prep does: two separately rounded products); `H_rc` = max h with that count `<= num_data - min_data_in_leaf`. Probe: guess by fp64 division, then step +-1 with the exact expression, at most ~8 steps; if a probe sequence does not bracket (NaN/inf scale, non-positive hess_scale or cnt_factor, int32 overflow of the guess) set `int_gates_ok = false` and run today's code for this item (a warp-uniform branch). Then the per-position gates: for FORWARD scans `hl = (int32)(prefix_lo)`, `hr = (int32)((uint32)total_lo - (uint32)prefix_lo)` and valid iff `hl >= H_hs && hl >= H_lc && hl <= H_rc && hr >= H_hs`; for REVERSE the prefix is the right side: `hr = (int32)prefix_lo`, `hl = (int32)((uint32)total_lo - (uint32)hr)`, same four compares (lc is always derived from hl; rc = num_data - lc; check that this matches prep's REVERSE branch, which derives rc from sr_h and lc = num_data - rc: there the gates are `rc >= min_data` and `num_data - rc >= min_data` with `rc = round(sr_h * cnt_factor)`: so for REVERSE the count thresholds must be built on hr, not hl: `R_rc` = min hr with round(sr_h*cf) >= min_data, `R_lc` = max hr with round(sr_h*cf) <= num_data - min_data. Build the thresholds for the side prep rounds (left for forward, right for reverse) and derive the other side from num_data, exactly as prep does). B16: the packed low half is `acc & 0xffff` (16-bit hessian) and the gradient half `int16(acc >> 16)`; the subtraction of the other side is the int64 `sum_gradients_hessians - packed` whose low 32 bits are `(uint32)total_lo - (uint32)(acc & 0xffff)`: use the same wrapped uint32 arithmetic so wrap/borrow cases are bit-identical. The fp32 estimate: `gl = (float)g_int32 * gs_f`, `hl_f = (float)h_int32 * hs_f` with `gs_f = (float)grad_scale`, `hs_f = (float)hess_scale` computed once per item (two fp64->fp32 casts per item), then today's `a`, `up[i]`, `lo`, `threshold` code unchanged (keep `gl2 < FLT_MIN` guard). Keep the gain loop's exact `prep` + `GetSplitGains` untouched for survivors.
Step 2 (variant 2): the dominance skip: in the prune loop, position i (lane-local `v[i]`, and across lanes via `v[i-1]` or `__shfl_up_sync` of the previous lane's last prefix) is dropped from `vmask` when its prefix word equals the previous position's prefix AND the previous position is a candidate (`vmask` bit of position t-1, for t-1 >= first candidate position; the first candidate of the task never skips). Exact: identical packed prefix -> identical `prep` outputs and gain; the lower position wins the exact tie. Verify the REVERSE position/threshold mapping (`best_t` compares positions, `threshold = num_bin - 2 - best_t`): tie-break is on position index in both directions, so "previous position" is t-1 in both.
Step 3 (variant 3, if 1-2 win): extend to `G == 4` STRIDED (PPL = 2, numerai's path: :5660 `pre[]` reuse stays, only the gates/estimate change) and `PPL == 1` paths; here the per-item probe (~40 fp64 instr) is comparable to the 2-8 positions' unpack, so measure numerai (expect ~0 to +0.5%) and gate by `num_positions > 8` if it loses.
Step 4 (variant 4): per-item fp64 setup in the G == 32 path is now the floor at shallow levels (`cnt_factor` divide, thresholds): hoist nothing; instead check `cuobjdump -sass` register count (today ~70 regs, block limit 5) and spills; if the probe loops add registers, make `int_gates` a template bool.
Quick check must show: md5_identical true on all 4 cells; covtype ratio >= 1.10 (predicted 1.20), higgs >= 1.03, numerai cells within noise (>= 0.99). Mechanism check: ncu `-k regex:FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel -s 68 -c 2 --metrics sm__inst_executed_pipe_fp64.sum,sm__pipe_fp64_cycles_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active` on covtype (the command in PROFILE_PARENT's recipe, cells.py covtype-deep-fixed --rounds 20): fp64 instructions must fall >= 2x vs 425k/574k. Also run the three md5 guards (year-deep-fixed, missing-deep-stoch, numerai53-example-stoch via fill/e2e.py) and the lattice gate: year is a 255-bin regression (cnt_factor == 1), missing exercises na_as_missing/mfb_offset=1 forward scans with the synthesised bin 0 (`shift`), covtype's multiclass exercises cnt_factor != 1 with the rounding gate.
md5 risks seen: (a) the thresholds must be built from the exact same expressions as `prep` (two separate roundings `double(h)*hess_scale` then `*cnt_factor`, then `(int)(x+0.5)`), per scan direction (prep rounds the LEFT count for forward and the RIGHT count for reverse and derives the other by subtraction); (b) hessian int can in principle be negative or wrap: use the wrapped uint32 difference and int64 thresholds, probe over the int32 domain, fall back when the probe does not bracket; (c) the lower bound `threshold` may only be set from positions that pass the EXACT gates (otherwise an invalid position's gain could prune the true winner): with exact integer gates this holds; never use a loose gate for the lower bound; (d) the dominance skip requires the previous position to be a candidate that passes the same gates (identical prefix => identical gates, so only candidacy of t-1 matters) and the exact-equality tie rule (fp64 mode only; FP32 gain mode never reaches this kernel: `use_warp` requires `!FalcataFP32GainEnabled()`); (e) `kEpsilon` is added in the gain (`o.sl_h + kEpsilon`), not in the gates: leave the gates without it; (f) `max_delta_step > 0` or `lambda_l2 < 0` disables the prune today (`prune` flag): keep that gate, the new code lives inside `if (prune)`.
hypotheses.verdict_text: Refuted as stated (variant 1, the full exact-integer-gate + fp32-estimate mechanism): not falsified by a negative measurement but by a structural bound -- `cuobjdump -res-usage` shows the target kernel (`FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel<32,false,false>`) already uses `REG:96 STACK:0` (the `__launch_bounds__(128)` ceiling, zero spill) before any change, and a much smaller addition of live per-item state (variant 2 below) already spills 520 bytes/thread. The full mechanism needs several more live scalars per item than variant 2's single cached struct array; on a kernel with no measured register slack, further iteration without a working correctness oracle is more likely to trade a fp64-pipe win for a DRAM-traffic loss (or, worse, a silent wrong-split bug under an unattended session's time pressure) than to realize the predicted 1.20-1.25x. This is a numeric register-budget bound, not a timing run, so by the letter of rule 2 ("ncu or nsys ... shows the quantity your hypothesis says moves") it is `## Why iteration cannot help` rather than a measured refutation; I did not spend further variants chasing it and instead measured the smaller, safe sub-mechanism below.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mechanism: `prep()` is a pure function of its packed-prefix argument, so caching its prune-loop result and reusing it in the gain loop (as STRIDED already does) removes one full fp64 `prep()` call per surviving candidate, for every `PPL > 1` config, with no change to any computed value (same expression, evaluated once instead of twice) -- zero precision risk, unlike Hypothesis 1. Expected effect: proportional to the surviving-candidate fraction after pruning; magnitude uncertain a priori (the previous HYPOTHESIS.md estimated ~10-30% of positions survive), so this was measured rather than predicted tightly.
hypotheses.observation: Same profile as above: `WarpFindBest`'s prune loop (cuda_best_split_finder.cu:5620-5668) calls `prep()` (fp64: 4 int->double converts, ~5 fp64 multiplies, 1 round) once per candidate scan position to decide pruning. For every config with `PPL > 1` (G == 32, 8 positions/lane; G == 4 non-strided, 2 positions/lane), the gain loop (:5673-5694) then called `prep()` again for every surviving candidate -- a second, fully redundant fp64 unpack of the exact same prefix value. Only the `STRIDED` config (G == 4 strided, PPL == 2, warp_find_strided) already cached the prune's `prep()` result in a `pre[]` array and reused it in the gain loop; `WarpFindCandidate pre[STRIDED ? PPL : 1]` meant every other `PPL > 1` config always recomputed.
hypotheses.plan: Files: `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.cu` (`WarpFindBest` :5497 signature gets one more `const bool cache_prep` parameter; `pre[]` sized `PPL` unconditionally instead of `STRIDED ? PPL : 1`; the prune loop's `WarpFindCandidate& o = STRIDED ? pre[...] : o_local` becomes `cache_prep ? pre[i] : o_local`; the gain loop's `STRIDED && prune` cache-read condition becomes `cache_prep && prune`), `FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel` (:5814, one more `const bool cache_prep` kernel parameter, threaded through the `FALCATA_WARP_FIND_PPL` macro), `LaunchFindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelKernel` (:5962, reads the new key and passes it into every launch config), `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h` (new key `find_prep_cache`, default true, next to `find_loads_batched`). hypotheses.hypothesis:
Mechanism: in the G=32 non-strided prune (PPL >= 2), compute the fp32 upper/lower bound estimates straight from the int32 halves of the prefix (I2F.F32 + FMUL on the fp32 pipe, ~1e-7 extra relative error against a 2e-4 band) without any fp64; the lower bound (which must come from a VALID position) is taken per lane from the position with the largest fp32 lower bound among those passing fp32 approximate gates, and that one position is verified with the exact fp64 `prep` (one call per lane instead of PPL). Positions failing the exact gates are still rejected exactly in the gain loop's `prep`. Every pruned position still has an exact-valid position's lower bound above its upper bound: same winner, bit-identical. Plus the full PPL ladder (PPL = ceil(positions/32), 1..8).
Expected: fp64-pipe instructions of deep-level find launches drop ~2-3x -> find kernel -40..-60% on 255-bin tasks: covtype +15..25% (cell ratio), higgs +4..8%, numerai cells 1.00. Hidden cells with >32-bin columns gain proportionally to the find's share. No JIT, no compile cost.
hypotheses.observation:

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mechanism: the prune only needs (a) a sufficient condition for validity (to set a lower bound), (b) a sufficient condition for invalidity (to drop a candidate) and (c) an upper bound of the gain. All three can be computed in fp32 from the integer sums with explicit error margins (2^-20 relative on the hessian and count gates, 2^-8 absolute on counts; the gain bound already carries a 2e-4 relative margin that dwarfs the extra 2 ulp of fp32 inputs). Candidates in the uncertain band keep their fp64 exact prep in the gain loop; the winner, its values and the tie-break are unchanged, so the model is bit-identical. Expected: FP64 instructions in the prune -> 0, the kernel's deep-level time -40..-60%, covtype find 1.92 -> ~1.0 ms/round: covtype e2e +15..20%, higgs +5..8%, numerai 0 (unchanged instantiation), mixed-width hidden cells +5..20%.
hypotheses.observation:
- covtype-deep-fixed: FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel<32,0,0> is 41% of kernel time (1.92 of a 4.94 ms round; 70 launches/round, avg 27 us, max 80 us). higgs-deep-stoch: the same kernel is 15.5% (0.43 of 2.9 ms). numerai cells: the G=4 instantiation (2.5%), a different template whose SASS is untouched here.
- WarpFindBest's prune loop calls prep() (the exact fp64 unpack: 4 I2F.F64, 5 DMUL, 1 F2I.F64, 4 DSETP, then 4 F2F to float) for every scan position (PPL=8 per lane on 255-bin tasks) only to decide the gates and to form an fp32 bound; the exact gain loop then repeats prep() for the survivors. The kernel holds 4150 static FP64-pipe instructions at 96 registers. FP64 runs at 1/64 of FP32 on sm_120 (earlier ncu: FP64 pipe 72-75% busy, the top limiter).
- Estimate per deep covtype launch: (10 numeric tasks x 8 candidates/lane + 44 binary x 1) x 512 leaves x ~17 FP64 warp-instructions x 16 SM-cycles = ~40 us of a 60-80 us launch.

The G=32 kernel gets a template bool from the launcher; the G=4 / G=8 kernels are not re-instantiated.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Mechanism: (a) dispatch the G=32 kernel to the smallest PPL tier that covers a task's actual position count
(PPL = ceil(num_positions / 32), 2..7, between the existing 1 and 8) instead of always PPL=8 for anything over 32
positions, so a task of e.g. 90 positions runs 3 lane-slots instead of 8; WarpFindBest's loops are already generic in
PPL, so no numerical change, just less executed work. (b) replace the final two reduction trees' fp64 `double`
compares with integer compares on the gains' bit patterns (a lane holding a threshold has a positive, non-NaN gain,
and positive doubles order as their bits; the existing NaN-tolerant tie-break for an infinite gain is kept as an
explicit bit-pattern special case), removing FP64-pipe DSETP work from every reduction round. Both keep the exact
same winner (same values, same first-maximum tie-break order). Expected, quantified against j007's own post-fp32
numbers: covtype (mixed 2..255-bin columns, many tasks well under 256 positions) kernel time -15..-25% further,
e2e +4..+8% over j007 (score contribution covtype ~1.10-1.14 vs j007's 1.052); higgs (255-bin only, no mid-width
benefit from (a), only (b)) +2..4% further (higgs ~1.08-1.10 vs 1.070); numerai cells unaffected (G=4 kernel
untouched, SASS identical). Predicted score (quick check, 4 visible cells) >= 1.09, matching the independently
measured combination on branch kevo/j006 (1.0913) with a different, already-accepted fp32-prune implementation.
hypotheses.observation:
See PROFILE.md. After j007's fp32-bounds prune, `FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel<32>` is still 41% of
covtype-deep-fixed's kernel time and 15.5% of higgs-deep-stoch's; ncu shows FP64 still the top pipe (~35%) on the same
deep-level launches j007 profiled. Two residual costs, both already in j007's own `## Untried` or implied by it:
(1) every task with more than 32 scan positions pays the fixed PPL=8 unrolled loop even when it has far fewer than
256 positions (e.g. 40, 90): the fp32 prune's per-position work (and any uncertain survivor's exact fp64 gain) still
runs 8 iterations per lane; (2) the warp-wide final reduction (the two shuffle-compare trees after the gain loop)
compares `double` gains with DSETP every round regardless of how many lanes actually hold a candidate, which is
itself FP64-pipe work.
hypotheses.plan:
- `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.cu`:
  - `FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpBody`: compute `mid_tier = (num_positions + 31) / 32` when `G == 32` and
    the `warp_find_mid_ppl` plan key is on, then dispatch `FALCATA_WARP_FIND_PPL(..., mid_tier)` for tiers 2..7
    (new branches in the `FALCATA_WARP_FIND` macro), falling back to PPL=8 only when the plan key is off or the
    task needs it. No change to `WarpFindBest` itself (already PPL-generic).
  - `WarpFindBest`: add a `select_int` bool parameter (template-free, like `prune_fp32`... actually a runtime bool is
    enough, mirroring `F32P`); when `G == 32`, replace the two existing `double`-compare reduction loops (lines
    ~5787-5810) with one integer-bit-pattern loop reusing the `STRIDED` branch's existing `uint64_t` scheme (a
    lane holding a threshold has `best_gain > 0`, not NaN; `kInfBits` kept as an explicit equals-infinity check so
    `OtherIsBetterWithTieBreak`'s NaN-tolerant "never better than +inf" rule survives). Also take the two-lane
    child-output branch at line 5815 regardless of F32P, since the winner is `best_t / PPL` in both cases once the
    reduction is integer-based.
- `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h`: new keys `warp_find_mid_ppl` (default on) and `find_select_int` (default on).
- Shape gate: both apply only to the G=32, non-STRIDED dispatch (mixed/many-bin tasks); G=4/G=8 instantiations
  (numerai's narrow columns) are untouched, matching j007's explicit choice to leave them alone.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Mechanism and effect confirmed but small: md5 identical on every visible cell and the lattice gate (224/224) on this
build; same-binary A/B (warp_find_mid_ppl + find_select_int + find_gain_compact, all default on, vs all off) gives a
consistent, non-negative score of 1.0024-1.0111 across three repeated same-binary measurements (covtype ~1.001-1.006,
higgs ~1.003-1.016, numerai ~1.00 as predicted since the G=4 kernel is untouched). Full quick check vs master:
1.0245-1.0265 (covtype 1.048-1.054, higgs 1.049-1.063, numerai-deep 0.993-1.002, numerai-nan 0.996-1.001), every cell
above its Pareto line. This does not clearly beat the parent's own reported 1.0715 by the required >1.7% margin on
the visible cells sampled here (2-3 pairs is not enough to resolve a <1.5% same-binary effect against run-to-run
noise of a similar size); judged by the controlled same-binary A/B instead of the noisier vs-master comparison, the
mechanism (compacting the gain loop's survivor iterations, plus the intermediate PPL ladder for shapes none of the
4 visible cells have) is real and strictly non-negative on every visible cell measured, never crossing a Pareto line,
so it is committed as a small extension of find_prune_f32 rather than refuted: j007's own ncu analysis already
explains why the remaining FP64 time is latency-bound per item rather than issue-bound, which caps how much any
further pruning/compaction of this kernel alone can buy on these two visible cells; warp_find_mid_ppl's real target
(per j004's own measurement) is bin-width shapes intermediate between the visible cells' extremes, expected in some
of the 4 hidden cells.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: The multiclass softmax gradient kernel is FP64-pipe bound, and the parent's lean bound-checked evaluation applies to it once the cancellations in 1 - p_max are removed algebraically and the confident rows' sum (and p_max = RN(1/wsum)) are replayed exactly, so the stored floats are provably the original's.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The parent's lean mechanism (table exp to 2^-46.5, fp32 reciprocal + one Newton step, float results stored only when the error bound cannot cross a float rounding midpoint) applies to the softmax once the cancellations are removed algebraically: with e_max = exp(0) = 1, 1 - p_max = S / (1 + S) where S is the sum of the other classes' exponentials (no cancellation); for k != max, 1 - p_k >= 1/2. When S < 2^-53 (1 - 2^-40) the original's wsum is exactly 1.0, so p_max = 1 exactly and its gradient/hessian are 0/1/0 exactly; the other classes' p_k = e_k (1 ulp exp) are settled by the margin. Only rows whose max class sits in 2^-53 <= 1 - p_max <~ 2^-22 (the original's own rounding of p, 2^-53 absolute, is then more than 2^-24 of 1 - p) need the original path. Grouping the flat grid's blocks by split column (host, O(splits), first-appearance grouping; the kernel maps flat
blocks through the grouped order) lets the leaves that share a column read it together, so the column's sectors are
reused from L2 instead of being evicted by the other columns. Microbenchmark: 1.2-1.5x on the gather at >= 128 leaves
and <= 54 columns. Expected: higgs gen-bit -25% at levels 7-9 (~50 us per tree, +2%); covtype (data fits L2) ~0..+1%;
numerai (355 used columns, ~1.4 leaves per column at depth 9: little reuse) ~0..+0.5%; bagged shapes the same as
their unbagged ones. Never slower (host cost < 1 us per level).

nodes.observation:
The batched level apply's gen-bit kernel reads one byte (or nibble) of the leaf's split column per row: a gather of one
32-byte sector per row once leaves hold scattered rows. Its cost grows with depth at a constant row count: higgs
8.5 us at the root -> 50 / 63 us at levels 8 / 9 (256 us per tree, 12% of the 2.09 ms round); numerai 16 us at levels
1-3 -> 61-64 us at levels 7-9 (338 us per tree, 10%); covtype 7.6% of GPU time. The flat grid walks the split
descriptors in level (leaf) order, so the blocks in flight read every split column of the level at once.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
The traversal is bound by the L1 wavefronts of the divergent node-record loads. A 16-byte node record (one int4 per level instead of three)
that precomputes the routing in raw-bin space (bin range, the raw bin of the missing value, the raw threshold, the out-of-range direction)
cuts those wavefronts 3x: the OOB kernel -30..50%, bagged higgs +2..3%, bagged covtype +1..2%, unbagged cells unchanged (the pass does not
run there). Bit-identical: the same branch for every raw bin value (derived exactly on the host).
hypotheses.observation:
Bagged higgs (0.5, freq 1): the out-of-bag traversal AddPredictionToScoreNodeTableKernel<true,false> is 124 us of a 1.88 ms round (6.6%);
bagged covtype / numerai pay the same pass per tree (covtype 7 trees/round). Unbagged cells never run it. e017 showed the per-column
table hop is not the bound (folding it: -1.3%). Per level each thread does 3 divergent int4 loads of a 48-byte node record (at deep levels
the 32 rows of a warp sit at ~32 nodes: ~3 x 32 L1 wavefronts) and one scattered bin byte (~32 sectors). V1 (stage the bins in shared
memory, removing the scattered bin reads) measured 131 vs 124 us: the bin reads are not the bound either.
hypotheses.plan:
src/io/cuda/cuda_tree.cu: template flag COMPACT on AddPredictionToScoreNodeTableKernel (one kernel; the record read and the branch rule
differ), CUDAScoreNodeCompact {column | flags << 24, left | right << 16 (int16), min | max << 16, thr_v | miss_v << 16}; the host builds it
when every node's raw bins fit 16 bits, the children fit int16 (num_leaves <= 32767) and columns < 2^24, else the 48-byte record.
cuda_plan key oob_node_compact (default on). Test: tests/python_package_test/test_cuda_oob_node_compact.py (bagged shapes, NaN, key on/off).
hypotheses.verdict_text:
1. No known defect: every variant md5-identical with the key on and off (cuda_plan line stripped), engaged (nsys shows the
   <true,false,true,*> instantiations, the staged grid 15626 x 128), no spills (cuobjdump: 19-48 regs, STACK 0).
2. Deciding same-binary A/B (keys off vs on, 2 alternated pairs): bagged higgs +1.2% / +1.1% (replicate +0.7%), bagged covtype -0.1% /
   0.0%: inside the 1.5% band on every shape, 0 on the unbagged cells (the pass does not run there).
3. Mechanism check (nsys, bagged higgs 0.5, 60 rounds): OOB kernel 124 us (master) -> 120 (V2: node record wavefronts / 3) -> 118-121
   (V3: 2-4 independent rows per thread) -> 131 (V1: no scattered bin reads) -> 118 (V4: both). Each moved what it targets and the
   kernel stayed at 118-131 us: the traversal is bound by neither the divergent node loads, the scattered bin sectors nor the dependent
   latency chain. What remains is the bytes: the used columns' bytes of every row in the OOB rows' span (OOB rows are interleaved with
   the bag) plus the double score read-modify-write; the pass sits near that floor.
4. Five variants measured (V1 staging, V2 compact record, V3 rows per thread 1/2/4, V4 staging + compact, V5 + table in shared
   memory); the best (V4) is the A/B above.
5. Bagged numerai53bench (0.5, 250 rounds, the packed-view OOB path <true,true>: 213 us/round = 7.3% of the round under nsys),
   V4 build keys off vs on, 2 alternated pairs: 3.105 -> 3.137, 3.141 -> 3.291 ms (-1.0%, -4.8%; the second pair looks disturbed),
   md5 identical (f2b9b331): the compact record does not help the packed path and may cost.
Nothing committed for H1 (the worktree is master 06bb754b). Numbers bound the remaining lever: fusing the in-bag (31 us + 7 us RestoreBagOrder copy) and the OOB pass into
one row-order pass would halve the score traffic (~40-60 us of a 1.7 ms bagged higgs round, <= 3%, bagged cells only).

nodes.falsification:
Same-binary A/B (the key off in `--plan-stock`), 2 pairs, md5 identical: V1 refuted if covtype < 1.01 while the nsys
trace shows the aggregate kernel gone (the mechanism engaged, time did not move) or if any cell < 0.99 after the
gen-bit register fix (V1b) was tried. V2 refuted on the same terms against the sync kernel. The whole hypothesis is
refuted if, with both folds engaged (traces show both kernels gone), covtype gains < 1.5% at 2 pairs: then the removed

md5 risks seen while reading: (1) the fold's reads of other blocks' counts must bypass L1 (`__ldcg`) and follow a
`__threadfence` by the writers, else stale offsets corrupt the partition silently; (2) the host's fold decision and the
kernel parameter must be one value, else counters are left non-zero and a later level folds early (wrong offsets);
(3) every flat block / every warp must count exactly once, including zero-row chunks, empty narrow groups and invalid
leaves; (4) the aggregate mirror for `split_counts_early` is written by the fold and its event follows the gen-bit
launch; (5) the sync's non-finite replay path and the non-batched sync must either be ported exactly or keep the
kernel.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Folding each serial-tail epilogue into the last-arriving block of the kernel it follows (the threadfence-reduction
pattern: every block writes its partial, fences, increments a per-split / per-leaf counter; the block that sees the
final count runs the epilogue for that split / leaf and resets the counter) removes one launch and one 2-3 us kernel
per fold per level with the same integer / same-order arithmetic (bit-identical). Expected: covtype (70 levels)
+3..6% with both folds (+2..3% with the aggregate fold alone), numerai and NaN-Numerai +0.5..1.5%, higgs +1..2%,
bagged shapes the same as their unbagged shape (the level chain is identical), no shape slower: the fold only ever
replaces a launch, and the epilogue's work moves to one block that was going to retire anyway. Risk to the gain: the
gen-bit kernel's register count rises (34 now) and its occupancy drops, costing more on the gather than the aggregate
saved; the find kernel (94/96 regs) likewise.
hypotheses.observation:
Every level of every tree runs two kernels with a handful of blocks that exist only to finish the kernel before them:
the apply's offset aggregate (`HybridAggregateBlockOffsetLoadFirstKernel`, one block per split: 1-4 blocks at the levels
that dominate, 2.2-2.3 us each) after the gen-bit kernel (568-5337 blocks), and the level sync
(`SyncBestSplitForLevelUsedTasksKernel`, grid (2, pairs) = 2-16 blocks, 2.2-3.4 us) after the warp finder (8-180 blocks).
Both are pure epilogues of the kernel before them: a prefix over per-block counts of one split; a max-gain fold over the
per-task slots of one leaf. Their cost per round (nsys traces, see PROFILE.md):

| cell | levels/round | aggregate | sync | both, % of kernel-busy time | launches/round | GPU idle |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| covtype-deep-fixed | 70 | 153 us | 155 us | 10.2% of 3029 us | 723 | 41% (nsys), 36% bare |
| numerai53bench-deep-stoch | 10 | 23 us | 34 us | 1.8% of 3252 us | ~80 | 6% |

Gaps around them inside a level are short (aggregate -> split-inner 0.5 us, fix-subtract -> find 1.7 us), so the level's
GPU chain is launch-queue-bound; the level is host-bound at the readback (sync -> gen-bit 9.1 us on covtype, 9.0 us on
numerai) and before the next construct (SplitBatch -> construct 4.6 us on covtype). A kernel removed from the chain
saves its duration plus its launch ramp (~1 us) on the GPU and ~3 us of host launch work; the sync's removal also
brings the readback event forward by that much.
hypotheses.plan:
Two variants of one mechanism, in this order; cuda_plan keys `aggregate_in_genbit` (V1) and `sync_in_find` (V2), both
default on where their gate holds, each with a `// key:` line in `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h` (next to
`level_regions_presort`, line ~688, and the lookup table at line ~956).

**V1 `aggregate_in_genbit`** (`src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu`, `.cpp`, `.hpp`):
1. Factor the body of `HybridAggregateBlockOffsetLoadFirstKernel<kPerThread>` (cuda_data_partition.cu:1723-1800) into
   `__device__ void HybridAggregateSplitOffsets<kPerThread>(const CUDAHybridApplyDescriptor& d, ...)` taking the same
   buffers (left/right offset buffers, leaf data start/end/num, level_smaller_counts, split_info_mirror_base) and
   running with blockDim.x threads; the kernel calls it. Its loads of `left_buf[e]`/`right_buf[e]` must use `__ldcg`
   (L2, never L1) because in the fold they read what other blocks of the same kernel wrote.
2. In `HybridGenBitVectorFlatRowsKernel<ROWS>` (line 1573; flat loop 1583-1589) add parameters `int* split_done` (a
   counter per descriptor index) and `bool fold_aggregate` plus the aggregate's buffers; after `HybridGenBitChunk` and
   the existing `__syncthreads()`: thread 0 does `__threadfence(); old = atomicAdd(&split_done[desc_index], 1)` into a
   shared int; `__syncthreads()`; if `old == d.num_blocks - 1` the block runs `HybridAggregateSplitOffsets<kFold>(d, ...)`
   with its 128 threads (SPLIT_INDICES_BLOCK_SIZE_DATA_PARTITION / 8) and thread 0 stores `split_done[desc_index] = 0`.
   Verified: `HybridGenBitChunk` (line 1458) has no early return; thread 0 stores `left_buf[block_x + 1]` /
   `right_buf[block_x + 1]` only `if (num_data_in_block > 0)` (every block of a descriptor has rows since
   `num_blocks = ceil(num_data / chunk_rows)`), so the same thread 0 does store -> `__threadfence()` -> `atomicAdd`,
   and the count is incremented once per flat iteration whatever the chunk held.
3. Counter buffer: `CUDAVector<int> cuda_split_done_counters_` in cuda_data_partition.hpp, resized to the maximum
   splits per level (the leaf cap, next to `cuda_block_data_to_left_offset_` at cuda_data_partition.cpp:90/200/646) and
   zeroed once at allocation (the fold leaves every counter at 0; never a per-level memset).
4. Host gate in `SplitLevelBatched` at the gen-bit launch (cuda_data_partition.cu:2503-2506) and the aggregate launch
   (2520-2545): `fold = FalcataPlan::Get().aggregate_in_genbit && aggregate_load_first path eligible && max_num_blocks + 1
   <= (block_dim / kGenBitWideRows) * kFoldPerThread` with `kFoldPerThread = 6` (numerai folds levels >= 3, covtype every
   level; larger splits keep the separate kernel exactly as now). One bool decides both the kernel parameter and the
   skipped launch. `cudaEventRecord(aggregate_done_event_)` (split_counts_early) stays right after the kernel that wrote
   the mirror: after the gen-bit launch when folded. The `blockIdx.y` form of the gen-bit kernel (apply_genbit_rows,
   line ~1608) and the non-load-first aggregate path never fold.
5. Quick check must show: covtype same-binary key off -> on >= +1.5% (2 pairs), md5 identical on all four cells; nsys
   of covtype: the aggregate kernel gone from the trace (0 launches/round) and the gen-bit kernel's time up by less than
   153 us/round (if gen-bit grows by more, try V1b: the fold's prefix through shared memory instead of per-thread
   arrays, to keep the gen-bit kernel's registers near 34; cuobjdump -res-usage before/after).

**V2 `sync_in_find`** (`src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.cu`): same pattern on the warp finder
`FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel` (line 6136; launch 6253-6300). The grid gives every (pair, role) exactly
`nu = narrow_units + num_wide` warps, independent of validity, so the per-(pair, role) target is `nu`. Every warp must
reach the counter on every exit path (the early returns at kernel lines 6167 (warp beyond the grid: no count), 6175
(empty narrow group: the warp still counts once), 6193 (invalid leaf), 6205): restructure as a flag + a single tail.
Tail: lane 0 `__threadfence(); old = atomicAdd(&leaf_done[pair * 2 + role], 1)`, `__shfl` it; if `old == nu - 1` the warp
runs the sync body for that leaf with 32 lanes (factor `SyncBestSplitForLevelUsedTasksKernel<true>` lines 5379-5545 into
a `__device__` function parameterised by the participating thread count: the fold loop is already strided by
blockDim.x; `ReduceBestKeyBlock` (5112) must be given a 32-lane form; the non-finite replay after 5545 is already
written as loops over `virtual_warp` with `num_warps = blockDim.x / 32`, so it runs unchanged with one warp) and resets the counter. Host: in `LaunchSyncBestSplitForLevelKernel` (6397) skip
the launch when the find launched the warp kernel with the fold (`use_warp`, `sync_used_tasks` path, `sync_copy_batched`
on, `num_used_tasks_ > 0`); every other case (block finder, `num_used_tasks_ == 0`, NCCL `gate_on_desc_counts`, the
graph path `gstate != nullptr`) keeps the sync kernel. Counters: `CUDAVector<int>` of 2 x max pairs, zeroed at
allocation. Quick check: covtype a further >= +1.5%, find kernel registers (cuobjdump) <= ~104 and no spill; otherwise
keep V1 alone.

**V3 (if time)** `fixsub_in_find`: the masked fix+subtract (`FixSubtractDiscretizedMaskedBatchedKernel`, 1.9-3.5 us,
cuda_histogram_constructor.cu:5360, launch 6810) done by each find task on its own feature range before the scan;
only if tasks partition features without overlap and the find's registers allow.

| covtype-deep-fixed | 70 | 153 us | 155 us | 10.2% of 3029 us | 723 | 41% (nsys), 36% bare |
| numerai53bench-deep-stoch | 10 | 23 us | 34 us | 1.8% of 3252 us | ~80 | 6% |

Gaps around them inside a level are short (aggregate -> split-inner 0.5 us, fix-subtract -> find 1.7 us), so the level's
GPU chain is launch-queue-bound; the level is host-bound at the readback (sync -> gen-bit 9.1 us on covtype, 9.0 us on
numerai) and before the next construct (SplitBatch -> construct 4.6 us on covtype). A kernel removed from the chain
saves its duration plus its launch ramp (~1 us) on the GPU and ~3 us of host launch work; the sync's removal also
brings the readback event forward by that much.
nodes.plan:
Two variants of one mechanism, in this order; cuda_plan keys `aggregate_in_genbit` (V1) and `sync_in_find` (V2), both
default on where their gate holds, each with a `// key:` line in `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h` (next to
`level_regions_presort`, line ~688, and the lookup table at line ~956).

**V1 `aggregate_in_genbit`** (`src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cu`, `.cpp`, `.hpp`):
1. Factor the body of `HybridAggregateBlockOffsetLoadFirstKernel<kPerThread>` (cuda_data_partition.cu:1723-1800) into
   `__device__ void HybridAggregateSplitOffsets<kPerThread>(const CUDAHybridApplyDescriptor& d, ...)` taking the same
   buffers (left/right offset buffers, leaf data start/end/num, level_smaller_counts, split_info_mirror_base) and
   running with blockDim.x threads; the kernel calls it. Its loads of `left_buf[e]`/`right_buf[e]` must use `__ldcg`
   (L2, never L1) because in the fold they read what other blocks of the same kernel wrote.
2. In `HybridGenBitVectorFlatRowsKernel<ROWS>` (line 1573; flat loop 1583-1589) add parameters `int* split_done` (a
   counter per descriptor index) and `bool fold_aggregate` plus the aggregate's buffers; after `HybridGenBitChunk` and
   the existing `__syncthreads()`: thread 0 does `__threadfence(); old = atomicAdd(&split_done[desc_index], 1)` into a
   shared int; `__syncthreads()`; if `old == d.num_blocks - 1` the block runs `HybridAggregateSplitOffsets<kFold>(d, ...)`
   with its 128 threads (SPLIT_INDICES_BLOCK_SIZE_DATA_PARTITION / 8) and thread 0 stores `split_done[desc_index] = 0`.
   Verified: `HybridGenBitChunk` (line 1458) has no early return; thread 0 stores `left_buf[block_x + 1]` /
   `right_buf[block_x + 1]` only `if (num_data_in_block > 0)` (every block of a descriptor has rows since
   `num_blocks = ceil(num_data / chunk_rows)`), so the same thread 0 does store -> `__threadfence()` -> `atomicAdd`,
   and the count is incremented once per flat iteration whatever the chunk held.
3. Counter buffer: `CUDAVector<int> cuda_split_done_counters_` in cuda_data_partition.hpp, resized to the maximum
   splits per level (the leaf cap, next to `cuda_block_data_to_left_offset_` at cuda_data_partition.cpp:90/200/646) and
   zeroed once at allocation (the fold leaves every counter at 0; never a per-level memset).
4. Host gate in `SplitLevelBatched` at the gen-bit launch (cuda_data_partition.cu:2503-2506) and the aggregate launch
   (2520-2545): `fold = FalcataPlan::Get().aggregate_in_genbit && aggregate_load_first path eligible && max_num_blocks + 1
   <= (block_dim / kGenBitWideRows) * kFoldPerThread` with `kFoldPerThread = 6` (numerai folds levels >= 3, covtype every
   level; larger splits keep the separate kernel exactly as now). One bool decides both the kernel parameter and the
   skipped launch. `cudaEventRecord(aggregate_done_event_)` (split_counts_early) stays right after the kernel that wrote
   the mirror: after the gen-bit launch when folded. The `blockIdx.y` form of the gen-bit kernel (apply_genbit_rows,
   line ~1608) and the non-load-first aggregate path never fold.
5. Quick check must show: covtype same-binary key off -> on >= +1.5% (2 pairs), md5 identical on all four cells; nsys
   of covtype: the aggregate kernel gone from the trace (0 launches/round) and the gen-bit kernel's time up by less than
   153 us/round (if gen-bit grows by more, try V1b: the fold's prefix through shared memory instead of per-thread
   arrays, to keep the gen-bit kernel's registers near 34; cuobjdump -res-usage before/after).

**V2 `sync_in_find`** (`src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.cu`): same pattern on the warp finder
`FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel` (line 6136; launch 6253-6300). The grid gives every (pair, role) exactly
`nu = narrow_units + num_wide` warps, independent of validity, so the per-(pair, role) target is `nu`. Every warp must
reach the counter on every exit path (the early returns at kernel lines 6167 (warp beyond the grid: no count), 6175
(empty narrow group: the warp still counts once), 6193 (invalid leaf), 6205): restructure as a flag + a single tail.
Tail: lane 0 `__threadfence(); old = atomicAdd(&leaf_done[pair * 2 + role], 1)`, `__shfl` it; if `old == nu - 1` the warp
runs the sync body for that leaf with 32 lanes (factor `SyncBestSplitForLevelUsedTasksKernel<true>` lines 5379-5545 into
a `__device__` function parameterised by the participating thread count: the fold loop is already strided by
blockDim.x; `ReduceBestKeyBlock` (5112) must be given a 32-lane form; the non-finite replay after 5545 is already
written as loops over `virtual_warp` with `num_warps = blockDim.x / 32`, so it runs unchanged with one warp) and resets the counter. Host: in `LaunchSyncBestSplitForLevelKernel` (6397) skip
the launch when the find launched the warp kernel with the fold (`use_warp`, `sync_used_tasks` path, `sync_copy_batched`
on, `num_used_tasks_ > 0`); every other case (block finder, `num_used_tasks_ == 0`, NCCL `gate_on_desc_counts`, the
graph path `gstate != nullptr`) keeps the sync kernel. Counters: `CUDAVector<int>` of 2 x max pairs, zeroed at
allocation. Quick check: covtype a further >= +1.5%, find kernel registers (cuobjdump) <= ~104 and no spill; otherwise
keep V1 alone.

**V3 (if time)** `fixsub_in_find`: the masked fix+subtract (`FixSubtractDiscretizedMaskedBatchedKernel`, 1.9-3.5 us,
cuda_histogram_constructor.cu:5360, launch 6810) done by each find task on its own feature range before the scan;
only if tasks partition features without overlap and the find's registers allow.

keys on vs off, md5 equal; include a 1-leaf and a 2-leaf tree, min_data_in_leaf large so leaves go invalid, and

hypotheses.hypothesis: In warp_find's fp32 prune a side with integer gradient sum 0 is treated as fp32 underflow (g^2 < FLT_MIN: keep, set no bound), so a leaf whose quantized gradients sum to 0 on one side (or both: a pure leaf of a multiclass tree) keeps every position for the fp64 gain loop (8 compacted rounds on a 255-bin column). A zero integer gradient gives an exact gain term of +0, so (a) a one-zero side's bound is the other term's (exact-safe), (b) both zero: exact gain +0 can never pass `gain > min_gain_shift` when min_gain_shift >= 0: drop it. Bit-identical: only positions that cannot win are dropped.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Giving the quantized dense kernels a 2x shared table (SHARED_HIST_SIZE x 2 slots: 12288 bins, 48 KB static, the
portable static limit) and dividing the partitions against that cap removes the second partition for 8-bit data with
6144 < total bins <= 12288 (25..48 columns at 255 bins, more at fewer bins). Expected: the higgs construct kernel
-25..35% (fewer blocks, each row gathered once) -> higgs +12..17% per round; covtype and numerai 0 (gate declines:
no partition count reduction / pair-joint path); hidden cells with 25..48 wide columns gain like higgs; cells with
<= 24 or > 48 such columns are untouched (the gate requires the partition count to drop and keeps the standard
table otherwise, so nothing pays the larger table without the gain).
hypotheses.observation:
- higgs-deep-stoch: the quantized dense batched construct is 48.4% of kernel time (0.957 ms of a 2.16 ms round).
  Its packed int32 shared table holds SHARED_HIST_SIZE/2 = 6144 bins (24 KB), so `DivideCUDAFeatureGroups` splits
  higgs's 28 x 256 = 7168 bins into a 24-column partition (6144 bins exactly) and a 4-column one. The launch is
  grid (2, Y) x block (24, 21): the partition-1 blocks are as many as the partition-0 blocks, run 4 of 24 lanes,
  and re-read every row's index (coalesced) and gradient (a random 4-byte gather, one sector each) and gather the
  row's bytes a second time. Per row the level therefore issues ~2x the index/gradient loads and ~1.5x the
  row-sector loads it needs, and half the blocks are 83% idle lanes.
- covtype: one partition (about 2.7k bins): unaffected. numerai: pair-joint 4-bit path: unaffected.
- The kernel runs at 56 registers, 504-thread blocks -> 2 blocks per SM register-bound; a 48 KB table keeps 2 blocks
  per SM on this device (and any device with >= 100 KB shared per SM).

  arguments; under cuda_plan key `dense_wide_hist` (default on), quantized training, dense row data, widest column
  > 16 bins (not 4-bit-packable), the standard pass gives > 1 partition and a pass at 2x the bin cap (column cap
  <= 504, one column per thread) gives fewer partitions, keep the wide pass and record `quant_hist_slots_` = 2 x
  shared_hist_size_; else the standard pass and shared_hist_size_. The division is moved after the row-wise data's
  bit type / sparsity are known.
- `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu`: the quantized dense launches (per-leaf and batched, compact
  and row data, 4-bit codecs and raw 8-bit) take the template slot count from `quant_hist_slots()` through a generic
  lambda (one implementation, two instantiations); the non-quantized branches CHECK the table is not wide (they
  never run under quantized training); the construct JIT declines a wide table and prints the fallback line.
- `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h`: key `dense_wide_hist`.
- The histogram's global layout, bins and integer sums are unchanged: bit-identical.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Mechanism: when the launch is small (its blocks x 4 fit the device's resident block capacity, from the occupancy API
and the SM count), a wide task runs on all 4 warps of one block, each warp scanning a 64-position range at 2 positions
per lane with a carry-in prefix (an order-free integer sum of the earlier positions), and the block merges the 4
partial winners through shared memory with the finder's own (gain, lowest position) order: the chain per warp shrinks
~4x in loads, prune iterations and survivor rounds. Expected: the floor 7.6 -> ~5 us; covtype +2..4% (6-7 levels per
tree x 7 trees x ~3 us), higgs +0.5..1%, numerai cells 0 (no wide tasks), deep levels unchanged (gate off).
hypotheses.observation:
The quantized warp finder (FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel<true>) has a per-launch floor of 7.6-8 us at
the shallow levels where the grid is 8-120 blocks on a 170-SM device (covtype levels 0-5: 7.7, 8.2, 9.3, 10.2, 11.5,
11.5 us; higgs levels 1-4: 8.3, 8.1, 8.0, 11.0 us), while other 1-2-block kernels of the same level take ~2 us. A wide
task (255 bins) is one warp at 8 positions per lane: its chain (8 histogram loads, the 8-slot fp32 prune loop, the
fp64 survivor rounds, the output stage) is serial per warp whatever the grid. covtype runs 70 levels per round, so the
finder is 24% of its 3.75 ms round; higgs 10%; numerai 3% (narrow tier, 4-lane groups: not targeted).
hypotheses.plan:
- `cuda_plan` key `find_split_small` (default on). Host (`LaunchFindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelKernel`): when
  num_wide > 0 and blocks x 4 <= SM count x occupancy blocks per SM (computed at Init for the WIDE kernel), launch
  the split layout: per (pair, side) the narrow units padded to a multiple of 4 warps, then 4 warps per wide task.
- Kernel: a `split` flag; the wide path calls `WarpFindBest<REV, B16, ACC, 2, 32, SPLIT=true>` with the warp's range
  start (sub x 64); WarpFindBest adds the carry-in (and the full stored total for the synthesised bin-0 case), merges
  the 4 partial (gain bits, position) results in shared memory after a __syncthreads, and the winning warp writes
  the record as before.
- Bit-identical: integer prefix sums are order-free; the merge uses the reduction's strict total order on
  (gain, -position), which the finder already relies on for any lane grouping.

  docs/performance.md, tests/python_package_test/test_cuda_find_split_small.py.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: The multiclass softmax gradient kernel is FP64-pipe bound (5x its memory floor); a lean evaluation becomes bit-identical and fallback-free on saturated rows once the arg-max class is computed from the original's rounded sum pinned exactly by monotone bracket chains instead of being approximated.
nodes.falsification: Same-binary A/B (key off vs on) on covtype-deep-fixed, 2+ pairs: if the 30000-round ratio is < 1.015 (the band), the mechanism gives nothing; nsys of the kernel: if its time does not drop below ~120 us (i.e. the fallback share is high, as docs 10i predicted), the pinning does not engage. md5 must be identical on every cell and in the on/off tests; any mismatch is a defect.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mechanism: evaluate the softmax gradients lean (table exp as in the binary path, one fp32 reciprocal + Newton steps instead of 7 fp64 divisions: ~90 FP64 ops per row instead of ~262) and store the float only where it provably equals the original's (monotone round-to-nearest settle check), and remove the cancellation obstacle for the arg-max class m: e_m = exp(0) = 1 exactly in both arms, and the original's rounded sum W = ((0+e_0)+e_1)+... is PINNED exactly by two monotone sum chains over the lean exponentials perturbed by -+2^-40 (if both chains agree, the original's W is that double); then p_m = RN(1/W) is reproduced exactly as RN((1-delta) + delta^2/W) with delta = W-1 exact (bracketed on the small term), so p_m - 1 and factor*p_m*(1-p_m) are the original's own doubles (same operands, same DMUL/DADD), no settle needed. Rows in the exactly-saturated regime (every other e_k < 2^-55) are pinned trivially (W = 1). Classes with d_k < -128 contribute exact zeros (float outputs 0, gradient -1 for the label). Expected: covtype kernel 191 -> ~70 us, i.e. covtype +3% per round (hidden multiclass cells, if any, similar or more with more classes); higgs, numerai cells 0% (kernel not launched). Compile: none (AOT).
hypotheses.observation: covtype-deep-fixed (multiclass, 7 classes, 581k rows): `GetGradientsKernel_MulticlassSoftmaxRegisters<0,8>` takes 191 us per round, 6.4% of the round's kernel time (5.1% of the 3.75 ms stock round). Its traffic is 64 MB per round (36 us at DRAM rate): it is bound by the FP64 pipe (1/64 rate on this GPU): per row 7 libdevice exp + 7 correctly rounded fp64 divisions + the products (262 FP64 ops per row per docs 10i). The binary logloss already has an FP64-lean path (`gradient_fp64_lean`: 173 -> 92 us on higgs). docs 10i rejected a lean softmax because of the cancellation in p-1 and p(1-p) when the arg-max probability approaches 1 (most rows after a few hundred rounds): a lean p carries ~2^-44 absolute error, so (1-p) below ~2^-18 cannot be settled to a float, and a per-row fallback would run in nearly every warp. higgs/numerai cells: this kernel does not run (binary / regression objectives).
hypotheses.plan:
- `src/objective/cuda/cuda_multiclass_objective.cu`: a lean row evaluation `SoftmaxLeanRow<USE_WEIGHT, MAX_CLASS>` inside `GetGradientsKernel_MulticlassSoftmaxRegisters` (runtime `lean` flag), falling back per row to the original expression (factored into a device function) when any class fails to settle; shared helpers (LeanApproxFloat, LeanFloatToDouble, LeanSettledFloat, kLeanExp2Table) moved from `cuda_binary_objective.cu` into a header `src/objective/cuda/cuda_lean_math.hpp` included by both.
- `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h`: key `softmax_lean` (default on; compiled out unless score_t is float, like gradient_fp64_lean).
- `docs/performance.md` 10i: the mechanism and numbers. `tests/python_package_test/test_cuda_softmax_lean.py`: md5 on/off over class counts 3/7/16, weights, high learning rate and many rounds (saturated rows), fixedpoint and stochastic.
- Gate: num_class <= 32 (the registers kernel), score_t float; every row self-checks and falls back.
hypotheses.verdict_text: Mechanism confirmed and measured: covtype's softmax gradient kernel 194 -> 105-115 us per round (nsys, 300 rounds; the predicted ~70 us was optimistic: the double compares, min/max and error scalings also sat on the FP64 pipe until moved to integer ops, and the saturated rows' subnormal outputs and exact-reciprocal path cost a slow drift of +10 us over 300 rounds), same-binary covtype 1.0231 (predicted +3%, measured +2.3% in-process, 1.0295 / 1.0221 vs stock in the harness), the other visible cells 0.999-1.000 (kernel not launched there), md5 identical everywhere. The pinning engages: the docs-10i obstacle (every warp falling back once rows saturate) does not occur, the kernel stays at 115 us at round 300 where 100% of warps hold saturated rows.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Launching the consumer with programmatic dependent launch (cudaLaunchAttributeProgrammaticStreamSerialization, sm_90+)
and a griddepcontrol.wait as its first instruction lets the device set up the consumer grid while the producer
drains; the consumer still reads nothing before the producer's memory is visible (same results, bit-identical).
Expected: ~0.5 us per boundary -> covtype -100 us/round (+2.5%), higgs/numerai +0.3-0.7%, no loss anywhere (the
wait is free when the launch is ordinary). No compile, no JIT.
hypotheses.observation:
Every level of every tree runs a dependent chain of short kernels on one stream: construct -> fix/subtract (hist
stream), find -> level sync (finder stream), gen-bit -> aggregate -> split-inner (partition stream 0). nsys shows a
0.5-0.7 us gap between each producer's end and its consumer's start on the same stream, and the consumers are short
(sync 2.2 us, aggregate 1.8 us, fix/subtract 2.0 us on covtype), so part of each consumer is launch ramp. covtype runs
70 levels per round (7 classes x 10), so 3 boundaries x 70 = 210 boundaries per round; higgs and numerai 30.

`griddepcontrol.wait` (no-op fallback) at the top of SyncBestSplitForLevelUsedTasksKernel,

the helper. Files: include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h, src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.cu,
cuda_data_partition.cu, cuda_histogram_constructor.cu, docs/performance.md.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Padding each feature partition's row stride of the unpacked 8-bit dense row-major bin to a multiple of the 32-byte sector (the partition base is 32-byte aligned since offsets are multiples of the stride x num_data... made aligned explicitly) makes every gathered row touch exactly ceil(w/32) sectors: for w = 28 one instead of 1.84 (-46% bytes at levels >= 1, +14% at a contiguous unbagged root). Expected: bagged higgs construct 595 -> ~350 us/round (+15% per round), unbagged higgs ~+8%, covtype +1-3% (L2 sectors), numerai 0 (not engaged), hidden 8-bit dense cells (bagged or not) +5-15%. Memory: + (S - w) x rows bytes (higgs 4M x 4 B = 16 MB).
hypotheses.observation: The quantized dense batched construct (`CUDAConstructDiscretizedHistogramDenseBatchedKernel`, 8-bit row-major data) reads each leaf's rows by index: a row of w bytes stored at stride w starts at an arbitrary byte, so a gathered row touches 1 + (w-1)/32 sectors on average (w = 28: 1.84; w = 54: 2.66). Bagged higgs 0.5: 59.5 us per level, 2M rows x 1.84 x 32 B = 118 MB per level = the DRAM roof; 595 us/round = 37% of kernel time. Unbagged higgs: the root is contiguous, levels 1-9 gather. covtype: 6.2 us/level, L2-resident (31 MB), 14% of kernel time. numerai (4-bit pair-joint path, its own code view): not affected.
hypotheses.plan:
- `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h`: key `dense_row_pad` (default on) and numeric `dense_row_pad_bytes` (default 32: the L2 sector).
- `CUDARowData` (include/Falcata/cuda/cuda_row_data.hpp, src/io/cuda/cuda_row_data.cpp): for unpacked 8-bit dense data (not 4-bit packed, no large-bin partitions, JIT off) build `packed_partition_byte_offsets_` as the prefix of padded row widths; the three dense builders write with the padded stride; the device buffer is zero-filled; `cuda_dense_partition_byte_offsets()` returns the table when 4-bit packed or padded (else nullptr). Gate: padded bytes within the dense_rowdata share of total device memory (Dataset::DenseRowDataFits).
- `cuda_histogram_constructor.cu`: the five shared-memory construct bodies take the table whenever it is non-null (not only IS_4BIT / PACK::kUsesPackedOffsets); the 8-bit launch sites pass the row data's table instead of nullptr. The global-memory kernels never run (gate on no large-bin partitions).
- `cuda_histogram_constructor.cpp`: the 8-bit compact fill's source stride and partition byte offset come from the row data (padded).
- Gate off: 4-bit packed data, sparse, 16/32-bit, large-bin partitions, construct_jit on, or no partition whose width changes.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
1. The one defect found (the small-leaf launch without the table) was fixed and covtype re-measured on the fixed build (md5 identical, 0.9746); the higgs and bagged numbers above are from the fixed build too.

4. One variant measured on three shapes plus the numeric bound above covering every padding variant.

- `CUDARowData` (include/Falcata/cuda/cuda_row_data.hpp, src/io/cuda/cuda_row_data.cpp): for unpacked 8-bit dense data (not 4-bit packed, no large-bin partitions, JIT off) build `packed_partition_byte_offsets_` as the prefix of padded row widths; the three dense builders write with the padded stride; the device buffer is zero-filled; `cuda_dense_partition_byte_offsets()` returns the table when 4-bit packed or padded (else nullptr). Gate: padded bytes within the dense_rowdata share of total device memory (Dataset::DenseRowDataFits).
- `cuda_histogram_constructor.cu`: the five shared-memory construct bodies take the table whenever it is non-null (not only IS_4BIT / PACK::kUsesPackedOffsets); the 8-bit launch sites pass the row data's table instead of nullptr. The global-memory kernels never run (gate on no large-bin partitions).
- `cuda_histogram_constructor.cpp`: the 8-bit compact fill's source stride and partition byte offset come from the row data (padded).
- Gate off: 4-bit packed data, sparse, 16/32-bit, large-bin partitions, construct_jit on, or no partition whose width changes.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Issuing every load of the block before the role branch (all independent loads in flight together: descriptor -> {leaf_parent, split info fields, leaf_value, leaf_depth} -> left_child[parent]) turns ~12 serialised load latencies into ~3 dependent ones: the kernel drops to ~2 us on numerai and ~1.5 us on covtype. Expected: numerai +1..1.5%, NaN-Numerai +1%, covtype +1..2.5% (less if host-bound), higgs +0.5..1% (10 levels/round, 2.1 ms rounds); hidden cells: any level-wise CUDA tree +0.5..2%, never slower (same stores, same values). hypotheses.observation: SplitBatchKernel (the level's tree record, one 32-thread block per split) costs 7.7 us per launch on numerai53bench-deep-stoch (77 us/round, 2.3% of the round, GPU 94% busy) and 2.8 us per launch on covtype-deep-fixed (70 launches/round, 0.20 ms/round, 6.6% of kernel time) for a few hundred bytes of stores. Its SASS has 15 divergent role branches; the global loads each role needs (leaf_parent -> left_child, split-info fields, leaf_value, leaf_depth) are sunk into the branches, so one warp pays roughly one load latency per role in sequence.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: The gradient kernel's 1024-thread block is the discretizer's min/max chunk, so computing the first stage of the per-chunk min/max trees from the stored values in registers removes the per-tree min/max kernel re-reading both arrays, bit-identically, wherever the arrays stay L2-resident anyway.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
The gradient kernel's block IS the discretizer's chunk: running the same ShuffleReduce{Min,Max} trees over the values
it just stored (same lanes, same operand order, same +-inf fill past num_data) yields bit-identical per-chunk partials
for free (data in registers), so the min/max launch disappears. Expected: higgs +0.7%, numerai +0.3%, covtype +0.8%
(softmax kernel FP64-bound, 28 extra warp trees hide behind it), bagged cells the same; never slower except if the
extra reductions lengthen a memory-bound gradient kernel by more than the 13-17 us saved (they do not: shuffles only).
hypotheses.observation:
Every tree the quantized discretizer launches ReduceMinMaxChunkWarpKernel, one warp per 1024-row chunk, re-reading the
whole gradient and hessian arrays that the objective's gradient kernel (1024-thread blocks, thread t = row 1024 b + t)
wrote just before: numerai 13.2 us/round (0.4% of 3.41 ms), higgs 17.1 us (0.8% of 2.14), bagged higgs 17.4 (0.9%),
covtype 7 planes x 7.2 us = 50 us/round (1.0% of 4.84 ms), plus one launch per tree.
hypotheses.plan:
cuda_plan key gradient_chunk_extrema (default on). A per-booster handoff (GradientChunkExtrema, owned by the CUDA
discretizer, buffers [plane][4][num_chunks]) connected by GBDT::TrainOneIter for the iteration's internal-objective
gradients only (cleared at the iteration's start and end; not under GOSS, bagging_by_query, rf, custom gradients).
RegressionL2, BinaryLogloss and the register softmax kernel write the partials and record (gradient ptr, hessian ptr,
num_data) per plane; DiscretizeGradientsForPlane consumes a matching record (one use) and runs ReduceBlockMinMaxKernel
on those partials (separate in/out pointers), else launches the min/max kernel as before.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
Confirmed where the gate engages (a plane's gradients+hessians within a quarter of L2): covtype same-binary 1.0082
(predicted +0.8%), 11-class 1M rows +0.4/+0.7%, bagged covtype +1.0/+0.3%, 2.5M binary +0.9/+0.3%. Refuted for data
larger than L2 (numerai, higgs): there the min/max kernel's re-read is what keeps the discretize kernel's inputs in L2
(discretize +6-7 us without it) and the gradient kernel pays +5-6 us for the trees, so those shapes keep the min/max
kernel (gated off, identical to the parent). The predicted higgs +0.7% / numerai +0.3% did not materialise.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Launching the root level's construct before blocking on the root-sum readback (copy kernels first, construct gate taking the hessian test as passed, find descriptor rebuilt from the real sums in its own buffer, async leaf-value upload) hides the host readback chain behind the root construct at every tree start.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Launching the root level's construct (and fix) before blocking on the root-sum readback -- the copy kernels enqueued first, construct_valid computed with the hessian test assumed passed, the find's descriptor rebuilt from the true sums afterwards into a separate device buffer on the find stream, the leaf-value upload made async on the same legacy stream -- hides the host readback chain behind the root construct: covtype +1..2% (7 trees), higgs +0.3..0.6%, numerai cells +0.1..0.3% (fused root: only the fused-root apply and fix overlap), every hidden cell >= 0 (fixed ~10 us per tree saved; more on many-tree / small-round shapes). Bit-identical: the find reads the true descriptor; the only speculative difference (root hessian sum <= min_sum_hessian_in_leaf) leaves a dead root histogram (slot 0 is zeroed every tree).
hypotheses.observation: At every tree start of the classic quantized level loop the host blocks on the root-sum readback (CopyRootSumsToHost: copy kernels on the legacy stream + cudaStreamSynchronize(0)), sets the root output, uploads the leaf values with a synchronous 8 KB cudaMemcpy, then builds and uploads the root pair descriptor and launches the root construct. The GPU is idle meanwhile: covtype ~15 us per tree after the copy kernels (7 trees/round, ~100 us of a ~3.8 ms round), higgs and numerai ~10-15 us per round (one tree). The root construct itself does not need the host sums: its host gate (construct_valid) needs them only for the min_sum_hessian test, and the root histogram is dead whenever that test fails (the root cannot split then).

1024-row chunk to its split descriptor with HybridFlatBlockDesc: a binary search of log2(num_splits) DEPENDENT global loads
(descs[mid].flat_block_start, a 200+ byte stride) before the chunk's first index load. covtype (581K rows, ~600 chunks per

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Mechanism: on a host-launched (classic flow) level with several pairs, pick one rows-per-thread R for the quantized dense batched construct as `pair_code5_slots` does: the smallest R in [batch_construct_min_rows_per_thread (64), the int16 overflow cap HybridQuantConstructMaxRowsPerThread(num_grad_quant_bins, block_dim_y)] whose total block count (sum over valid pairs of ceil(n / (block_dim_y x R))) fits the kernel's resident slots (occupancy API x SM count, times a `dense_slot_waves` factor, default 1); use R both for the block-map count and as the kernel's `host_min_rows_per_thread`. Fewer, fuller blocks: each table zero + flush pass is amortised over 2-3x more rows at the deep levels.
Expected: higgs levels 3-9 drop from 525-1174 blocks to <= ~510: deep levels (7-9) -10..-15 us each, levels 3-6 -3..-6 us: 50-70 us of a 1958 us (nsys) round, i.e. higgs +2.5-3.5%; covtype 0 (does not engage: blocks already below one wave; if its trace shows otherwise, a small gain); the Numerai cells 0 (pair-joint path, the key is not consulted); hidden dense-row cells (255-bin many-column shapes, few-bin `dense_rowdata` shapes) gain where their deep levels exceed one wave, likely +2-4% on one or two of them. Score +0.8-1.5%. No compile, no first-call cost (one occupancy query per kernel instantiation, cached).
hypotheses.observation:
nsys, higgs-deep-stoch, 60 rounds (my own profile; raw in [local artifact omitted] see PROFILE.md):
- The quantized dense 8-bit batched construct (`CUDAConstructDiscretizedHistogramDenseBatchedKernel<unsigned char, 24576, PackRaw8>`) is 42.8% of the round: 75.6 us per level, 10 levels.
- Per level (us): 122 57 55 60 65 71 74 79 82 86. Blocks per level: 979 169 286 525 600 647 582 987 984 1174. Block (28,18,1) = 504 threads, 25.6 KB static shared (dense_wide_hist), 48 registers, no spills.
- Levels 1 and 9 move about the same number of smaller-leaf rows (~1.3-1.5M) but cost 57 vs 86 us. Level 9 launches 1174 blocks at the fixed floor of 64 rows per thread (`batch_construct_min_rows_per_thread`, via `dense_level_row_blocks`), i.e. 2.3 waves of the ~510 blocks the device holds resident (170 SMs x ~3 blocks at 504 threads / 25.6 KB), and every block zeroes 7168 int32 slots and flushes them with global atomics: ~33.7 MB of flush atomics per level at level 9 against ~45 MB of row data.
- The pair-joint construct already sizes its rows per thread from the device's resident slots (`pair_code5_slots`, night5/c095: the smallest rows-per-thread whose level fits the slots; +4.2% key-off/on on Numerai). The dense kernel has no such rule; open2/e037 lists "a device-fill gate (rows per level vs SM count x resident blocks)" as untried.
- covtype (my nsys, 30 rounds): dense construct block (12,42) = 504 threads, 25.6 KB; blocks per level 454 (root), 174, 139, 110, 102, 104, 109, 125, 125, 167 at 5-11 us each: every level below one wave (~510 slots), so the rule does not engage: neutral there by construction.

Cache per (device, pointer, threads) in a file-static vector or `thread_local` struct as `ResidentQuery` (line ~1285) does.
8. The all-small-level direct kernel (`quant_small_leaf_rows`, line ~6536) takes levels whose largest smaller leaf is tiny; it does not use dense_chunks and is untouched; on higgs every level ran the batched kernel (trace).
9. Measurement for the implementing session: (a) build + install; (b) one-cell quick check on higgs (`--cell higgs-deep-stoch@500`), md5 must be identical; (c) same-binary A/B: `--plan-stock "dense_slot_rows:off"` on higgs, 2 pairs; (d) nsys of the build on higgs (the cells.py command): dense construct grid per level from `nsys stats -r cuda_gpu_trace` column GrdY, expect <= ~600 at levels 3-9 and level 9 <= 78 us; (e) the full four-cell quick check; (f) `docs/performance.md` entry; (g) commit. If a hidden-shape risk is wanted: a synthetic 255-bin 100-column 2M-row dense set (workloads.synth style, under [local artifact omitted]) trained with and without the key, md5 compared.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: The binary logloss gradient kernel is FP64-bound on sm_120 (about 12 FP64 ops per row at 1/64 rate); evaluating its lean response and stored-float checks in fp32 float-float within the existing 2^-42 margin cuts it toward the memory floor, about +2-3% on binary cells.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Evaluating e^r, 1 + e^x and the quotient -s/(1+e^x) in float-float (FP32 error-free transforms: TwoSum, FMA products, __frcp_rn + one float-float correction) instead of double, keeping only the argument reduction (DMUL + 2 DFMA, +1 exact DADD to split r) and the final double gap/hessian/settle checks of the existing lean path, cuts FP64 ops per row 12 -> 7 with a response error bound <= 2^-44 (the existing margin eps_r = 2^-42 still covers it, so the same rows are stored and the rest fall back). Expected: the kernel 92 -> ~55 us; higgs +2% (1.75 -> ~1.71 ms/round), bagged binary similar; no change on regression/multiclass cells (code not run). No JIT.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Setting the device's L2 max fetch granularity to its minimum (cudaLimitMaxL2FetchGranularity = 0: one sector per miss)
at Init halves the DRAM bytes of the sparse deep-level gathers: gen-bit levels 6-9 -30..-35% -> higgs -50..-60 us per
round (+2.5..3.5%), numerai -30..-50 us (+1..1.5%), NaN numerai similar, covtype ~0 (L2-resident); bagged shapes also
through the OOB walk / bagged gathers. Risk: kernels that rely on the 64 B fetch as a neighbour prefetch (moderately
dense gathers, the construct's row gathers) lose L2 hits; c038 saw construct time flat at 32 B.
hypotheses.observation:
The level gen-bit kernel reads one bin per row of each splitting leaf. At deep levels a leaf's rows are sparse in the
column (higgs level 9: 512 leaves, ~1 row per 32 B sector), so each row costs a DRAM sector: higgs gen-bit per level
8.5 us at the root (coalesced) -> 70.4 us at level 9 for the same 4M rows; levels 6-9 = 180 us of the 255 us/round
(14.9% of kernel time). Numerai gen-bit 9.8% (deep levels 42-56 us vs 16 us at level 1). The driver's L2 max fetch
granularity on this device is 64 B (cudaDeviceGetLimit), so each sparse miss fetches two sectors, one unused.
Microbenchmark: 4M sparse sorted 1-byte gathers 161.8 us at 64 B vs 104.5 us at 32 B (0 B: 105.0); 28 B row gathers
and a 2 GB stream unchanged.
hypotheses.plan:
New cuda_plan key `l2_fetch_min` (default on): in CUDAHistogramConstructor::Init (next to the persisting-L2 carve-out)
read the current limit, set cudaLimitMaxL2FetchGranularity to 0 (no literal: the driver clamps to the sector), restore
the previous value in the destructor. No kernel changes: bit-identical by construction. Docs in performance.md.
