hypotheses.hypothesis: Mechanism: fold the per-side sync into the finder kernel as a last-arriving-warp epilogue (threadfence reduction: each finder warp, at every one of its exits, fences and increments a per-(pair, side) counter; the warp that sees count == units_per_side - 1 performs that side's sync over the used tasks with 32 lanes, reading the slots through L2 (`__ldcg`), writes the leaf entry and the mirror exactly as the sync kernel does, and resets the counter). One launch and one 2-3 us kernel leave the dependent chain of every level with identical bits (the finite reduction is a total order; the non-finite replay is ported per warp). Expected per cell: covtype-deep-fixed +2..4% (70 x (2.2 us kernel + ~1 us dependent-launch gap) = up to 220 us of 3.7 ms, less the fold's own ~0.5-1 us on the retiring warp), numerai53bench-deep-stoch and -nan +0.5..1% (10 x 3.4 us; the fold over 352 slots on 32 lanes costs ~1.5-2 us, hidden where other sides' warps still run), higgs +1..1.5% (10 x 2-3 us); bagged and hidden shapes: the same level chain, the same gain per level; no shape slower while the finder's register count stays at 96 (the fold is a cold branch; checked with cuobjdump). No compile, no JIT.
hypotheses.observation: Every quantized level launches, on stream 0 in a dependent chain, the warp finder (one warp per task unit, 4 warps per block, 94/96 registers) and then `SyncBestSplitForLevelUsedTasksKernel` (grid (2, num_pairs) x 256 threads: per leaf side, the max-gain task among the used tasks' slots, written to `cuda_leaf_best_split_info_[leaf]` and the readback mirror). nsys: covtype-deep-fixed 70 levels/round, sync 2.2 us x 70 = 155 us = 5.4% of kernel time (plus one dependent launch gap per level), the round 3.7 ms with ~20% host idle, so the finder -> sync -> gen-bit -> aggregate chain is the critical path the host waits on (split_counts_early reads the aggregate's counts). numerai53bench-deep-stoch: 10 x 3.4 us = 34 us = 1.0% of 3.41 ms (352 used tasks per side). higgs: 10 levels, 28 tasks, ~2-3 us each = ~1.4% of 1.75 ms (survey breakdown; not re-profiled). The sync's work is tiny (covtype: 54 slots x 2 reads per side); its 2.2 us is launch, ramp and a 256-thread block reduction for 2 slots per thread. Its finite-gain reduction is a total order (`FiniteGainOrderKey` descending, then lowest slot index: `ReduceBestKeyBlock`, cuda_best_split_finder.cu:5112-5160), so the winner is independent of how slots are distributed over threads.
hypotheses.plan:
Files: `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.cu` (kernel `FindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelWarpKernel` at ~6226-6370, its launcher `LaunchFindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelKernel` ~6371-6445, `LaunchSyncBestSplitForLevelKernel` ~6540-6600, the sync kernel `SyncBestSplitForLevelUsedTasksKernel` 5387-5613 whose fold/replay/store code is reused), `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.cpp` (`FindBestSplitsForLevel` 750-771 calls the finder launcher then the sync launcher back to back; `FindBestSplitsForLevelVector` 734-747 too), `src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_best_split_finder.hpp` (a device counter buffer `cuda_sync_fold_counters_`, int per (pair, side), sized 2 x num_leaves_, zeroed once at Init; a member `sync_folded_this_level_`), `include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h` (new key `bool find_sync_fold = true;  // key: find_sync_fold`, plus its `Field()` line; and an int key `find_sync_fold_max_tasks` default 1024 = 32 slots per lane, the runtime gate on the fold's serial work), `docs/performance.md` (a new subsection next to 10's level-sync entries: what it does, where it engages, the measured numbers), `tests/python_package_test/test_cuda_find_sync_fold.py` (md5 of the model with the key on vs off on a binary, a multiclass and a regression config, feature_fraction < 1 and = 1, and one config that produces a tie or an invalid leaf; model with the key off is the reference).

Steps (V1):
1. Host gate, computed once per level in `LaunchFindBestSplitsDiscretizedForLevelKernel` before the launch and stored in `sync_folded_this_level_`: `FalcataPlan::Get().find_sync_fold && use_warp && gstate == nullptr` and the sync would take the used-tasks kernel (replicate the condition of LaunchSyncBestSplitForLevelKernel: `sync_used_tasks && (used_list || all_tasks_one_block || (!compact_tasks && num_blocks_per_leaf > 1))`) and `(used_list ? num_used_tasks_ : num_tasks_) <= find_sync_fold_max_tasks`. The mirror decision (`leaf_mirror_requested_`, `pinned_leaf_best_split_info_device_`, `leaf_mirror_written_`) moves into a small helper used by both launchers so the fold and the kernel compute the same `leaf_mirror` pointer. `LaunchSyncBestSplitForLevelKernel` returns at once when `sync_folded_this_level_` is set (and clears it): the two decisions are one value (e023's md5 risk 2).
2. Kernel: new parameters (fold flag, `int* fold_counters`, `const int* used_task_indices`, `int num_used_tasks`, `const int8_t* is_feature_used` already there, `gate_on_desc_counts`, `CUDASplitInfo* leaf_best`, `CUDASplitInfo* leaf_mirror`). Restructure the warp body into a `__device__ __forceinline__` function that returns at every current early exit; the kernel then, when the fold flag is set: `__syncwarp(); __threadfence();` lane 0 `old = atomicAdd(&fold_counters[pair_index * 2 + side], 1)`, broadcast; if `old == units_per_side - 1` (units_per_side = nu of the kernel's layout, every warp of the side counts once, including padding warps, empty groups, unused features and invalid sides; the split_wide sub-warps count after their block merge and the write, i.e. after the `__syncthreads` of the merge), the warp runs `SyncFoldSide(...)`: the fold of SyncBestSplitForLevelUsedTasksKernel's BATCHED path over positions lane, lane+32, ... with `__ldcg` loads of `is_valid`/`gain`, the per-lane selection by `(FiniteGainOrderKey desc, read_index asc)` (equivalent to the kernel's first-max-then-lowest-index result since the block reduction already breaks ties by lowest read_index), a warp-only `ReduceBestKey` (the shuffle half of ReduceBestKeyBlock), the identical store code (`LoadSplitInfoFields`/`StoreSplitInfoFields`, `inner_feature_index`, `is_valid`, `MirrorLeafBestSplitEntry` adapted to one warp), the `leaf_index < 0` / `!leaf_valid` branches exactly as the kernel; the non-finite case (`__any_sync` of non_finite) runs a per-warp port of the replay path 5560-5613 with num_warps = 1 (read it line by line; its double compares and merge order must be reproduced); finally lane 0 stores 0 to the counter (`__threadfence()` first). Warps with `warp >= nu * num_pairs * 2` do not count.
3. Build; `cuobjdump -res-usage` on both finder instantiations: registers must stay 94/96 and spills 0. If they rise, V2.
4. Quick check on all four visible cells (the brief's command); md5 identical is mandatory. Then same-binary A/B `--plan-stock find_sync_fold:off` on covtype and one Numerai cell, 2 pairs. Then the lattice gate. Also a bagged covtype or higgs run with the key on/off (md5 and ms) in a script under the scratch dir.

Variants, in order: V1 as above. V2 (if registers rose or covtype did not gain): the fold body as a `__noinline__` device function so the hot path's allocation is unchanged, or the fold on lane 0 only for sides with <= 32 slots. V3: count per block instead of per warp when `split_wide` (4 sub-warps per task) to cut atomics. V4: raise/lower `find_sync_fold_max_tasks` (the 352-task Numerai sides: measure the fold's duration in nsys as the finder's tail growth). V5 (if confirmed, time left): the same fold for the non-used-tasks sync kernel path (`SyncBestSplitForLevelKernel`, several blocks per leaf) by extending the gate, or leaving that path on the kernel.

Shape gate: engages for every quantized level that takes the warp finder and the used-tasks sync, any bin count, column count, bagged or not; the only threshold is the per-side slot count against a plan key (default 1024, 32 per lane), so the fold's serial work is bounded on wide feature sets.

md5 risks seen: (a) every warp of a side must count exactly once at every exit path of the finder (invalid side, padding warp, empty narrow group, unused feature, split-wide sub-warps) or a later level folds early or never; (b) slot reads in the fold must be `__ldcg` after the writers' `__threadfence()`; (c) the mirror pointer and `leaf_mirror_written_` must be set identically whether the kernel or the fold writes; (d) the non-finite replay must be ported exactly (compare on a config that yields inf gains if one exists in the test sweep; otherwise port verbatim with num_warps = 1 and keep the kernel's code as the reference); (e) the counters live per (pair, side) up to 2 x num_leaves_ and are zeroed at Init and re-zeroed by the last warp; (f) the graph-capture path (`FALCATA_HYBRID_GRAPH_SUPPORTED`, ~6500-6538, graph_loop) records the sync's role statics: either disable the fold while capturing or record the fold flag in the captured launch; (g) `FindBestSplitsForLevelVector` passes `gate_on_desc_counts=false`: the fold takes the same value from the host gate.

Verified in the planning session (binds the steps above):
- Counting rule (replaces "count at every exit" in step 2): the finder kernel's early returns at lines ~6269-6316 (warp beyond the grid, padding warp, empty narrow group, invalid side, padding slot, unused feature) become a `bool active` that skips the find body; `WarpFindBest`'s own returns (its split-wide merge: the four sub-warps `__syncthreads` at ~6142, the losing warps return at ~6173 and the WINNING sub-warp `m_sub` (or `group` at ~6170) writes `out`: it is not always sub 0) return to the kernel as now. Then one epilogue every thread reaches: `__threadfence(); __syncthreads();` (sm_70+: exited threads do not block a barrier, but with `active` no thread exits early anyway), then lane 0 of every warp with `warp < nu * num_pairs * 2` does `atomicAdd(&counter[pair_index * 2 + is_larger], 1)`, `__syncwarp`, broadcast; `old == nu - 1` makes this warp the side's folder (units_per_side = nu of the kernel's layout, line ~6265: narrow_pad + num_wide * split_u, counted per warp; in the split-wide layout every block is one wide task or four narrow units, so the writer's store precedes the barrier and every count). Warps beyond the grid never count. One barrier per block per level is the fold's whole hot-path cost.
- Tie-break equivalence: `host_used_task_indices_` is built by an ascending loop over task_index (cuda_best_split_finder.cpp:552-558), so the sync kernel's per-thread first-max over ascending positions followed by `ReduceBestKeyBlock` (lowest read_index among equal keys) yields the global (max key, lowest slot) winner; the warp fold selects by exactly that total order per lane and in its shuffle reduction: identical bits for finite gains, whatever the lane count.
- Non-finite replay (5556-5613): a loop over all `num_tasks` in chunks of NUM_TASKS_PER_SYNC_BLOCK x kReplayWarps(8) x 32 lanes, `ReduceBestGainWarp` per virtual warp into shared buffers, `ReduceBestGainBlock` over the 8 entries by warp 0, blocks merged by strict greater; `for (virtual_warp = warp_id; < kReplayWarps; += num_warps)` with num_warps = 1 is this loop on one warp, so the port is the same code with per-warp shared slices of 8 (double, bool, uint32) in the finder's static shared memory (adds 8 x 13 B x 4 warps = 416 B; the wide instantiation holds 10304 B now, check occupancy is unchanged).
- Graph capture (6496-6538, gstate != nullptr) uses the block finder and `SyncBestSplitForLevelKernel` + `SyncBestSplitForLevelKernelAllBlocks`: the fold's gate (`use_warp`, i.e. gstate == nullptr) never meets it; nothing to change there.
- `FindBestSplitsForLevel` (cpp:750-771) and `FindBestSplitsForLevelVector` (cpp:734-747) each call the finder launcher then `LaunchSyncBestSplitForLevelKernel` with nothing between: the host flag set by the finder launcher and consumed (and cleared) by the sync launcher is safe; the gate must also require that the sync launcher's own conditions would choose the used-tasks kernel (otherwise the multi-block kernel path stays).
- Counter storage: `CUDAVector<int>` of 2 x num_leaves_ (allocated and memset once at Init / BeforeTrain when num_leaves_ is known; the memset is a one-time allocation-time initialisation, not a per-round sync), reset by the folding warp with a plain store after its writes and a `__threadfence()`.
- Register ceiling: the wide finder runs 96 registers x 128 threads = 12288 per block, 5 blocks per SM out of the 64K register file (shared memory 10304 B allows more); the next allocation granule (104) drops it to 4 blocks. hypotheses.hypothesis:
Carrying the packed int32 gradients in leaf order through the partition (ordered gradients: the split-inner and gap
copy kernels move a row's gradient with its index, +8 contiguous bytes per row per level) lets the dense construct
read gradients by position, contiguously: one random sector per row instead of two. Upper bound first, by a probe
(wrong model, measurement only): the construct reading gradients at the row's position instead of its index. If the
probe cuts the higgs construct by >= 20% (755 -> <= 600 us/round), the full mechanism is worth building (net of the
partition's extra ~8 B/row/level, ~20 us/round); if not, the construct is not gather-bound on the gradient and the
hypothesis is refuted.
hypotheses.observation:
higgs-deep-stoch (nsys 60 rounds, parent): CUDAConstructDiscretizedHistogramDenseBatchedKernel 755 us/round (44%),
10 launches, ~75 us each at the deep levels. Per row the kernel gathers two random sectors: the row's 28 bin bytes
(row-major 8-bit) and its packed int32 gradient (cuda_gradients_and_hessians[idx]); at level 9 a leaf holds ~1/512
of the rows, so consecutive rows of a leaf are never in the same sector. ~2M smaller-leaf rows x 2 x 32 B = ~128 MB
of random sectors per level, ~70 us at the observed rate: the construct's deep levels look gather-bound, and half
of the gathered bytes serve a 4-byte gradient. Bagged higgs 0.5: the same kernel 485 us/round (34%).

hypotheses.falsification: Same-binary A/B (`dense_lane_major:off` in --plan-stock), 2 pairs on higgs: ratio < 1.02 refutes (the kernel is not bound by its shared atomic wavefronts); nsys of the dense kernel per level must drop (root < 100 us, deep levels < 55 us) else the mechanism did not engage or does not matter; covtype and the numerai cells must stay within their 1.5% bands.
hypotheses.hypothesis: A bin-major shared table with the warp size as its column stride (slot = bin * 32 + column lane) makes a warp's 32 column atomics hit 32 distinct banks (the few lanes of a straddled second row lane give at most 2-way conflicts), cutting the atomic phase 1.75-3.5x. Expected: higgs dense construct 754 -> ~550-600 us (root toward the 75 us DRAM floor, deep levels toward the gather rate), round -8 to -10% (ratio 1.08-1.11); hidden 255-bin dense cells (year-like, epsilon-like, bagged or not) similar where the gate engages; covtype declines the gate (its lane-major table would be 3.1x its natural 2638 cells: the zero/flush of tiny leaves would grow) -> 1.000; numerai cells 1.000 (not engaged). Integer sums of the same addends: bit-identical.
hypotheses.observation: higgs-deep-stoch: the dense 8-bit batched construct is 42.8% of kernel time (754 us/round; root 121 us, deep levels 59-78 us each). The root reads 128 MB contiguous at 1.06 TB/s (DRAM ~1.7 TB/s); e054's direct read brought it to 108 us and left "the shared atomics" as the rest; e034's sector padding cut the deep levels' bytes 45% and made them slower: neither level is DRAM-bound. Each row costs the block one warp ATOMS per 32 columns with 32 random banks (~3.5 wavefronts expected for 32 balls in 32 bins) plus 3 LDGs. covtype: the same kernel is 15% but its launches are tiny leaves (6.2 us, zero+flush dominated). Numerai cells: the kernel does not run (pair-joint path).
hypotheses.plan:
- `ConstructDiscretizedHistogramDenseInner` (src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu): a block-uniform runtime flag `lane_major` (from a host-computed gate passed as a kernel argument) selects slot = column_hist_offsets[col] + bin (generic) or slot = lane_stride * bin + local column (lane-major), one implementation: `base + bin * stride` with (base, stride) = (offset, 1) or (x, warpSize). Zeroing covers max_bins * stride cells; the flush walks tiles of 4 bins x 8 columns per warp (shared reads 4-way conflicted at most, global atomics in 16-byte runs) and skips cells outside a column's bin range and bins unused this tree (bin_used).
- Gate (host, per partition set, in the batched launch): one column per thread (max columns per partition <= blockDim.x), max bins of any partition's column * warpSize <= the instance's table capacity (SHARED_HIST_SIZE / 2 ints), and the lane-major cell count <= 2x the partition's natural cell count (so the extra zero/flush stays small against the row work).
- cuda_plan key `dense_lane_major` (include/Falcata/falcata_plan.h, default on); docs/performance.md entry.
hypotheses.verdict_text:
1. No defect found in the build: md5 identical on every variant, registers and stack unchanged, the gate engaged (the 4-bit and covtype shapes decline it by design; higgs' partition takes it, verified by the time change).
2. Deciding number: same-binary A/B, `dense_lane_major:off` vs on, 2 pairs each, higgs-deep-stoch: V1 0.894, V2 0.738, V3 0.976 (same-arm spread 0.6-1.1%).
3. Mechanism check: the table layout is conflict-free by construction (slot = bin * 32 + column: bank = column lane) and the flush of V3 issues the same coalesced 128-byte atomics as the generic one, yet no level of the dense construct got faster (root 122 -> 134 us, L9 81 -> 86): the shared atomics' bank conflicts are not what bounds this kernel. What the variants moved instead was the flush's L2 request count, and the time followed it (V2 vs V1 vs V3): the kernel's flush of 7,168 cells per block is a first-order cost.
4. Three variants measured.

hypotheses.hypothesis: One single-pass kernel per level that gathers the bin, decides the direction, computes the chunk's left/right prefix within its split by a decoupled look-back over the preceding chunks' published counts (CUB's single-pass scan / partition scheme: each chunk publishes its aggregate then its inclusive prefix with a status flag; a chunk reads back until it finds an inclusive prefix) and scatters the indices to their final positions, removes the aggregate kernel, the split-inner's second pass (index + ballot re-read) and two launch gaps per level: expected numerai -60..-90 us per round (+2..2.5%), higgs -60..-80 us (+3..4%), bagged shapes the same mechanism (the bagged apply shares the chunk body), covtype unchanged (gated off: its levels have fewer chunks than the GPU holds at once, so the gate below leaves the three-kernel path), hidden cells +1..3% where they are GPU-bound. hypotheses.hypothesis:
Fewer host instructions and bytes on that path shorten the idle directly: (1) the fused-mirror readback copies only
the fields the level flow reads (one cache line per leaf instead of 2.6, no scrub pass; the sync kernel writes a
compact per-leaf record for the host), (2) the budget-binding sort as one std::sort of (gain, leaf) keys (same
order), (3) the per-split host loops trimmed where the instrumentation shows them hot. Expected: the deep levels'
host compute halves: covtype -90..-100 us/round (+2.5%), higgs -8..-10 us (+0.5%), numerai -7 us (+0.2%), hidden deep
cells like covtype; shapes with few leaves unchanged. Bit-identical: host bookkeeping only, the same descriptors
and the same order of splits.
hypotheses.observation:
Per level the GPU idles from the sync kernel's end until the gen-bit kernel starts: numerai 7.2 + 2.5 us x 10 levels
(97 us/round, 2.9%), covtype 7.8 + 2.5 us x 70 (717 us/round under nsys, ~35% of a 4.54 ms traced round; ~20% untraced).
API trace (parent profile, numerai; my covtype profile): the cudaDeviceSynchronize wake is 0.84 us; the host compute
between its return and the first cudaMemcpyAsync grows linearly with the leaf count: numerai levels 1-10: 0.8, 0.6,
0.6, 0.7, 1.0, 1.8, 2.6, 3.7, 4.3, 4.8 us (15 us/round); covtype: 0.6, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.9, 1.6, 2.7, 4.3, 6.3, 9.1 us
(27 us per tree, 190 us/round under nsys = 4.2% of the traced round; the compute is not inflated by nsys, so about
5% of the untraced 3.7 ms). The routines on that path: ReadPrefetchedLeafBestSplits (a 168-byte-per-leaf memcpy of
every leaf's CUDASplitInfo from the mapped pinned staging the sync kernel wrote over PCIe, plus a pointer-scrub pass),
CollectSplittableLeaves (every leaf), ArbitrateLevelBudget (a std::stable_sort of the candidates by gain on a
budget-binding level: every covtype tree's level 10, higgs' level 10), ApplyLevelBatched's per-split loop and
SplitLevelBatched's descriptor build (per split, with a std::sort of the regions and the gap scan). All of it is on
the GPU-critical path (the GPU has nothing to run until the gen-bit is launched).

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Passing the level's apply descriptors to the gen-bit kernel as a __grid_constant__ by-value parameter when they fit the
portable 4 KB parameter block (size classes 8 / 30 descriptors), with block 0 publishing them to the device descriptor
buffer for the later kernels of the level (aggregate, split-inner, struct, gap copy: same stream, after the gen-bit's
completion), removes one H2D op from the host chain of every such level: ~1 us of host time per level, and the level
is host-paced so the gen-bit and everything after it start ~1 us earlier. Levels with <= 30 descriptors: covtype ~6 of
10 per tree -> ~45 levels x 1 us = 45 us of 3.6 ms = +1.2%; higgs ~6 levels x 1 us of 1.71 ms = +0.3%; numerai +0.1-0.2%
(GPU-bound). Bit-identical (same descriptors, same kernels). No compile.
hypotheses.observation:
covtype (multiclass, 70 levels/round) is host-paced: under nsys each level is ~42 us and every kernel starts ~1.5 us after
its host launch returns. The gen-bit (first kernel of the level apply) is preceded on its stream by a pageable H2D of the
level's apply descriptors (num_splits + num_gaps x 128 B): sync end -> gen-bit start ~7.8 us (nsys), of which the copy's
API call is ~1.9 us (nsys) / 1.2 us (microbench, no nsys). A by-value kernel parameter of 4 KB adds only 0.22 us to a
launch (1.54 vs 1.32 us). Numerai/higgs have 10 levels per round, so the same per-level cost is a smaller share.

  instantiation HybridGenBitVectorFlatRowsInlineKernel<ROWS, CAP> reading the descriptors from its __grid_constant__
  parameter, block 0 storing them to cuda_apply_descs_. Launch helper picks the smallest class that fits.
- src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_data_partition.cpp: skip the H2D when the plan key is on, the level has no categorical
  descriptors, the flat-rows gen-bit is the selected kernel, and num_descs fits the largest class.

without nsys and is not the binding latency; replacing it with a by-value parameter saves at most 0.4 us of chain

runtime by the occupancy API) used only for levels whose grid spills past one wave of the default build but fits one
wave of the capped build removes the second wave: higgs L5 25 -> ~13 us per tree (+0.7%), Numerai 1-2 levels per tree
(+0.2%), covtype levels below one wave keep the default build (0). Bit-identical (same code, register allocation only).

against 12 us for the 448-block level before it: a small second wave. Narrow tier (Numerai) 94 registers; its levels at
833-968 blocks also straddle one wave.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Replacing the prune's two IEEE divisions by __fdividef (MUFU.RCP + FMUL, <= 2 ulp, i.e. <= 2.4e-7 relative, far inside kRel) where every denominator is provably below 2^124 (a task-uniform check on the hessian scale and lambda_l2; otherwise the IEEE path) removes ~6 instructions and a divergent slow-path branch per division, i.e. ~12 per scan position of the wide tier (8 positions per lane at 255 bins) and the narrow tier. Prune decisions stay sure (the bound only needs to contain the exact gain; the extra 2 ulp is covered by kRel), so the same candidates survive or the exact fp64 gain loop decides: bit-identical. Expected: finder -5..-10% on wide-bin shapes; covtype +0.5..1.5%, higgs +0.5..1%, numerai cells ~0 (5-6 bin tasks have 1-2 candidates), hidden wide-bin cells +0.5..2%. No compile.

On covtype the host waits (cudaDeviceSynchronize, ~13 us) for construct -> fix -> find -> sync each level, so finder time is on the critical path. Its fp32 prune computes per scan position a = gl^2/(hl+l2) + gr^2/(hr+l2) with two IEEE-exact fp32 divisions (SASS: 272 FCHK sequences: MUFU.RCP, Newton FFMAs, FCHK, branch to a slow path); the bound is then widened by kRel = 2e-4 relative, ~1000x larger than the division's rounding.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Skipping the map's zero store at the tree start when the tree's flow rewrites the whole map before its readers (and, for a tree that
ends without a batched apply, writing leaf 0's window through the existing materialize pass instead) halves the index fill's bytes:
numerai -12 us/round (+0.35%), higgs -6 us (+0.35%), covtype -5 us (+0.15%), bagged shapes the whole scatter launch (+0.3-0.6%).

hypotheses.observation:
Numerai (parent profile, steady tree): the tree start's FillDataIndicesBeforeTrainKernel takes 27.2 us per round (0.8% of 3.38 ms),
writing data_indices[i] = i and data_index_to_leaf_index[i] = 0 (8 B/row, 44 MB: at the DRAM floor); higgs 12.5 us (0.7% of 1.75 ms);
covtype ~2 us x 7 trees. With bagging the map zero is a separate scatter launch (FillDataIndexToLeafIndexKernel) over the bag rows.
Under the batched level apply (every visible cell's flow) the map is never read during the tree: the final level's split-inner writes the
split leaves' rows and MaterializeHybridLeafMapSubset the residual leaves' rows before any tree-end reader (score update, refit, linear).
So the zero store is dead whenever batched_apply_ran. Everything larger on these profiles has a measured negative (see Prior attempts).

The whole device tree's lean tree end (skip_host_cache -> inline_all_map -> final_map_only + active slab readback) is gated to
`objective == regression && is_constant_hessian` only. Nothing in that path depends on the objective: the host leaf cache it
skips is consumed only by host searches/tails (CHECKed stale) and by the host RenewTreeOutput, which never runs for
CUDA-boosted non-renewing objectives. Extending the gate to every unweighted, unbagged, CUDA-boosted objective that does not
renew tree outputs (binary, multiclass(ova), cross-entropy, poisson/gamma/tweedie, huber/fair, L2) removes per tree the
73 KB split-batch readback, the host bookkeeping and the post-tree leaf-map pass: covtype +3-5%, higgs +1-2%, numerai 0,
hidden binary/multiclass depth-bounded unbagged shapes +1-5%, bagged shapes unchanged. Bit-identical (same kernels compute the
same map / leaf values).

block once the kernel is light) on the other objectives whose gradient kernels are FP64-bound: Poisson (178 us, 11.6%
of a 4M-row round) -> ~60 us, Fair (125 us, 8.9%) -> ~60 us: +5-10% on such cells, bagged or not; L2 / Huber (memory
floor) and the visible cells unchanged.

nodes.archive_hypothesis_text: Running the tiled 4-bit compact fill (and the fused root-histogram fill) over slot chunks of at most 256 instead of the per-cell gather past 256 byte slots makes wide feature-sampled 4-bit shapes 1.5-2x faster with no change elsewhere.

hypotheses.hypothesis:
Chunking the plain tiled fill over slot groups of <= kFill4BitTiledMaxSlots (a second grid dimension; runs wider than
a chunk are split into pieces stored row-segment by row-segment) serves every width with the tiled kernel's coalesced
column-run loads: the wide fill drops from ~15 ms to ~2-3 ms per tree, i.e. 1.5-2x on wide feature-sampled 4-bit
shapes, no change at <= 256 slots (the same launch, chunk table null) and on 8-bit data. Bit-identical (the same bytes
are written; no arithmetic).
hypotheses.observation:
All visible cells' 4-bit compact fills have <= 256 byte slots (numerai ff 0.1: 176) and take the tiled / fused fill
(1.15 ms/round on numerai). Above 256 byte slots (more than 512 sampled 4-bit columns: wide data at moderate
feature_fraction) CompactFill4BitTiledEligible refuses and the per-cell gather CUDAFillCompactData4BitKernel runs:
open5/e080 measured it at 15.5 ms of a 23-28 ms round on Numarai-width data at ff 0.3 (vs ~1.2 ms for the tiled fused
fill at ff 0.1, i.e. ~4.5x the bytes in ~13x the time).
hypotheses.plan:
cuda_histogram_constructor.{cu,cpp,hpp}, _kernels.cuh: the tiled kernel takes an optional chunk table (lo, n per
blockIdx.y); the host builds it from the byte-slot runs where n > 256; eligibility admits n > 256 when the new key
`tiled_fill_chunks` (default on) holds; the fused root-hist fill stays at <= 256 slots. Key in falcata_plan.h, docs.
hypotheses.verdict_text: Wide feature-sampled 4-bit shapes (> 256 byte slots) train 1.24-2.6x faster (final key off vs on 2 pairs: 1.49-2.31x; md5 identical); the mechanism moved as predicted (per-cell gather 2.87 ms/tree -> chunked fused fill 0.70 ms/tree including the root histogram). The visible cells are not engaged (quick check 1.0261 vs master, the parent's level).
